- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, during this minute and a half, i should like to begin by congratulating our colleague mr schroedter. i think that many have already done so, but she deserves it because she has been particularly open and attentive to everyone's proposals, and i think that her availability has given her report the quality we see today. i would like to add my voice to the regret she expressed that parliament has in some way taken the lead on these guidelines, since the negotiation procedure with the states is now so far advanced that it cannot be expected that this report will have an immediate impact, which i regret. it therefore seems to me that it should anticipate and set the guidelines for the mid-term review in 2003, and even influence the second programming phase which will follow 2003. in short, i would like to say that we are entering a period of programming management for 2000-06, which should not be a routine period, for the simple reason that we have two major challenges to face. the first is the harmonization of national spatial planning policies and regional development policies. subsidies are not enough to make development happen, when infrastructure or public services are lacking. this is a fundamental question we must ask ourselves: how can we ensure that the union's policy is in line with subsidiary national spatial planning policies? - mr president, the priority given to financial and monetary criteria is reinforcing the rise in inequalities of all kinds. for example, french planning experts believe that the most likely scenario today is a deepening of regional differentiation within each country. the structural funds have helped to slow down this process. our project of a europe geared to the satisfaction of social needs aims at a convergence of living conditions from above. its implementation would certainly involve an extension of redistributive instruments such as the structural funds. we are proposing in particular a unified tax on capital, which would make it possible to provide funds to support the harmonization of social protection systems and the reduction of working time at european level. the commission, which is required to present guidelines, does so only with regret and in a vague manner. the report proposed today gives political matters a new lease of life. it is one of the steps towards a policy of employment and sustainable development. this is what will lead us to vote for it.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this sixth periodic report on the situation and socioeconomic development of the regions of the european union marks the crossing of a new threshold in the analysis of regional data and highlights the progress made in this field since the publication of the fifth periodic report. however, i think that the talk of a real convergence of average levels of regional development in europe offers a somewhat truncated reality of the situation and, unfortunately, this is often the message that is repeated in the press and in some speeches. the commission's report largely relativizes this observation, particularly when it refers to the socioeconomic situation of certain regions of the union which are particularly close to my heart: i am referring to the french overseas departments and, more generally, to the outermost regions. in this respect, i am pleased that the committee on regional policy has adopted one of my amendments calling on the commission to reserve a special chapter in its next report on cohesion for the specific case of the outermost regions and, more specifically, for the impact analysis of the measures to be adopted shortly under the new article 299 (2) of the treaty of amsterdam. finally, it seems to me that the sixth periodic report offers interesting arguments for a genuine project of sustainable and balanced development of the european territory, particularly when it summarises the importance of the relationship between the centre of europe and its periphery. even if the commission still hesitates to express it too explicitly, its periodic report shows us the urgency of promoting a polycentric development of the community area, through the union's structural policies and within the framework of the approach initiated by the esc.
- (fi) mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i thank the rapporteur for dealing with this extremely important subject, because it is the way in which the social and economic situation develops that determines the way in which the european citizens judge the success of our action. this issue, which has repercussions on their daily lives, is of key importance for the credibility of the european union. it must be admitted that the european union has already supported, i would say in a remarkable way, the development of the poor countries. i remember what portugal and greece looked like when i first ran there 25 years ago. in this respect, to use a very french expression, we can say frankly "chapeau!" to the european union. the european union deserves a hat-trick, but within countries the disparities between rich and poor regions remain too great. what is the consequence of this? people reacted by 'voting with their feet', leaving their area in the hope of finding better incomes. we are thus forced to build schools, hospitals, in short to rebuild the entire infrastructure, for the same people, in the same country, several times over. this is very costly and also causes extremely serious social problems. yet, most people would like to stay in their hometown if given the opportunity - in other words, if there is work available. we must give them the opportunity. this is the moral duty of the european union and the duty of all of us. as a solution, i think we should strongly encourage entrepreneurship. by 'entrepreneurship' i do not mean just the ownership of a business, but a state of mind. i mean an attitude, the fact that human beings want to move forward in life, whether they are workers, business owners or civil servants. what is a just society? it is a society in which a person of humble origin can get ahead in life, so that his children have a little easier life. this is also how positive development of the regions is possible, because i am sure that people make efforts and work if they are given the opportunity. in conclusion, i would say that we should take a cue from america, where hard work is still in fashion and success is a mark of competence and not a source of envy, as is often the case in europe.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as the seconds are running out, i shall now come to the main points. first, the fruits of growth are not shared equally within the union. an example of this is the outermost regions, which are still hit hard by dramatic unemployment rates. the rate is 37% in réunion, for example. but this is not a cyclical situation, it is structural. it is our remoteness, our insularity, in short, our own personality that creates it. to deal with this, article 299 (2) of the treaty of amsterdam provided for the principle of special and derogating treatment. it is a matter of putting this principle into practice. the commission document announced for december 1999 was postponed to january and then to february and the initial reflections do not give much cause for optimism. i therefore make a solemn appeal to the council and the commission. with regard to taxation, state aid, the structural funds and the defence of our traditional products, it is urgent to devise concrete measures that are both bold and ambitious. otherwise, convergence and cohesion will unfortunately remain mere words for us and there is a fear that the structural policy pursued in our regions, despite the large sums committed, will end in failure.
- mr president, commissioner, we have to answer two simple questions. are state aid to undertakings or agreements between undertakings legitimate in a market economy and who should control these exceptions to the absolute rules of the market economy? on the first point, we are very clear that, in order to take account of the requirements of sustainable development to which the european union has subscribed, it is essential that, in certain cases, there be state aid to enterprises, whether in the form of tax exemptions, differentiated taxation or outright direct aid. it is also legitimate that there may be agreements between undertakings, agreements of self-limitation, all of which make it possible to reduce the harmful effects of competition on social or ecological requirements. so we answer very clearly, yes, it is legitimate that there should be aid, that there should be agreements, but we say that each of these agreements must be explicitly subject to an argument. the von wogau report proposes that the control of this legitimacy should be transferred to the national level. we think it is a relatively dangerous proposal, but we will vote for it anyway because we recognize that the commission cannot do everything. we ask for the greatest possible transparency and for the commission to be given greater powers of investigation to verify the legitimacy of these exceptions ex post facto.
- mr president, commissioner, during this pivotal year, before the changeover to the single currency, the commission has made every effort to ensure that the euro can be born in a favourable environment. competition policy has, in the context of these means, contributed to this development. we, for our part, remain firmly opposed to the single currency, which, far from bringing us the advantages and flexibility of a common currency, confines us to an artificial shackle imposed on the peoples of europe. that said, governance is planning, it is also being responsible, and in this new, imposed context, competition law naturally has a vital role to play. the commission has focused its action on several areas: on the structure of the markets by actively pursuing anticompetitive practices, by refocusing the control activities of its departments on cases of clear community interest and by demonstrating its desire to modernise competition law. as far as state aid is concerned, care must be taken not to burden the system and the introduction of a public register in which all aid is recorded does not seem desirable to us, since this burdensome obligation would naturally run counter to attempts to alleviate bureaucratic constraints. finally, as regards the modernisation of the application of articles 85 and 86 of the treaty, we do not think that decentralised application is necessarily the right way forward. the commission not only retains the power to remove a case from the jurisdiction of the national authorities, but it also clearly obliges the national courts to avoid any conflict with the commission's decisions. the national states would thus become the secular arm of the commission for the enforcement of rules over which they have no control. in conclusion, i would say that if certain measures are taken in the right direction, we will naturally remain vigilant to avoid a federalist approach which would be to the detriment of europe and the sovereignty of the states.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in this important debate on competition, i am speaking this morning in particular about mr langen's text on the steel aid code. as the court of justice recognised in 1996, the steel sector is particularly sensitive to distortions of competition. i had reached this conclusion a few years ago in a report i had written on the strengths and weaknesses of the european steel industry. it was therefore legitimate to set up a system of aid to this sector to ensure the survival of successful firms, even if this was contrary to article 4 of the ecsc treaty. this is indeed the purpose of the sixth steel aid code, but at the same time it is important to avoid any distortion of competition and any serious disturbance of the markets, which is why it is important to regulate such aid. it is therefore necessary to continue to limit state aid to aid for research and development, environmental protection and closures of firms. in the same vein, it is essential that member states fulfil their obligation to report to the commission on aid granted to their steel undertakings. the commission suggests shorter time limits. i approve this request. like the rapporteur, i welcome the commission's report, but i regret that it does not cover all aspects of aid. although the steel aid code is very clearly worded, the commission has authorised aid to steel undertakings which do not fall within the categories covered by the code. in the interests of equality, the code must be applied or amended. finally, mr president, with the expiry of the ecsc treaty, the rules will have to be revised, because i believe that the aid system will have to continue beyond 2002 and i am therefore in favour of a council regulation which will guarantee security in this area. we are therefore awaiting, and i am awaiting, proposals from the european commission in this respect.
- the commission report confirms that, with the exception of germany, state aid to enterprises is increasing. the commission is concerned only with the conditions of competition. we, on the other hand, take the view that the interests of the working classes are at stake. society gains nothing from these huge transfers of public funds to private companies. look at the automobile sector, where subsidies and miscellaneous state aid increased by 24% over the reference period. what do you want to do with it ? it's not about keeping jobs. all these companies have cut jobs or even laid off workers. it is not to improve working conditions, for by producing more with fewer workers, working conditions are made worse. did these companies need state aid to survive? no, the automobile companies have been making huge profits for years. state aid is not only perverse because, as the jonckheer report acknowledges, it leads to a hunt for subsidies by relocating from one country to another, it is unacceptable because it spends public money on the enrichment of a handful of private shareholders. it is because the richest are being favoured with state money that social protection is being reduced, public services are being abandoned and hospitals are being closed across europe. the point of my vote against the jonckheer report is to affirm the need for another policy, namely the cessation of all aid to private enterprises and the use of the money thus saved to develop public services and to hire staff.
- mr president, mrs theato's report on the protection of the european union's financial interests proposes, in particular, as a first step, the centralisation of criminal prosecutions by the creation of a european public prosecutor. this proposal is deeply opposed to the spirit of the present system, in which criminal law and criminal procedure, which are at the heart of national legal systems, must be the sovereignty of each people and the exclusive jurisdiction of each state. the idea of a european public prosecutor is, on the contrary, to limit the states to a subordinate role in these matters. moreover, this proposal would trigger a chain of reforms that is absolutely unpredictable. the european parliament has also called for the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office to be set up in order to ensure that the european union's anti-fraud office, olaf, is able to carry out its investigations. but at the same time, we learn from the van hulten report that is being discussed today that the european public prosecutor should himself be supervised by a court of the european union. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. the big one may also be hiding a giant one, since we shall soon see a european criminal law proposed and why not a european justice minister, controlled by an extension of the powers of the european parliament. i think we must therefore think carefully about the balance of power that we risk upsetting by introducing this kind of seemingly one-off reform. finally, it seems to us that proposals such as that of the european public prosecutor show the inability to imagine europe as anything other than a pyramidal and centralised structure, organised around a superstate. the europe of nations group, on the other hand, wants a polycentric europe that links nations in a network. the network could, for example, lead to better coordination between national prosecutor's offices, with the possible creation of national training courses specialising in criminal offences at the expense of community finances. the legal framework, mr president, therefore already exists. he's good in his principles. it just needs to be perfected.
- mr president, mrs theato is proposing an institutional revolution for two reasons. public opinion, indifferent to 20 million unemployed and thousands of mad cows, would be worried about fraud which would endanger the interests of finance and these two reasons would justify a double system: a european criminal code with anti-community offences and a european public prosecutor. mrs theato has probably forgotten that there is a european prison, since the fbi, the european police, exists alongside olaf. the whole thing would be established by two regulations, one for the public prosecutor, one for the criminal code, regulations based on article 280 of the treaty, that is to say, on secondary law, since the nature of secondary law is to allow all deviations. indeed, there is a double drift. first, the classic ideological drift, euro-federalist, a single market, a single vat, a single diplomacy, a single army, and now a single criminal law and a single public prosecutor. all this to combat fraud of less than a billion euros, while tens of billions of euros are being allowed to slip through the cracks because of the gsps, the free trade zones, the customs gifts to chiquita and the billions lost on the fourth resource, gdp, as a result of the budgetary rationing pact. then comes the puritan drift: northern german europe, lutheran, calvinist, quaker europe, wants to impose its moral order on us. the more you loosen up on manners, the tighter you tighten up on your wallet.

in writing. - the european union apparently finances itself with four own resources. in fact, the european budget is fed by vat and the levy on gdp, especially since the abandonment of community preference and the multiplication of free trade areas have caused the customs duties and the common agricultural levy, already amputated by the gsp, to collapse. the commission has also proposed that the community should be able to take part in the negotiations on the fourth resource, which is the community's own resources. the european union is a federalist state, and it is therefore more than ever financed by the commonplace intergovernmental organisation that it is, but refuses to be. this is clear from the regulations before us. the main tasks of the commission are to 'account for own resources' and to 'make them available' or to 'control' the amounts of established entitlements made available to the commission. the newly created advisory committee is composed of representatives of the member states which are taxpayers. the debate on 'community criminal law', the 'community prosecutor general' or the community police, with olaf, is far from over. there is no european federal tax here yet. but it is true that the europe of 25 will want a european income tax, unless it is on profits, or co2 taxation finances this budget 2025.
in writing. - i welcome the report on better harmonization in the training of safety advisers for the transport of dangerous goods. in recent years, the transport of dangerous goods, both domestically and internationally, has increased considerably, which has increased the risk of accidents. some of these were due to insufficient knowledge of the risks inherent in such transport. it has therefore become necessary, in the context of the completion of the internal market, to adopt measures to ensure better risk prevention. directive 96/35/ec has met this requirement. undertakings transporting dangerous goods and undertakings carrying out loading or unloading operations in connection with such transport have been rightly required to comply with rules on risk prevention, whether transport is by road, rail or inland waterway. to facilitate the achievement of this objective, directive 96/35/ec provided for the appointment of safety advisers for the transport of dangerous goods with appropriate professional training. the purpose of the training of the advisers was to provide them with knowledge of the essential legislative, regulatory and administrative provisions applicable to such transport. while this was a step forward at the time, the lack of specific provisions on harmonising the examination conditions proved problematic. it therefore appeared necessary to close this gap in order to achieve a high and uniform level of training of safety advisers, but also to avoid a disparity in training costs and, consequently, an impact on competition between undertakings in the member states. the commission proposal aims to ensure uniform training of security advisers. it defines the minimum content of examinations and the tasks of the competent authority and the requirements to be met by the examination bodies. our parliament has voted in favour of this text. however, it submitted several amendments, most of which were accepted in the council's common position, in particular as regards the need to draw up a questionnaire and statements concerning the authorisation of certain documents in the context of 'the specifications of the examination procedures proposed by the examination body'. i also support the postponement of the date of application of these provisions to three months after the entry into force of the directive for reasons of realism. i would like to conclude by stressing that harmonization of the professional qualifications of these advisers will help to improve the quality of service in the interests of users, to minimise the risks of accidents which may lead to environmental degradation and to serious damage which may affect the physical integrity of any person who may come into contact with dangerous goods.
in writing. - i spoke last october on the hatzidakis report on the transport of dangerous goods by rail. the words i am going to say today are not far removed from those i said then. they sum up their position as follows: i regret that in a crucial area such as the transport of dangerous goods we have always put off adopting harmonized standards to the detriment of human safety and the environment. i would remind you that a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the transport of dangerous goods by road entered into force on 1 january 1997. the commission has also decided to initiate proceedings under article 93 (2) of the treaty in respect of a number of aid measures granted to the steel industry in the united kingdom. it is from that date that we should have taken a decision on a proposal from the european commission to end these derogations. the european committee for standardisation (cen) proposes standards in this field, which are then incorporated into the european agreement concerning the international carriage of dangerous goods by road, signed in geneva in 1957 (better known as the adr), which applies throughout europe and whose provisions form the basis for the legislation applicable in the eu. cen was not able to complete its work within the time allotted. the commission proposal we are discussing today is therefore aimed at amending the directive to solve these problems in the short term and not at ending the transitional arrangements as it should have been! this is exactly what happened with the transport of these goods by rail, with this difference: a delay had been set. at present, we have no idea when cen will be able to make any concrete proposals. until then, there is no need for member states to amend their national regulations. the report also accepts that some flexibility should be introduced and acknowledges the possibility for states to adopt or apply different standards. the latter will thus be able to continue to apply their own standards for certain transportable pressure equipment for which european standards are lacking. they may also adopt different provisions for local and ad hoc transport. i therefore wanted to express my deep dissatisfaction and concern by this explanation of vote.

in writing. - the berend report provides an interesting analysis of the economic situation and development of the regions of the european union. however, the french delegation to the union for europe of nations group cannot but disagree with some of the statements contained in it. thus, paragraph 26 'stresses the need for budgetary consolidation as a condition for the success of economic and wealth, employment and activities in certain areas: hamburg, brussels, antwerp, luxembourg, île-de-france, darmstadt, oberbayern, bremen, vienna, karlsruhe and emilia-romagna. contrary to what the rapporteur claims, the establishment of economic and monetary union should exacerbate the desertification of the most remote, rural and less populated regions in favour of the union's central axis (benelux, north-west germany, northern italy, ile-de-france, etc.). the poorer regions are gradually catching up. the average of the 10 poorest regions was 41% of community gnp in 1986. it was 50% in 1996. the increase was particularly marked in portugal and ireland. in reality, while the rich are getting richer and the very poor poorer, it appears that the average regions, those covered by objective 2, are experiencing a sometimes considerable decline in their gdp and a worsening of the employment situation. this is particularly clear in france: the champagne-ardennes region, which i have the honour of representing, saw its gdp rise from 105 to 94% of the community average, that of the pays de loire fell from 95 to 91%, that of auvergne from 89 to 83%. the trend is general, not sparing the rhône-alpes or alsace. this is confirmed in sweden, finland, where unemployment has also risen at alarming rates in recent years, and in several parts of the united kingdom. it may therefore seem strange that objective 2, which is devoted to industrial and rural regions undergoing economic restructuring, was sacrificed, during the reform of the structural funds, in favour of objectives 1 and 3: its budget for the period 1999-2006 will be ecu 22.5 billion, a figure roughly similar to that for the period 1994-1999. the rural regions eligible under objective 5b will be among the main victims of this situation: in france, 27% of the population eligible for structural funds will lose their eligibility at the end of the transition period, a figure sometimes much higher in certain regions such as the pays de la loire, alsace or lower normandy, electoral strongholds of the right, victims of the political clientelism of the government of the left. it is doubtful that regional policy, based on such choices, can contribute to the harmonious development of the territories of the member states of the european union.
in writing. - in view of the employment situation in the community and the european union's stated ambition to tackle unemployment decisively, the commission's analysis of mergers should take account of factors other than competition. i would like to take the example of the restructuring of the company abb-alsthom power, whose employees are represented in strasbourg by a large delegation from all over europe. the management of abb-alsthom power, which is the result of a merger completed in june 1999, has announced a restructuring with already prospects of job cuts in a number of countries. this negative situation for employment raises many questions, particularly about the information given to the european works council, which has existed since 1996. this implies updating and strengthening the community directive on european works councils. this also implies a control of concentrations which takes employment, the environment and consumers into account. the report of the committee on economic and monetary affairs is not adequate in this respect, and i therefore abstained.
in writing. - the commission's white paper on the modernisation of the rules for the application of articles 85 and 86 of the ec treaty (new articles 81 and 82) certainly does not propose to 'renationalise' competition policy, as some in the european parliament fear. but in any case it suggests some rather interesting possibilities for the european union. noting that its services are overburdened by prior notifications of agreements between undertakings liable to distort trade, and fearing that this number will increase further with the entry of new member states, the commission proposes to abolish the system of prior authorisation of such agreements and to apply the competition rules more decentrally at member state level. the most remarkable, in my view, is the signal that this proposal sends us: the commission anticipates the consequences of enlargement and understands that it necessarily implies, almost mechanically, a reform of the centralised system. the reform here is, of course, about relaxation, not dismantling. it is provided on paper that the commission will retain central control and steering of the new system. the von wogau report, which the european parliament has just voted on, encourages it to do so. but at the same time it is clear that the disruption introduced by enlargement can lead to a limitation of community powers and an extension of subsidiarity. this is another europe that can emerge in the long term. is this not what some socialists in the european parliament are worried about? the german social democrats voted against the von wogau report because they believe it could fragment european competition policy, in other words, in other words, it could undermine the super-state of uniformity. strangely enough, some of the employers have joined them, preferring the european "single window" system, which they consider to be more economical and legally stable. this is indeed an advantage of the present system. but on the other hand, it is also necessary to consider, more broadly, that the beginning of decentralisation initiated today can lead in the long run to greater freedom to take account of the needs of each country, from which everyone will benefit.
in writing. - the workers' representatives will not vote in favour of these reports on european competition policy. competition, that is to say the war between large companies, is constantly being expressed in redundancies, in factory closures, not to mention the huge waste in the use of production capacity. we have another example with the job-cutting plan in europe of the abb alsthom power trust. 18 million unemployed, 50 million poor in the european union, one of the richest regions in the world: this is the result of the competition that the european institutions intend to encourage. the commission's desire to regulate the conditions of competition in the european market is ridiculous, because the only law that competition obeys is the law of the jungle where the powerful crush or devour the weak. it's mostly socially repulsive. the european commission's report shows clearly that the institutions of the union are only interested in the big capitalist groups that are engaged in this economic war and not at all in the victims of it. nothing to prevent the spread of unemployment, nothing to protect the workers, nothing to prevent large companies from pushing a fraction of the population into poverty, simply to enrich their shareholders even more! so if we do acknowledge a merit in this report, it is that it shows that the working majority of society has nothing to look to the european institutions to preserve, let alone improve, their living conditions.

in writing. - i welcome the quality of the seventh report on state aid in the eu, the fact that it is now published annually and the fact that the directorate-general for competition publishes general commission - (es) mr president, i should like first of all to thank this parliament for giving me the opportunity to speak about the disaster that occurred on the french coast following the sinking of the oil tanker erika on 12 december 1999, which polluted more than 400 kilometres of coastline, caused the death of thousands of birds and had other extremely negative effects on the environment and on the maintenance of our seas and coasts in a state of safety and compliance with minimum values, which we must demand in a developed society like ours. the sinking of the erika is, in a way, the antithesis of what we are all fighting for: sustainable development, development that respects the environment. this is a very clear case of a violation of this vision of development and progress, a flagrant case of what not to do. i could dwell on the concrete facts that made this catastrophe possible. i won't, because we all know them. i will confine myself to saying that the commission shares the indignation of not only the people living on the french coast who were affected by this disaster, but also of all europeans - and not just europeans - in the face of such an event. the commission has expressed its solidarity and its willingness to contribute, by all the means at its disposal, to combating the tragic consequences of this event. but i think that's not enough. we must find solutions and proposals to prevent similar events from happening again. so, on the environmental front, i would like to point out that in collaboration with the french authorities and at their request, commissioner wallström, who is responsible for the environment, set up an environmental crisis unit immediately after the shipwreck. this unit set up the community working group on marine pollution and offered the french authorities the services of the best european experts in pollution control. the commission also took part in the deployment of pollution control instruments at the disaster site and coordinated the action of 11 eu member states, which sent more than 26 kilometres of floating barriers to the site. we believe that the coordination and the results achieved show some progress and are a success in the sense that there is genuine european solidarity. this is partly the result of the work done by the commission over the past few years. this work has led to the creation of a community system which compiles all the information on the means of combating this type of pollution in the community, the setting up of the community working group and the co-financing of the project for training and improving pollution control techniques in the european union. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the commission therefore welcomes the positive response given by the european parliament at first reading to its draft decision on the establishment of a legal framework for improving cooperation in the fight against accidental pollution. the commission hopes that recent events will help to speed up the final approval of this text by parliament and the council and thus to unblock the current situation. but as far as transport is concerned, i would like to stress that the sinking of the erika raises again the problem of preventing maritime accidents and, more specifically, the problem of the safe transport of polluting products. in this case, the marine environment. in this area, i think it is essential to begin by stressing that the european union has not been inactive since the famous sinking of the amoco cadiz in 1978, also off the french coast. but perhaps we should ask ourselves whether more should not be done and, therefore, whether we should not do more. in the last six years, some 15 community regulations and directives have been adopted. this legislation is still recent. the member states now have a legal basis to combat flags of convenience and all those who do not comply with their security obligations. it is up to the member states to demonstrate that they have the political will to equip their maritime administrations with the resources necessary to carry out their tasks of monitoring and enforcing community standards and to apply and enforce, where appropriate, compliance with community standards already approved. it goes without saying that the commission must ensure that these standards are applied in a uniform manner in all member states. as regards the sinking of the erika, the results of the preliminary investigation by the french authorities into the causes of the accident have already been communicated to the commission. the report shows how lightly - the word is weak - the checks were carried out. i would point out that the commission, for its part, contacted the italian authorities responsible for inspections in ports and the classification society rina, which is responsible for the latest classifications of the erika, as early as 21 december 1999 in order to obtain explanations on the checks carried out on the tanker. the commission must verify whether the relevant community directives have been correctly applied in this case, both by the italian authorities as a port state and by rina as a classification society. this is a vital step if we are to improve our directives and our action in the future. in any event, i would like to inform parliament that a special commission mission will be visiting rina on the 28th of this month to carry out an inspection and that, depending on the findings of this mission, the commission will take the necessary measures. when i say that it will 'take the necessary measures', i do not exclude the possibility of deleting rina from the list of companies approved by the commission. ladies and gentlemen, the commission has also made a similar request to the maritime authorities of malta - the erika was flying the maltese flag - which, i should like to stress, have so far offered us their full cooperation. nevertheless, and without prejudice to the results of all these investigations - how the shipwreck occurred, what the final reasons are and what is the responsibility of rina and the italian port authorities in the inspections carried out - the erika accident raises a series of questions which deserve careful consideration and which, in my view, require us to act urgently. ladies and gentlemen, the commission was preparing a communication on maritime safety and port security. but these events are undoubtedly forcing us to speed up the presentation of this communication and to concentrate mainly on the transport of dangerous, polluting products, in particular oil, gas or chemicals. this document will be accompanied by a series of legislative proposals to strengthen maritime safety in community waters. the commission plans to adopt them before june this year so that the debates on the proposed measures can begin both in this house and in the council, starting in the second half of 2000, under the french presidency. as regards the content of this communication, we propose to deal mainly with the following points: first, the strengthening of controls on vessels at risk, regardless of their flag - although some statistical data speak for themselves: as regards inspections carried out in ports, it was found that 5.9 out of 100 vessels flying the flag of one of the 15 member states of the european union had irregularities. the world average is about 15.6 irregularities for inspections carried out in european ports. in the case of ships flying the maltese flag - such as the erika - the figure is 19.7 and it is much higher for other flags. in order to strengthen controls, we will amend the existing directives on classification societies, on the inspection of ships in ports and on the frequency of inspections according to the age and flag of the ship. we all know that a car must be subjected to an annual technical inspection after the first four years. unfortunately, the same cannot be said of boats. we want to encourage and make these procedures - which have been incorporated into the latest international agreements concluded within the imo (international maritime organisation) via the solas (international convention for the safety of life at sea) and marpol (international convention for the prevention of pollution from ships) agreements - mandatory. secondly, the use of environmentally friendly tankers in the use of european ports should be encouraged. in other words, the tankers that call at our ports must be double-hulled, not single-hulled, which are more likely to cause pollution in the event of an accident. the latter should be subject to measures to accelerate their gradual abandonment, as is happening in the united states. this would avoid the risk, which we are running at the moment, of oil tankers which are not allowed to dock in american ports being diverted to european ports. thirdly, ladies and gentlemen, the communication will deal with the complex and thorny question of liability and compensation for damage suffered in the event of pollution caused by a disaster. the commission intends to get out of the present legal impasse and to put forward proposals to raise the maximum limits of liability of the parties involved and, moreover, to introduce new persons in the chain of responsibility which, today, falls almost entirely on the shipowners, on the owners of vessels. more specifically, we intend to introduce a system for defining and requiring the liability of the owner or carrier of the cargo - indeed, what is called complacent shipowners is called charterers who are not concerned about the quality of the vessels they charter - and to increase the amount of insurance taken out by shipowners in relation to the total amount of insurance per vessel. finally, the commission intends to continue its efforts to improve transparency as regards the quality of vessels operating in european waters. the commission is also proposing to speed up the introduction of the equasix system - starting in may this year - which is nothing more or less than a real-time information system on the status of the international fleet of all vessels. this programme is being developed in agreement with the french authorities and will provide complete real-time information on the situation of the various vessels and also on the training of the crews, which is also an important element. ladies and gentlemen - and this is my conclusion - we are here not only to talk about the erika disaster and the actions taken so far, but also to draw conclusions to prevent such disasters from happening again. we must ensure that the standards for maritime safety are effectively applied. the international maritime organisation has no power - we all know that - to control or make mandatory the standards approved by certain states, which often forget the commitments they have made or turn a blind eye - to say nothing else - to what they have signed up to in these conventions. secondly, we must strive to achieve a more competitive european shipping industry, a capable and extremely safe industry, maintaining the current level of demand, but we must also be able to fight, as regards flags of convenience, against the abuses committed under these flags. finally, ladies and gentlemen, we must combat the irresponsibility of certain shipowners, of certain shipping companies, of certain states, of certain companies, of certain shipping operators, who are a threat to our environment and who can cause disasters such as the one that has unfortunately struck the french coast in recent days.
- mr president, i will speak on behalf of the epp but also as a briton directly concerned and shocked by these events. we have tabled a motion for a resolution with mrs grossetête and the epp. we are here today with a compromise proposal, and i welcome that. the sinking of the erika is indeed a european matter, firstly because it mutilates and defiles some of europe's most beautiful beaches with very serious consequences for tourism, maritime professionals and environmentalists, and secondly because what is at stake is regulation and control, the natural dimension of which is clearly european. such a disaster almost certainly would not have occurred off the coast of the united states. why would you do that ? - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, europe is facing a very difficult test at the beginning of the new millennium. first of all, i would like to express my deep sympathy to the families who lost loved ones in the terrible weather that ravaged europe last december. the storm is an unprecedented ecological disaster for our forests. let me say a few words about the forest in my own region, lorraine, which has been destroyed to a great extent. i commend the local authorities, the volunteers and the public enterprises for their exemplary mobilization, but unfortunately they are not at the end of their sentence. it is europe's duty to support them and thus complement the efforts of the governments of the member states affected by the disaster. i welcome mr barnier's statement and i welcome the measures announced by the commission. i am certainly not forgetting the economic dimension of the matter, the timber sector is devastated and a whole population is suffering the dramatic effects. the community action programme on civil protection, established by the council decision of 9 december 2000, started on 1 january 2000. i ask the member states to seize this opportunity: this programme must be fully operational. if it was effective in some areas - and i have no doubt that commissioner barnier is sincere - i regret that it is still in its infancy in the forestry sector. until funds are released at community level, priority is given to material aid in the framework of partnership exchanges between member states. it is therefore urgent to strengthen the forestry road network and to restore it as quickly as possible. the lending of forestry equipment and the provision of qualified forestry personnel are also part of this scheme. the next challenge will be to avoid the plant health problems associated with the abandonment of large volumes of timber in forests and the pollution of the groundwater due to equally large stockpiles of timber. finally, it is imperative to slow down the exploitation of standing timber in order to give priority to the purchase of wood chips. these timber sales will need to be supported by strong media coverage at member state level. this aid for the mobilisation of wood is, of course, only the first stage of support in the form of aid for the replanting of forests and aid for rural development. i would ask the commission to include it in a reflection on post-emergency management. this is a sad opportunity for europe to renew its forest heritage in view of its role in the conservation of wildlife and the natural environment and in the economy of our countries. so for now, it is time for solidarity and cooperation between member states in the face of an ecological and economic calamity. it is up to europe to propose priority actions to safeguard the wood sector so that this solidarity can take on its full meaning.
- my dear colleagues, we should not both have lost our memories. it is true that there is a joint decision by the commission and parliament to abolish the emergency lines. it is also true that there is a lot of european money - commissioner barnier said that for oyster farming and agriculture, article 30 of the rural development regulation would be used, for forestry, article 33, for enterprises, the exceptions to competition law set out in article 87 (2) of the treaty, for public facilities, the structural funds. the fact remains that not a penny more than what was distributed before the storm will be released today to demonstrate concrete, active solidarity. it is simply a matter of the states acting as communicating vessels and taking from here what they will give elsewhere. it is not enough and i am personally pleased that mr barnier has mentioned here an idea which is dear to me and which i also expressed when i greeted the press in bordeaux, namely the establishment of a strengthened european civil security policy. i believe that our citizens must feel the urgency if we want the european citizenship we so earnestly seek to exist, if we want the mandate that our president, mrs fontaine, has given us to bring the union and the citizens of europe closer together to be effective. so i think that a euro-civil security corps, the constitution of genuine civil protection blue helmets, present in the troubled areas, within the union, since we do not have an emergency procedure today, but also outside if the need arises, in venezuela or elsewhere, would be something that we should wish for and i would like to tell commissioner barnier that he will find in me an active ally of this idea which i believe is generous and european.

counsel. - (pt) madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it is with great pleasure that i am here today to present to the european parliament the work programme of the portuguese presidency for the first half of 2000. you have already read the text of this programme, and i shall therefore limit myself to stressing some of the main points. i would like to begin by emphasizing that my country understands that the work of the presidency is not only aimed at the desirable efficiency at the level of the council of ministers, but also at an effort of close cooperation with the community institutions and all the community bodies, as well as at permanent transparency of the activities of the presidency vis-à-vis european public opinion. the portuguese presidency's relationship with the european parliament will deserve particular attention because of the specific role it plays in the interinstitutional framework and because of the fact that this body enjoys legitimacy deriving from the direct vote of the european citizens of the various countries. that is the first message i wanted to convey and it guarantees that the presidency will always be available to provide clarifications and to cooperate fully and frankly with this house. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, europe is now at a decisive moment in defining its model of political and economic organization and in asserting its identity at the global level in the face of the new challenges it intends to face. the project of creating conditions for stability and development throughout the continent, which is the great political objective of the present european generation, obliges us to make a choice between certain options which will influence the dimension of the union's own future project. in recent years we have been able to secure very significant progress which respects the creation of the internal market and the gradual consolidation of the ambitious project of the single currency. we must now go further: we must ensure that these benefits are accompanied by the parallel development of other policies in order to increase the consistency of a coherent process which responds to the major concerns and aspirations of the european people. if we fail to use the instruments at our disposal in an effective and convincing way, that is to say, the europe we have already succeeded in building, it is obvious that it will not be possible to stimulate the will of our citizens to accept the construction of more europe. the portuguese presidency will commit itself to ensuring that the european social model evolves in the future in a way that is compatible with maintaining the union's ability to be at the forefront of global economic competitiveness. to help make this project a reality, we will be organising an extraordinary european council in march next year under the title 'employment, economic reforms and social cohesion - for a europe of innovation and knowledge'. what is the purpose of this initiative, some of you may ask. will this idea add any value to the one that just took place? or does portugal intend to start a new process to be added to those already sketched out in luxembourg, cardiff or cologne? this is a legitimate question and you already have part of the answer in the document that the portuguese prime minister announced two days ago. with this work project we intend to create a better articulation, a better coordination of the processes in progress, while introducing a new dimension. we must ensure that europe gains a new impetus which will enable it to become, within 10 years, the most dynamic and active economic area in the world. to do this, it is important to ensure that the european economy manages to optimise all the instruments at its disposal and, in particular, that it does not allow itself any delay in the decisive struggle for competitiveness. we believe that this struggle now involves the democratization of the information and knowledge society at european level, by radically reducing the distance which separates it in this field from other areas with which it competes due to economic globalisation. it is this effort to modernise, update and combine new resources that we propose to launch at the lisbon european council. we are counting on all of us, on this parliament, on the social partners, on the other areas of civil society and, of course, on the governments of the member states, to achieve this essential objective. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the political division of the european continent has ceased to exist for several years now. the unification of europe has become a strategic objective which the european union must fully assume and for which there can be no hesitation. for decades, people with restricted wills have been told that we are building a model of freedom and progress on this side of europe that we want to see shared by all. it is now time to be consistent with what we have said. the project of enlarging the european union and all the contractual models we intend to create with other countries on the continent are aimed in the same direction: to guarantee a large area of stability and development that can give the whole of europe a future of peace and progress. the portuguese presidency has an important task of ensuring the continuity of the enlargement negotiations which began in 1998 in the light of rigorous technical criteria and an assessment of the objective merits of each of the candidates. we intend to open all possible negotiating chapters with these countries in a rapid and efficient manner based on the proposals made by the european commission. as for the six candidate countries which have already started negotiations, we will also work with full commitment to ensure that they have the opportunity to make up any lost time, without in any way jeopardising the negotiation processes already under way. the special case of turkey will deserve our special attention, given its particular situation and the need to ensure a consistent expectation of closer relations with the union, of which it is one of the key countries on the world stage. enlargement is thus a european objective which the portuguese presidency will not shy away from and to which it will give impetus. the european union considers that for enlargement to take place, it is essential to reform its institutions in order to make their respective functioning more democratic, more efficient and more transparent. some of these reforms can be carried out without changing the treaties, by improving the working methods of the institutions. other reforms require a revision of the treaties, which will be done at an intergovernmental conference which we will launch in a few weeks' time and which will be concluded by the end of this year. this is undoubtedly a difficult and delicate task because it concerns the management of decision-making power within the union. we want to start it on the basis of a model combining ambition and realism, that is to say, going as far as possible and necessary within the framework of a consensus guaranteeing the acceptability of the results by the member states by the end of the year 2000. this date should be respected even if, as everyone knows, circumstances may lead to a prolongation of the debate which leads to delays in the enlargement process, circumstances which would certainly have negative political effects and which need to be taken into account. we are aware that with this new reform we run the risk of falling short of the expectations of some and we are well aware of the legitimate desire of many of you in this parliament to go further. i can assure you that the portuguese presidency will do everything within the mandate given to it in helsinki to make the agenda of this conference a set of topics which can constitute substantial reform, but, in making this commitment on behalf of the presidency, i cannot of course guarantee miracles and, in particular, i cannot promise that the joint will of the governments of the member states will live up to your expectations and wishes. i speak to you with sincerity and frankness because i do not want to create false illusions. in this context, i would like to return to a point which concerns the portuguese presidency, or more precisely, which has always concerned my country, even before it began this presidency: the way in which the european parliament is represented at this intergovernmental conference. in this respect, which we also know is sensitive, our position, without wishing to depart from what was envisaged in the helsinki conclusions, is to try to go as far as possible in the development of this parliament, whether in the formal framework established in those conclusions or in an informal model which this institution considers appropriate. the cooperation of the presidency is guaranteed, in whatever form. although it must be admitted that we are faced with a representation model which has improved the status of this european parliament during the negotiations of the treaty of amsterdam, we consider it important to work in a way which can promote the establishment of an environment of trust and effective collaboration between the council and parliament. i have therefore written to the president of the european parliament to inform her that the presidency intends to begin the work of the intergovernmental conference at a special ministerial meeting on the sidelines of the february general affairs council, in accordance with the decisions taken in helsinki. i shall therefore have the opportunity, at the beginning of each ministerial conference, to exchange views with the president and two representatives of this parliament. the council will also have two observers at all meetings of the preparatory group, which will be chaired by the secretary of state for european affairs. i also indicated in that letter that the presidency is keen to ensure effective involvement of the european parliament in the igc agenda. we are prepared to consider our participation in any other working model that parliament deems appropriate, in accordance with the helsinki conclusions. i want to assure you that you can count on us for this joint work. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the union's role in the world can only be asserted in defence of its principles and its interests, which are aimed at giving credibility to europe's voice, if we are able to guarantee an effective response to the crises that arise on the strategic scene, to which we cannot remain indifferent. the kosovo crisis has been and continues to be a lesson for all of us, from which we must draw the consequences, possibly with different visions. i believe that now, more than in the past, the need for europe to have its own capabilities has become apparent in order to act effectively and in a timely manner in crisis management and in the execution of operations that can guarantee stability and peace in areas vital to our collective security. the european council in helsinki gave the portuguese presidency the task of putting into practice new security and defence mechanisms in the european framework, compatible with the commitments undertaken by some of us in the framework of the atlantic alliance, as well as a specific situation affecting certain partners within the european union. it is also important that we can ensure that this new model is fully compatible with the interests of our nato partners, both at european level and in the transatlantic context. during these six months we will test the common will to work in this area and try to ensure the design of a model of articulation that can be comfortable for the different sensitivities and interests involved. this is undoubtedly a difficult task, but we are convinced that it is a challenge of major importance for the credibility of the union's external action and we will naturally explore the possibilities offered by our simultaneous presidencies of the european union and the western european union. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to make a few comments on the union's external relations and to highlight some of the complementary aspects of the portuguese presidency's work programme. we believe that the european effort to have strong and operative institutions at home must go hand in hand with ensuring that sufficient attention is paid to what is happening outside its own area. europe has always been a winner when it has maintained an active and open external dimension, when it has not withdrawn into itself in order not to face the challenges posed by the outside world. we are now faced with the need to look this world in the eye and to be present in an operative way. for this reason, our presidency intends to carry out a series of actions which promote and strengthen europe's presence in the world, whether in the continuation of the traditional lines of existing relations or by promoting new initiatives in areas which we believe should be at the heart of the european agenda. we will of course pay particular attention to the serious situation in the balkans and to relations with russia and ukraine, with particular emphasis on the hotspots of tension affecting this area close to the union. we also intend to ensure that the mediterranean remains high on our external agenda, and we will take various initiatives in the context of the barcelona process and ensure visibility of the union's involvement in the middle east peace process. an important first step was taken by my recent trip to the region, during which i visited syria, israel, palestine, jordan, egypt and lebanon with the high representative of the common foreign and security policy and the commission. we are still determined to develop an integrated political dialogue with the whole of africa and to ensure that the process established under the lomé convention is successfully pursued. latin america will deserve a special place in this external action framework, given the growing importance of this area for europe and the complementarity of the interests which today unite us with this area of the world. the transatlantic dialogue with the united states and canada will also be high on our agenda, with particular attention to the aspects which have shaped our joint participation in the euro-atlantic institutions and, in particular, our commitment to relaunching the debate in the world trade organisation in the near future. many other initiatives, particularly in the multilateral framework and in bilateral political dialogue, could be highlighted. i shall confine myself to emphasizing the novelty of the summit with india and the ministerial meetings with australia and new zealand. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would not like to prolong my speech any further, but i would like to allow a question-and-answer session, which i shall be very happy to answer. i would not like to end without mentioning two key priorities which will be the focus of our work and one which is directly related to the functioning of this house. the first question relates to the field of justice and home affairs: this is very likely one of the sectors in which the union's activities are expanding and which, after amsterdam, has shown more promise. in this respect, we are awaiting concrete proposals from the european commission to enable us to achieve the creation of an area of freedom, security and justice that meets the expectations of european citizens in this respect in the european project. the second question concerns the question of food safety: we are currently experiencing a very delicate situation at european level with the creation of an atmosphere of distrust which has implications for the internal market and which has a negative impact on consumer protection, in addition to the effects in the context of our external relations. we think it's important to reverse this trend. to do this, it is vital that we succeed in ensuring a harmonized framework of work at european level, namely through the creation of an agency that can function as an instrument for articulating the different national dimensions. the draft recently put forward by the commission in its white paper will be dealt with properly by the portuguese presidency, in particular through a report to be presented to the feira council in june. finally, i should like to make it clear that the question of the status of members and assistants of this parliament will receive the necessary attention from the presidency, because we believe that it is essential to guarantee an important aspect which concerns the dignity of the functions of those who act within this institution. in this context, we will do our utmost to ensure that, through dialogue with you and joint work within the council, a fair and balanced solution to this problem is found. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, these are the main messages i wanted to convey to you on behalf of the portuguese government as the portuguese presidency of the union begins. i am of course at your disposal for any further clarification you may require. thank you for your attention. - madam president, between its first and its last version, the theato report on the protection of the community's financial interests has undergone an interesting development. the proposal for a community regulation establishing an independent european prosecutor has been dropped as being clearly contrary to article 280 of the treaty and has been reduced to a simple call for the next intergovernmental conference. it has been replaced by the proposal for a regulation creating a rather bizarre new entity, an independent european body exercising powers to monitor the regularity of investigations by the anti-fraud office, olaf. in this second proposal i find the echo of my speech of 25 october last, in which i was concerned, like a few other members, about the conditions under which the interinstitutional agreement on olaf investigations is to be applied in the european parliament. perhaps they are trying to take our criticisms into account, even if it is belatedly. unfortunately, this new independent body, which is supposed to be an independent office, seems very strange to me and still does not answer the fundamental question i was asking, which is that of the autonomy of our assembly. as for the independent european prosecutor, it is a proposal which runs counter to our conception of a europe of nations, as i explained in yesterday's debate and in the debate on 13 september on the second report of the committee of independent experts. it is, however, still being put forward by a whole series of lawyers, supposedly intellectually independent, but in reality, more often than not, paid directly or indirectly by the commission. they would do better to deal with the privileges and immunities of the commission which, according to the independent experts' report itself, are hampering the fight against fraud. we also find it quite extraordinary that the idea of the european prosecutor should be included in the theato report without any consultation of our committee responsible for monitoring institutional affairs, when such an innovation would profoundly alter the balance of the institutions. but as is usual in european affairs, reforms are launched without really explaining the scale of their implications at the outset. this is part of the disinformation that keeps the system moving forward.
- madam president, the report presented to us today proposed that the commission be given discharge in accordance with article 276 of the treaty in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european communities for the financial year 1997. the french members of the europe of nations group, for their part, refused to vote in favour of this measure. the report on the discharge for 1997 was already postponed by parliament on 4 may last, because it appeared that the santer commission, which had resigned and was confined to the discharge of current affairs, was not in a position to make the commitments for reform that seemed necessary in the light of the extent of the criticism from the court of auditors. today the prodi commission has indeed made these commitments and has already initiated several reforms. does that mean we should grant discharge? it should be recalled that the court of auditors' report for 1997 was very severe and refused to grant the statement of assurance on the reliability of the underlying transactions, as defined in article 248 of the treaty. the court, while stating that the commitments appeared to it to be regular, added this essential clarification: 'as in previous years, the impact of errors affecting the operations underlying the commission's payments is of such importance that the court cannot give assurance that these operations are legal and regular'. if the court does not want to give its assurance on the whole of the 1997 budget, why have the members of the european parliament decided to give their moral guarantee by giving the discharge? of course, we are told that the commission is not the same, but we reply that the implementation of the 1997 budget is still what it is. she hasn't changed in six months. moreover, not all the wrong underlying transactions are the responsibility of the commission. member states have often been involved.
- madam president, the van hulten report on reforms to remedy the commission's crisis follows fairly closely the second report by the independent experts on which my group already commented on 13 september. but the reforms proposed are not sufficiently put into perspective, so that the multiplicity of proposals for improvements, sometimes good, sometimes bad, may hide the real problems of the functioning of the european institutions. in particular, since the first report by the independent experts revealed cases of individual failures, one might have expected the second to analyse the corruption channels operating on a permanent basis around the european institutions, as described in some documents circulating at the time of the report's drafting. but none of that. of course, it is better to propose reforms for the future than to go back and forth on the past. but i think that in this case the sugaring of the past is blinding the scale of the reforms that are needed. of course, there are many such reforms, but what is at issue above all is the theory of the commission's independence, which prevents people from being aware that the commission is to be nothing more than a service common to the member states and which prevents the member states from exercising real control over it. the commission must therefore be opposed to all those who would make the commission an opaque fortress to control, in particular: giving the council back genuine political control over the commission; to strengthen the two-way cooperation between the european court of auditors and national courts, in order to improve controls both in the states and in brussels; to remove the quasi-diplomatic privileges enjoyed by the commission which hamper investigations; to open the european civil service much more to national civil servants specialised in temporary secondment; finally, as our committee on employment and social affairs proposed in an opinion which has not been followed up, we should completely review the possibility of financing interest groups, without prior authorization, from part a of the budget, a possibility which today opens the door to the distribution of subsidies without a legal basis and encourages patronage around the commission.
