- the next item is the report (a5-0042/2000) by mr goebbels, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy, on the recommendation of the european central bank for a council regulation (ec) on the supplementary calls for foreign reserve assets by the european central bank (ecb 0001/1999 - c5-0202/1999 - 1999/0817 (cns))
- (de) mr president, in its draft legislative resolution, parliament endorses the ecb's recommendation calling for a council regulation on the additional call for other foreign reserves. the reasons given are as follows. firstly, the treaty provides for this. if this appeal is not covered by a regulation, it could be seen as a difference of opinion between the ecb and the council. secondly, the necessary financial independence of the ecb must be strengthened. thirdly, the credibility of the monetary intervention instrument and the ecb's ability to react to various scenarios must be ensured. of course, there is nothing wrong with a structural improvement in the financial situation of the ecb. the only question is whether the problem can be solved permanently with outside funding. before a judgment can be made, at least the following questions must be discussed. first, is it reasonable for the economy to pursue a monetary policy as restrictive as that of the ecb, more restrictive than that of the edf? secondly, is the rise in interest rates on marginal refinancing and deposit-taking, as has been the case since 9 february this year, not contrary to cyclical developments? thirdly, is not taking stronger measures to combat unemployment the most effective way of ensuring price stability? fourthly, should not more importance be attached, alongside supply-oriented economic policy, to demand-oriented economic policy, i.e. the strengthening of the european internal market by lowering income taxes in the member states? fifthly, is it wrong to think that the fixing of exchange rates at the time of the introduction of the euro reflected more a political wish than an economic reality? sixthly, what are the concrete causes of the losses likely to be incurred by the ecb in 1999? the answer to these questions requires our group not to approve this motion for a resolution, not because the ecb has too few foreign exchange reserves, but because it is badly structured and will therefore constantly complain of such liquidity difficulties.

mr president, one can rightly be intrigued by the european central bank's request to double the ceiling on its ability to call on the national central banks for foreign reserves. it is true that raising the current ceiling of eur 50 billion - in reality eur 39.5 billion, because some countries are not participating in the single currency - to eur 100 billion may at first sight seem acceptable, given that national central banks will still have eur 300 billion of official reserves of their own. however, this operation is so close in time to the date on which the single currency was launched that it clearly shows that the valuation of reserves carried out at that time was largely underestimated. why would you do that ? apart from a few technical explanations of detail, such as the exact number of ecb staff, there is only one valid reason: the europe-optimism surrounding the launch of the euro, as it was called at the time, led to the idea that the single currency would naturally be strong and that the question of reserves was therefore secondary. everyone seems to be coming back to more realism now. but the matter is not closed, because the explanatory memorandum to the draft regulation, like that of the european parliament's report, worries us rather by pointing out incidentally that the purpose of raising the ceiling is, i quote: 'to promote the ecb's ability to adapt to different possible scenarios'. since we are not looking at a scenario of the euro rising - in which case there would obviously be no need for additional reserves - we are looking at a scenario of the euro falling. the european parliament's report is even more alarmist, since it mentions in full the potential instability of the euro, which, in its view, would not be more approved. this is a mistake which will probably not please mr duisenberg, who explains every day that the euro is basically a stable currency. but it's still a very revealing lapse. it is not realistic to believe that an artificial currency can inspire the same confidence as a currency firmly supported by a people.

in writing. - the proposal of the european central bank leads us to ask ourselves and to act with caution, and this for two reasons: as regards the method, it can be seen that the way of proceeding remains the same: the community institutions present truncated reports, which minimize the consequences of a further loss of sovereignty for the states, and they proceed by small successive touches. the commission argued, for example, that when the euro was introduced, the sovereignty of the member states was in no way threatened by the ecb or the escb, which was set up to hold and manage the official foreign reserves of the member states. however, it is not mentioned that the national central banks manage these funds on behalf of the ecb, which is the sole master of monetary policy, and that, while article 30-1 of the statute of the ecb set the maximum amount of reserve assets at eur 50 billion, an amount considered sufficient to ensure the ecb's independence, two years later the dogma of independence calls for article 30-4 to provide additional assets on the grounds that its independence and credibility still need to be increased... we have to ask ourselves whether this gulf is bottomless or even bottomless! in the end, the "dress" of this new exorbitant demand must not deceive us; this is not only a question of giving more financial resources to an independent institution to implement an effective monetary policy for the benefit of the member states, but also indirectly generating additional resources for a technocratic structure to enable it to finance ever-increasing operational needs. the artistic blur is thus skillfully maintained; while the euro was supposed to be 'strong and stable' and the reserve assets were originally intended to serve as a defence during the transitional period (if necessary), it now appears that neither of these forecasts has been met and that frankfurt is totally immobile! a new question arises: the question of the effective use of these financial means. why should the states abandon their resources to a community institution which, because of its necessary independence, must not be subject to control? in conclusion, let us remember that the state is not defined only by the sovereignty it possesses by virtue of its autonomy to act. experience shows that its authority and credibility on the international scene depend very much on the resources at its disposal: we must therefore be careful, because to deprive it of both would be, in the long run, to deny it!
- doc. a5-0046/2000 by mrs izquierdo rojo, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, on the proposal for a council regulation on information measures in the field of the common agricultural policy (com (99) 536 - c5-0249/1999 - 1999/0209 (cns)).
commission - (fi) mr president, first of all i should like to thank the rapporteur, mrs maria izquierdo rojo, and the members of the committee on agriculture for this report. the purpose of the proposal for a regulation is to provide the european commission with an instrument enabling it to present the model of action for european agriculture and to give greater publicity to the common agricultural policy. it will therefore facilitate the implementation of the agricultural policy. the amendments proposed by the european parliament are now being discussed. in general, they are not intended to change the substance, but rather to clarify the proposals. amendments nos 2 and 6 concern the bodies and organisations which will be covered by the aid. article 2 states that all agricultural organisations and rural stakeholders are involved. the proposed additions are therefore unnecessary. amendments nos 5, 8 and 10 concern the eligible shares. amendment no 5 contains details on information measures for rural men and women and on the debate on agricultural policy. these details are unnecessary, because they are already contained in the commission's proposal. one of the wording changes proposed in this amendment, 'assist them in their choice', is not in line with the commission's proposal. the purpose of this regulation is not to offer specific services to farmers. this can be done better by local bodies. the available resources would also be insufficient for this purpose. similarly, as regards the text added to article 3, i would point out that information visits are not excluded. the list of eligible actions is not exhaustive, as is implied by the word 'particularly'. the commission is, however, prepared to accept this clarification. however, funding for long-term exchange programmes cannot be accepted, as such actions do not fall within the scope of information policy. amendment no 10 concerns article 5 of the treaty. the commission is in favour of the objectives set out in the regulation, as is shown by the fact that they are implicitly included in article 1, which concerns the european agricultural model of action. there is therefore no reason to repeat the contents of this model in full. amendments nos 7 and 13 concern the percentage of funding. the commission considers that it is not desirable to finance more than 75% of the eligible costs. the resources available are not very large. the lower the share of funding, the more it is possible to grant and the greater the multiplier effect. amendments nos 9 and 12 concern the adjustment and allocation of appropriations. as we know, the european parliament exercises budgetary authority jointly with the council. the commission therefore considers that amendment no 9 is unnecessary. as regards amendment no 12, which proposes to incorporate the adjustment of appropriations into the regulation, i would say that if this adjustment is fixed in advance, the necessary flexibility for budgetary administration is lost, which may be detrimental to the requests for funding that will be submitted. amendment no 11 is about evaluation. the commission shares the view of the parliament on the usefulness of regular evaluation. it is in the implementing regulation that it can best be taken into account. amendment no 4 concerns the administrative measures. the commission considers that this additional introductory paragraph is unnecessary in the regulation. the administrative details, the evaluation and the subsequent evaluation will be specified in an implementing regulation. in this connection, it should be recalled that in a procedure it is necessary to ensure effective control of public funds, regardless of the transparency or simplicity of the procedure. amendments nos 1 and 3 deal with language issues. the commission considers that these details are unnecessary, since in the commission's proposal paragraphs 4 and 7 of the introduction are not so restrictive.
- thank you, chief. the debate is closed. we'll move on to the vote. (parliament adopted the legislative resolution)
- doc. a5-045/2000 by mrs izquierdo rojo, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, on the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1577/96 introducing a specific measure in favour of certain leguminous vegetables (com (99) 428 - c5-0187/1999 - 1999/0182 (cns))
commission. - (fi) mr president, i should like to thank the rapporteur, mrs maria izquierdo rojo, once again for her well-written and constructive report. the question of pulses in question is based on two commission documents. the first is the report on the aid scheme for pulses and the second is the proposal to improve the management of the scheme. what are these plants ? i know that the spanish members are well aware of this, but let me make it clear that legumes are three annual plants with a high protein content and which are harvested as dried seeds. lentils and chickpeas are used in human nutrition, while the seeds of the lesser known vesca are used as fodder. grain legumes are grown in fields mainly in the south of the european union, as they are well adapted to a very dry climate. in fact, spain's share of the eu's pulses crop is 90%. grain legumes are not covered by the aid scheme revised by agenda 2000, although they may be used in crop rotation with other crops grown in fields, such as cereals. they have their own scheme, where the fixed aid per hectare is eur 181 and the maximum guaranteed area is 400 000 hectares. the scheme was introduced in 1989 because of the decline in the area under leguminous crops in favour of other cereals, which were already overproducing. the aim of this special scheme was to preserve traditional cereal legume crops through aid per hectare. what conclusions can be drawn from the commission's report? when we look at the application of the scheme, we find that the maximum guaranteed area of 400 000 hectares has been systematically exceeded. this leads to two conclusions. firstly, the objective of the scheme has been fully achieved and secondly, the areas should be more stable. if we look at the exceedances of the maximum guaranteed area in recent years, we see that the areas have been exceeded, particularly with regard to the weeds. although the scheme is generally applied satisfactorily, the management of the maximum guaranteed areas is problematic, as producers exceeding the maximum areas are not treated differently from other producers. how could we improve the diet? efforts should be made to find measures for improvement within the framework of the current system and the appropriations allocated to it. we are in a situation where agenda 2000 has been adopted and international trade negotiations are only just about to begin. i would also point out that the amendment proposed by the rapporteur, namely to combine the current aid with that under another common market organization, that of seeds, would not be a desirable improvement. i refer to amendment no 2. it cannot be accepted for two reasons. the first is that the regimes are in contradiction with each other, because in one the weeds are theoretically to be harvested for fodder, and in the other for sowing. the second is that it could lead to additional costs. the commission proposes, in accordance with its report, to subdivide the maximum guaranteed area in a 40/60 ratio as follows: 160 000 hectares for lentils and chickpeas and 240 000 hectares for legumes. it is also proposed to replace the management committee for dried feed with the management committee for cereals. the purpose of this amendment is simply to incorporate into the rules a practice which has become commonplace in committees. finally, i would point out that the commission agrees with the amendments proposed by the rapporteur which confirm its position and which propose that the commission submit a new report - amendment no 3 - and endeavour to improve the system, namely amendment no 1. ladies and gentlemen, in the light of my comments, i think it should not be difficult to adopt the proposal so that it can be implemented from the 2000-01 marketing year.
- thank you, chief. the debate is closed. we'll move on to the vote. (parliament adopted the legislative resolution)

perhaps i could continue with the other aspect of my presentation to parliament this afternoon: it is the proposal to introduce esb tests, and i have the pleasure of presenting it to parliament this afternoon. i have stated on several occasions that i regard the new rapid postmortem tests as one of the most important instruments in our fight to control bse. the commission has been working on a proposal to introduce these tests in bse control throughout the community since september last year. we currently have three different tests that have been shown to provide excellent results when used to test animals with clinical signs of disease after death. these tests provide new opportunities for routine testing on a large number of animals. an active control programme carried out in switzerland has demonstrated that the use of rapid post-mortem tests is likely to significantly improve the effectiveness of bse control, in particular if they focus on animals that have died on the holding or are sent for emergency slaughter. since 1998, the community has had a bse surveillance programme based on the examination of animals showing clinical symptoms which may suggest the presence of bse. the commission is now proposing to replace this programme with a new one in which each member state tests a representative sample of animals which have died on the farm and have been killed in an emergency on its territory. the size of the sample will be increased from 25 to 100 times for each member state, depending on the size of its herd, compared with the current system. i expect the new proposed monitoring system to provide much better information than is currently available on the incidence of bse in the community. i am also pleased to be able to tell parliament that these particular tests will produce a result within 24 hours. we propose to test a minimum of 65 000 animals per year throughout the community; the tests will start in january 2001. the proposed decision does not in itself have any implications for the community budget, but this matter will be discussed next week in the special veterinary committee. i commend to parliament the proposals which have been made this afternoon through the commission.

mr president, while this parliament is getting lost in the details, we are forced to deal quickly with one of the essential dimensions of the european problem: the mediterranean. the complementarities that exist between the interests of the two continents, europe and africa, this vast euro-african whole of which the mediterranean is necessarily the pivot, give our mediterranean policy an importance, and i would say a gravity, which is unfortunately very little reflected in the programmes carried out so far by the european institutions and the fact that, as in the case of meda, three quarters of the programmes adopted remain unimplemented. the fact is that we are completely unaware of the issues at stake. this one's huge. we said it, let's say it again. we will only succeed in creating a unified and fraternal whole between the north and the south of this sea between the continents if we remain at the centre of the world's balances, instead of being relegated to the periphery of the world's balances, to the benefit, of course, of other geostrategic ensembles: the atlantic first, the indian ocean, or above all the pacific, basins on whose shores we are increasingly just comrades. there is no salvation here, except through a voluntarism which means - i say this clearly - that we should put atlantic solidarity or relations with the asian continent in the background and concentrate on privileged relations - i say 'privileged' in the strict sense of the term - with the arab world. this would mean, for example, accepting countries such as morocco, tunisia or algeria into the union as full member states. without this voluntarism, we shall have no chance of controlling the world's imbalances, or rather its growing imbalances, no control over economic flows - i am thinking in particular of raw materials, but also of agricultural production - no control over demographic flows, whose balances are rapidly being upset to our detriment, as everyone knows, but also no control over cultural flows, because we certainly have no better allies than our arab and african partners to resist what is hastily called globalisation, and which seems to me to be very largely the mechanization of the world. our nations will remain great powers in the next century depending on whether or not they have met the test of the mediterranean partnership. needless to say, we are pessimistic about this. firstly, because this essential dimension lives on in the lethargy and the complacent vagaries of discourse, as evidenced by the pale - so pale - barcelona process, a miserable alibi for our indifference to the land. pessimism also because our atlantic partner, the united states of america, has fully understood that there is no better way to subject europe to its empire than to cut off the fruitful ties it can maintain with its mediterranean neighbours and which is ingenious in erecting on both sides of this basin an obscure but effective wall. the gulf war, the inclusion of libya and even syria in the list of nations to which washington has cleverly drawn us, are just some of the more recent examples. finally, pessimism because europe remains too divided on this point, too many states, especially the northern states of europe, preferring the atlantic link to the euro-arab and euro-african link, as evidenced by the gradual abandonment of the so-called lomé policy and the anaemia of the mediterranean policy. in short, on this subject as on others, only the nations, in the first place france, which remains the leading mediterranean power, remain to try to meet this immense challenge by means of its arab policy and its policy of the francophonie. it may do so alone, but it will do so for the benefit of europe as a whole.
mr president, the basic economic instrument for the implementation of our mediterranean policy, which emerged from the barcelona process, is undoubtedly the meda programme, for which i am the rapporteur on activities, and whose regulations we are amending with our colleague, mr valdivielso de cué. i would like to draw the attention of our colleagues to these reports which are being discussed in committee and which will be submitted to our assembly next june. i would like to emphasize two important points here: firstly, meda is a good programme, a young programme, which has commission. - mr president, in november 1996 the european commission adopted its first communication on the fight against child sex tourism. a year later, in november 1997, a european parliament resolution and a statement by the tourism council demonstrated the broad institutional consensus on the broad lines of the commission's communication. this support has since been concretised by the creation of a new budget line, with the funds made available for awareness campaigns in the european union against the development of sex tourism involving children. it is now reflected in the council conclusions of 21 december 1999, which show a new and firm political commitment to an important social problem, for the solution of which we are responsible. if, as we hope, the european parliament direction will provide additional elements to respond to the concerns expressed by european citizens regarding the development of this scourge. the report by mrs klamt follows up the commission communication of may 1999 presenting the actions carried out for the period 1997-98 and specifying the operational follow-up to be given with a view to the launching and/or implementation of new actions. you will have noted that community action in the fight against child sex tourism is continuing at a steady pace, in the framework of the initially agreed strategy aimed at reducing demand in cooperation, in particular with the tourism industry and the ngos concerned, and at addressing supply sources in the countries of destination of tourists by any appropriate means, including community policies in the field of external relations and development cooperation. the importance of this second component was also recalled by the commission in 1998 when it drew up the strategy to support the development of sustainable tourism in developing countries, which envisaged encouraging the specific problem of sex tourism involving children to be taken into account in a structured political dialogue with the countries most affected, particularly at regional level. the development of sex tourism involving children is a flagrant violation of the very idea of a human community gathered be focused on the search for and exploitation of synergies between these two modes of intervention, which are largely complementary in this case. this is all the more so as, alongside the progress made in effective self-regulation, i.e. including mechanisms for monitoring commitments, the development of police and judicial cooperation in europe is not without positive consequences for the crackdown on child sex tourism. the council joint action of 24 february 1997 on combating trafficking in human beings and the sexual exploitation of children, which provides for each member state to undertake to review its national legislation concerning measures relating to types of intentional behaviour, is exemplary in this respect. the fact that the existence of a double criminalization remains possible, by way of exception, must not obscure the essential contribution of that joint action, namely the assertion of the principle of extraterritorial jurisdiction applicable to one of its nationals or to a person habitually resident in its territory. this helps to understand the great interest that legislative reforms in this area and their practical translation in the application of the laws on a daily basis arouse. hence the importance attached by the european parliament to the assessment of the member states' compliance with their obligations under this joint action, which could be an opportunity to pay particular attention to the crackdown on child sex tourism, to draw up a preliminary assessment of the situation. in operational terms, implementation of all the planned actions continued at a steady pace. the fight against child sex tourism is an opportunity for the commission to mobilise its various services in the context of strengthening internal coordination. it also provides the commission with an opportunity to step up its cooperation with the national administrations, professional associations and non-governmental organisations concerned. other commission initiatives to increase the involvement of the tourism industry have also produced tangible results, in particular in the development and strengthening of codes of conduct and other self-regulatory mechanisms for the tourism industry. as you will understand, your support can only encourage us to continue with determination on the path we have set out.

draft motion for a resolution prepared by the committee responsible.

opportunity to thank mr turmes again for his work. but it goes further. as mr linhkor has pointed out, it is parliament which is partly pushing the commission to take more concrete action in the field of renewable energy and parliament has always acted as a vanguard and a driving force in this field. we all agree that renewable energy must play a key role in securing energy distribution and helping to reduce dependence on imports and implement the commitments signed in kyoto. however, they can also contribute to the technological development of the european union and enable clean technologies to be exported to other parts of the world. i would like to point out that mr turmes' report fully shares these views. the commission already supports the production of wind, solar, geothermal, biomass and small hydroelectric power stations, in other words all renewable energy sources, except for large hydroelectric power stations, which we do not think should be supported because they have sufficient potential and they have some extremely negative environmental aspects, since the construction of a dam always involves flooding a valley. but i would like to say to mr turmes that we cannot consider peat as a renewable energy source. the altener programme is a magnificent achievement and parliament has always been associated with and collaborated with the commission's efforts and has even - i repeat - been a driving force in giving greater ambition to the commission's proposals. we are faced with a major challenge, which is to define the most appropriate mechanisms to support the development of green electricity within an internal market, an open single electricity market, such as we want in the european union. i can assure you that all the points raised here will be taken into account in the directive, which will be debated in the coming days. turning to practical matters, i would like to say that virtually all the points raised in mr turmes' report deserve our support and are fully in line with our analysis. while it is true that some aspects are more questionable, they also deserve to be analysed in depth, although they are rejected in some cases for lack of feasibility or because they pose problems that are more important than the solutions they propose. i would like to stress that the report stresses the importance of the objective of doubling the share of renewable energy in gross domestic energy consumption from 6% to 12%. in the proposal for a directive we hope to set objectives chosen by each country, individual objectives for each country in the european union, not mandatory objectives but objectives which, at least from a political point of view, have an impact on the results and i think this is a very important step. i agree with mr turmes that the various national systems in force at the time of adoption of this directive must be protected. we are going to do that, but that does not mean that in five years' time we should not review the various systems and focus on those which are likely to be the most effective and which have led to greater development of renewable energy in the countries concerned. in any case, as you know, on 2 december 1999, at the energy council, i presented a questionnaire to the member states to see the state of play and to be able to present a directive which could achieve the necessary consensus to reach a rapid conclusion, both in parliament and in the council. the results of this questionnaire, which have been analysed by the services and which have resulted in a document of what i consider to be excellent quality, will, i hope, enable us to move beyond the formalities in parliament and the council rather quickly. the proposal - let us be very clear - simply seeks to encourage the production of electricity from renewable energy sources within the european union. i would like to say that i have taken note of what mr linhkor has said about agricultural policy and the possibility of encouraging non-food production. as a former minister of agriculture, i am sensitive to these issues and this is one of the issues which, in a way, is also taken into consideration in the proposal. i would also like to point out that our objective with all this is to have a more secure, more secure and more environmentally friendly energy supply throughout the union. in conclusion, mr president, some speakers have mentioned depreciation in their speeches. mr vidal-quadras and mr valdivielso have also said this recently. renewable energy cannot compete with conventional energy at present, especially when one considers that conventional energy has certain external costs which are obviously not internalised. we must support renewable energy. i think that we cannot burden other energy sources at the moment - that is my view, although there are others - for reasons of competitiveness and growth. but we can support renewable energy precisely because of its obvious environmental and emission-reducing characteristics. in this sense, those who rely on renewable energy must be assured that they will get a fair return on their investment. and of course we must create a stable framework for investments which pay off over a number of years. this is one of the topics currently being debated in the commission and the most difficult in some cases, with other elements but, in the end, everyone in the commission shares this need to promote green energy. mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur and all the speakers and assure them that this aspect of stability which allows medium-term investment decisions to be taken will also be included in the proposal for a directive which i hope to be able to present to you shortly.

- madam president, i think that the council and commission's statements have been very enlightening. the united states now recognises the existence of the "scholarship" system. languages are being lost in some of the union's governments. the press is full of details about this sprawling network of electronic surveillance. and yet, what an embarrassment in the words of the council and the commission! what an emberlified speech to avoid answering the questions posed. i have not heard any explanation as to why it took until parliamentarians discovered this enormous matter almost two years ago, and then they recently brought evidence of the truth of their revelations, for the council to agree very implicitly and with extreme circumstance that there is a problem. i would remind you of this problem: by virtue of privileged and very special links, a strategic ally and a member country join forces in the shadows to monitor private communications and spy on companies in other countries of the union. where are we going ? "father, keep us from our friends. our enemies, i will take care of". now that this truth has been established, you will understand, mr president, commissioner, that we felt entitled to ask you a little more about some of the questions that everyone is asking today. first, what do you know about the type of information intercepted by this system, the recipients to whom this information was ultimately transmitted and the reliability of the protections in place in europe for citizens' privacy and strategic information of companies? secondly, beyond the formal exchange of correspondence to which the commissioner referred, what serious steps have been taken towards the us authorities in this matter and with what results? thirdly, what can you tell us about the role that britain has played, or at least intends to play in this respect in the future, in this system? like it or not, the "scaffold" file is now open and will remain so. after the european parliament, other assemblies and the united states congress itself, with which i have been in contact, because there is no anti-americanism in our approach, have taken up the matter. our citizens are on alert. i would therefore like to turn to those of our colleagues who are still hesitant. attempting to stop this movement would now be a rearguard battle, which democratic opinion would no doubt judge harshly. on the contrary, and i have heard the comments, in particular from the spokesman for the socialist group, also from the liberal group, on the contrary, to advance together truth, transparency and ethics in international relations would meet a strong expectation. this is the choice made by more than a quarter of the members of this house when they tabled the request for a committee of inquiry. i think parliament will grow up to make it its business.
- madam president, i will be extremely brief, since i have only one minute. i will simply say that the revelation of the existence of the electronic espionage network 'eschelon', which was set up by the us national security agency, shows an extreme disregard for the rights, freedoms and sovereignty of the countries of europe. and we would like to think that this case is not indicative of a general attitude towards the european union. in this respect, we are astonished by the council's report. the presidency began by stating an excellent principle: any system of interception of communications is inadmissible if it does not respect the principles of human dignity and the legal standards of the member states, but the rest of the speech was extremely confusing. we have talked about the transmission of data within europe, the schengen information system, europol, all things that are not really in the subject. the question put to the council is extremely simple: are we going to ask for an end to the activities of the echelon network, which are contrary to the rights and freedoms of citizens? if this eschelon network is really intended to combat international organized crime, madam president, we must ask to be involved, we must take our share of the burden and we must create an international organization for this purpose. otherwise, this network must be closed down and we are joining the parliamentary committee of inquiry which has been requested by several groups in this european parliament, including the europe of nations group.
- madam president, all global communications by cable, satellite, telephone, fax, e-mail, mobile would be intercepted by the country of the statue of liberty, jefferson, lincoln, human rights! for us, of course, this is a shake-up, not of our technical knowledge of encryption, but of our political beliefs. the single market, competition and competitiveness were regarded as gods, all under the arbitration of the wto. we did everything with mr monti, yesterday with mr van miert, to preserve pure, perfect competition, even against our companies, our banks, our aircraft manufacturers, our insurers, the crédit lyonnais, rhone-poulenc. and then you find out that in this market, there is cheating, there is espionage, there are distortions of competition. this parliament, which wanted to spy on members with olaf in the name of protecting europe's financial interests, discovers that we are being spied on by the united states, against our financial interests, even in the wto negotiations. we believed our freedoms were being threatened by mr. haider's austria. and it is through the britain of mr tony blair, of glyn ford, where fifteen thousand agents, spread over gibraltar, cyprus, and even on english soil, are spying on us. so, madam president, are you going to london again? in writing. - the regulation aims to reduce noise pollution around community airports, which are generally close to the economic centres of the union, i.e. in highly urbanised areas. the regulation provides for a ban, as from may 2000, on certain noisy aircraft equipped with noise abatement devices called 'hushkits'. the civil aviation industry is growing at an annual rate of some 6%, which is expected to double in 10 years! this can only be accompanied by a gradual reduction in aircraft noise. the noise problem is also a current issue at american airports. it is at international level, within the icao, that stricter standards for aircraft noise should be established. the resolution emphasizes this. the regulation was deferred for one year in 1999 and will apply in may with a large number of derogations. according to the latest euro-american talks, this conflict is not ready to be settled, since, moreover, the americans have lodged an appeal with the icao. the us industry is exerting enormous pressure and the prospect of elections is distorting the game. the us position on the regulation is ambiguous; although the us administration is in favour of closing the case, the us manufacturers are strongly opposed to the standards, set out in the regulation, which would penalise them. but how can we defend such derogations on the pretext that there is a dispute? - mr president, the action plans on asylum and migration, which focus on the problems faced by the countries of origin and transit of asylum seekers and migrants, seem to us to be an excellent initiative in principle. we are therefore surprised at the severity of the european parliament's report and the general tone of yesterday's debate. in order to make a useful contribution to migration flows, action must be taken on their root causes. the aim of the action plans is therefore to list the problems faced by each target country, whether they relate to political institutions, human rights, the economy or administration, and to propose to the union countries and to third countries an integrated approach combining development aid, legal measures or foreign policy actions. we therefore think that this is a smart exercise, and that it should be conducted more often at european level. why are so many of our colleagues critical? firstly, because they consider that this intelligent exercise is taking place in a far too intergovernmental context and that the high-level group responsible for preparing the plans is made up of representatives of the commission, but also, horresco referens, of national officials. however, it seems to us that, while consultation is useful at european level, the presence of national officials and the central role given to the member states in the decision-making process are the very conditions for the effectiveness of the action plans. the second category of criticism is that the action plans are too repressive because they contain measures to combat illegal immigration and advocate the extension of readmission agreements with third countries. but for us, this is not a defect, it is a good idea. it is an absolutely essential part of these plans. you can't want everything and its opposite at the same time.

in writing. - the text we are debating today is certainly more important to us than the others, since it concerns the protection of children against sex tourism. the european commission is giving us an overview of the measures already taken in this field. the results clearly show that the european union and its member states need to step up their efforts to combat sex tourism and the exploitation of children. member states should have extraterritorial legislation enabling them to investigate, prosecute and punish any individual guilty of crimes committed abroad and related to the sexual exploitation of children. we must go further by implementing measures such as the establishment of a coherent policy on child protection by creating a new general legal basis in the context of the next revision of the treaty, with sufficient community funding. i also believe that it is essential to incorporate the rights of the child in the charter of fundamental rights. at the same time, action on the ground is needed to encourage travel agencies, tour operators, transport companies and advertisers to set up self-regulatory systems to combat child sex tourism by setting up toll-free telephone numbers for children in need in all member states. exemplary sanctions should be adopted against those who commit such monstrosities. indeed, people in a foreign country, in an unfamiliar area, may act in complete anonymity and convince themselves that child abuse is less reprehensible in a different social and cultural context and that the moral concepts prevailing in their country are not there. this is intolerable ! in writing. - the final text of mr turmes' report can only make those who are concerned about reconciling a rational energy policy with the vital imperative of preserving the environment uncomfortable. the general objectives of this report are not the problem: the current situation and the number of disasters it has caused have made us regularly aware of the importance of the issue, and there is no need at this time to insist on the importance of putting an end to an energy policy whose constraints force rusty ships to carry carcinogenic petroleum waste without control and under a flag of complacency. but here we are, mr turmes' text, under the dual influence of the compromises so dear to this house and the ecological 'credo' which, starting from proven findings, then takes the paths of the most ethereal utopia, turns into a veritable 'gas factory' producing something other than the simple promotion of renewable energies. mr rapporteur, we shall therefore, out of charity, pass over the indirect effect of your proposal to create a tax on co2 emissions, which highlights the ecological nature of nuclear energy, its 'clean' nature contributing to the preservation of the ozone layer: while we welcome this possible interpretation, we are not sure that this was the aim you were seeking. but it must be stressed that in your first paragraph you propose nothing less than the creation of a european tax: the adoption of such a measure would set a very serious precedent for all those who oppose a uniform european taxation. you are naively calling for a uniform application of the community rules on state aid, so that all member states and all energy sources are subject to the same provisions: you are therefore hoping, in fact, as soon as possible, to impose a common energy policy, not just a common one, but an identical one, on northern finland, the centre of spain, the southern alps and the outermost regions of the union, and it is symbolic - and to say the least somewhat distressing - that the only amendment tabled in plenary underlines the specific nature of island situations, a proof of the lack of discernment to which your frantic attempt to impose your conception of energy policy leads you. but where your egalitarian fancy turns into doctrinaire blindness is when you assume your desire to see binding targets imposed on the member states in this matter, accompanied by sanctions in the event of failure to achieve the objectives: this kind of summation is not to be put in a box which has not yet officially renounced to consider the member states as independent nations, freely conducting the policies of their choice. you have the merit of unveiling your batteries, but in a somewhat peremptory way, by stating that the member states recognize that it is necessary to promote renewable energy sources as a priority: we believe that it is indeed necessary to promote these renewable energy sources, but that the priority is the elaboration of a comprehensive energy plan which does not ignore the existing one, and includes in particular the necessary adaptations of nuclear infrastructures towards greater safety, as it is true that its total eradication, which you seem to hold so dear, is possible only if 7/10ths of the surface of the planet is devoted exclusively to the development of alternative energies as you define them. this is enough to condemn a text whose good intentions do not suffice to conceal the federalist logic and harmful unrealism.
in writing. - since we do not trust the health industry, which is more interested in profits than in people, and unfortunately some researchers and doctors who follow their logic, we can only agree with the spirit of amendment 3 bis (new) which rejects all manipulation of the human germline and all cloning of human beings. the meaning of our vote against human cloning is above all an act of distrust of the present economic and social organization, and by no means an act of distrust of science and its possibilities. we are not opposed in principle to the use of human germline for people who want to have children without risking malformations, nor are we opposed to cloning to develop human tissues for transplantation. such techniques would undoubtedly represent a progress for mankind, as would many others still to come, if they were not, as they are now, diverted by the lure of profit, if they were put at the service of a conscious and disinterested humanity.

congratulate the rapporteur - i do not think that the measures proposed are adequate to the problem we are facing. communication techniques are transforming the data. the internet thus has structuring and multiplier effects on the trade and trafficking in child pornography. this traffic is unprecedented in its scale and geographical areas covered. there is an urgency and specific measures must be proposed because we are dealing with networks. in all the member states of the union, individual acts of paedophilia are suppressed, but ignorance and inefficiency continue to prevail in the suppression of networks. we are dealing with ephemeral, evolving sites that are constantly adapting and whose control is complex. this requires an assessment of the situation of paedophile networks in the countries of the european union. the existence of these networks confirms the need for a common legal area. the rapporteur once again calls on the union to turn to the member states, to ask them to make an effort to make the legislation in this area compatible. i agree with him, but when faced with a transnational problem, we need a response at the level of the union. the common judicial area measures were taken in each member state to set up specific units working in coordination, as the report recommends, this would not solve the problem of networks, because the work involved would remain confined to national borders. the traffickers of child pornography, often repeat offenders, are thus identified. it is a matter of prevention, of neutralizing their activities and dismantling their networks. the european union must have a suitable structure and a european instrument for information and action. this tool should not only be used to call on states to provide information but priority. mr kirkhope's report is full of very good intentions, but other proposals have to be made in the light of the present situation. i think that the commission and the council should take mr president, ladies and gentlemen, a great deal has been said about our colleague mr kirkhope's report, which contains many interesting elements, and i should like to add a few trivia to all these comments. but i will start by saying, first of all, that child pornography is essentially the result of two phenomena. the first is the explosion of pornography in general, and the second is, of course, the sexual exploitation of children. i'm talking about the explosion of pornography in general, because i don't think it's possible to completely isolate child pornography from the rest of pornography. in fact, there is a phenomenon of habituation - if i may say so - in the consumer, who, when he is in the presence of incitements to pornography on television, in the hotel chains - including here in strasbourg or brussels - in all the magazines, in front of the kiosks, is necessarily driven, one day or another, to seek, as with drugs, each time stronger sensations. this is what is happening, and this is why those who, for example, in france in 1987, thought they could, in the name of freedom, vigorously oppose the common sense measure that pornographic magazines should be removed from the kiosk and only be offered in the back of the store, bear responsibility for the measures they condemn today. i have just heard our colleague mr ainardi - a member of the left - complain, for example, that a number of files are being compiled and not used for police or law enforcement purposes, as they should be. i would simply remind our colleague that one of the very first judicial, judicial and police measures taken by the left-wing government in france was to order the destruction of the sex offenders' files. it is not surprising, then, that we have reached the point where we have made the sexual exploitation of children a matter of course. but is this not also the inevitable extension of a number of other measures that have been taken? mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are very relieved to have received the proposal for a council decision establishing a european refugee fund. after kosovo, chechnya and afghanistan, to name just a few of the tragedies that are bloodying our planet, the creation of such an agency is becoming more urgent. the report shows how much parliamentary activity can benefit europe. that is why we support these proposals. we shall emphasize only three points here. firstly, if there is one aspect of this report which is not satisfactory, it is the financial aspect. the amounts allocated to the fund are very small in view of the scale of its tasks - improving reception conditions, integrating persons with international protection, promoting voluntary return by helping with reintegration in the country of origin. these are huge tasks and require far more money than originally planned. we must give ourselves the means to achieve our common ambition, to make europe a land of solidarity and welcome, respectful of the dignity of the human person and of the values for which thousands of people seek asylum, in particular democratic freedoms of expression and peace. secondly, improving reception conditions should include access to care for all, children's schooling, and training. families who have already been uprooted by their exile must benefit from the schooling of their children and the training of young people in order to regain a certain stability, promote their social and economic integration and facilitate their eventual return. thirdly, many of us are calling for the ngos and associations that work with refugees on a daily basis to be consulted both in the definition of the necessary programmes and in their implementation. it would be a grave mistake to exclude from this process those who often fill in the gaps of the state with their invaluable experience. finally, i would like to stress once again the increasingly urgent need for the member states to reach a common asylum legislation quickly. only such progress will enable the european fund to achieve its full potential.
mr president, it seems legitimate for the european states to show solidarity in the event of an exceptional, massive, sudden influx of refugees caused by some external catastrophe. but what the commission is proposing today is quite different. the aim is to set up a permanent european fund, which will distribute funds to help member states manage the usual flow of refugees, real or fake. this proposal raises a number of questions. are the member states no longer able to manage the refugees they receive in normal times? how will their situation improve if they give money to brussels, so that brussels will pay it back to them immediately? will there be net contributors and net beneficiaries? if so, which ones? the answers are nowhere to be found in the reports that have been sent to us. it does not even contain any figures for the number of refugees currently in the various countries of europe. so once again we are faced with an important decision to be made blindly. this is all the more worrying as the proposed system itself risks accelerating the drift, since the relief of the immediate cost for each state may weaken its vigilance, ultimately increasing the overall burden for all. it's a perverse effect that insurance companies are well aware of. this risk is in turn all the greater because the proposed text defines very vaguely who is entitled to refugee status. of course, there is the refugee in the sense of the 1951 geneva convention - which is normal - but it is also seen that all kinds of displaced persons can be added, including those who are accepted, not because of international commitments, but only because of national legislation, decisions or practices. in these circumstances, the risk of a financial drift is extreme, mr president, and the report itself suggests this when it says that the appropriations provided - eur 36 million, anyway - are far below the potential demand. if we want to contain this risk, the europe of nations group believes that there is only one solution: to retain the financial responsibility of each member state for the reception of its refugees and to reserve european solidarity only for exceptional and dramatic circumstances.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i do not have time to philosophize for a minute. it is therefore important to thank the commission, to thank our rapporteur, mr staes, for finally giving meaning to the white paper which romano prodi had presented and which included a chapter on the food chain and animal feed. this first link in the chain begins with the animal and ends with the human. but we have the impression that the council does not see this. the council did not seem to see that after the dioxin crisis there have been cases of mad cow disease every day since the beginning of the year all over europe. the council does not see, therefore, what we have seen, namely that in order to comply with european legislation, structures are needed which monitor and intervene quickly in the event of a problem. in the context of the forthcoming establishment of the european health authority, it would therefore be desirable that real resources could be allocated to it to enable rapid detection and thus avoid any contagion. it would also be desirable for all the players in the feed chain to sign with the responsible health authorities genuine specifications which aim to reduce accidents as much as possible and accept the notions of thresholds, actions to eliminate from the circuit any raw material of additives or feed components in order to restore consumer confidence.

- mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commission representatives, ladies and gentlemen, the discharge procedure is a complex exercise. we must evaluate a budget two years after it has been implemented by the commission, taking into account both the budget being drawn up, the improvements needed in budget implementation and the achievement of the political objectives of the european union. to this in writing. - the proposal under discussion today aims to amend directive 95/53/ec in order to have a legal instrument better adapted to the needs of controls in the field of animal feed. following the dioxin crisis in may 1999, the adaptation of this legislation has become essential. the commission then announced a legislative programme to improve food safety regulation. the programme has been adopted by the council and the european parliament; it includes a review of directive 95/53/ec. several problems were identified at the time. thus, dysfunctions in crisis management, in particular poor coordination between the various authorities concerned, have emerged and have been identified in the context of a commission audit. information on dioxin contamination was provided to the commission late and the measures taken at national level were not sufficient. to overcome these shortcomings, the proposal provides for the possibility for experts from the commission and the member states to carry out checks not only in the community but also in third countries, in particular following the appearance of a phenomenon likely to have a negative influence on the safety of feedingstuffs put into circulation in the community; adopt a safeguard regime and give the commission the possibility, if necessary, to send community experts to verify compliance with community rules and to adopt appropriate measures; to entrust the commission with the adoption, in addition to the general programmes already provided for in directive 95/53/ec, of specific coordinated control programmes in the event of unexpected contamination which may constitute an imminent and serious danger to human and animal health. the common position did not reserve the right for the european commission to take safeguard measures adapted to the animal feed context in case of emergency. this is obviously very objectionable, even irresponsible! the rapporteur therefore proposes to reintroduce this provision, which i welcome, because without it the protection of consumers in situations of food crisis is not guaranteed.
in writing. - i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work on the proposal to amend directive 95/2/ec. this directive authorises the use of certain novel food additives which are currently prohibited but which have recently been assessed by the scientific committee on food (scf) and found fit for human consumption. the report reflects the concerns of consumers about the proliferation of additives, chemical substances in everyday food. the latter has been profoundly changed by changes in lifestyle and the introduction of new technologies. the time spent on preparing meals has been considerably reduced. this often leads us to eat prepared food, which is convenient but not really to our liking and especially not to our needs in terms of vitamins, salts, minerals... the food that ends up on our plates has often been heavily processed, resulting in a loss of taste, texture, and color. to counteract these drawbacks, food chemists add flavorings, flavor enhancers, preservatives, and dyes. and as food supply chains become longer and longer, the use of preservatives and antioxidants is becoming more and more essential. this is causing concern among consumers who, following the recent food crises, are increasingly keen to know what is on their plate! in response to these concerns, the european union has developed a particularly complex set of legislation designed to avoid any risk to consumers. thus, in order to justify the incorporation of an additive in a food, three criteria must be met, for which the margin of interpretation remains very wide: the technological need for the additive to be authorised. it is obviously determined by industry, which is thinking primarily in terms of reducing production costs and winning markets. this criterion currently weighs heavily in the balance. the concept of usefulness to the consumer is particularly vague. does the consumer really want to eat a fruit or vegetable that can stay in the refrigerator for a month without changing its appearance? finally, the safety. before a substance is authorised for use as a food additive, it is, in principle, subject to a toxicological assessment. normally, many tests on laboratory animals are carried out to determine whether this substance is harmless and at what dose it can be safely consumed. there are still gaps ! on the one hand, human beings do not always react like animals; the transposition of the results obtained from animals to humans is therefore still a problem. in addition, the effect of each substance taken in isolation is assessed in these experiments. yet, our diet often contains a cocktail of various substances, the effects of which are not always known! the precautionary principle must be applied as rigorously as possible in the case of foodstuffs! the commission proposal has not taken sufficient account of this! we therefore expect it to propose provisions which are more in the direction of better consumer protection, but also of the promotion of quality food!
in writing. - as i said in the previous part-session, during a debate on child sex tourism, there is nothing more horrifying and disgusting than the sexual exploitation of children. but we must admit that the internet facilitates these "practices" by allowing perverts of all kinds to anonymously consult illicit sites. this is a very alarming fact, and it is essential that we think about ways of combating this phenomenon in order to protect our children. i also welcome the work of the committee on civil liberties, which has produced some very interesting proposals. it suggests that in each member state of the european union, special police units should be responsible for monitoring the internet for pornographic material involving children. it is not enough to react to the violations already revealed if we want to act effectively against child pornography on the internet. the report also sets the age limit of 16 as the reference age for defining what is to be considered as child pornography. i also support the rapporteur when he insists that the council decision should be more binding and that the proposed measures should not be left to the discretion of the member states. in the same way, the concept of 'child pornography' must be understood in a broad sense! it is proposed to add that 'the production, sale and distribution or any other form of trafficking in child pornography and the possession of such material are punishable'. however, 'detention shall be punishable only if it is the result of an act committed knowingly or intentionally or is deliberately pursued'. otherwise, users who "surf" on the internet and inadvertently stumble upon a site containing child pornography could also be punished. the definition of a criminal offence is also extended to representations which, although not involving children, could or would lead to belief in such a person. the sanctions against users of child pornography must be exemplary. it is also very important to organise better cooperation between the police forces of the member states through europol. the european parliament must make bold proposals and be very vigilant. we must mobilize all the preventive, repressive and other means possible to combat these phenomena. this proposal is in that direction; that's why i can only support him.
in writing. - this initiative by the council is indispensable because childhood and naivety cannot be used for commercial purposes, which are degrading and which deny all human value. it is essential to be able to prevent these violations of the rights of the individual and of the child and not merely react. i share the view of our rapporteur and the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs that the council's proposal should be made more binding. the definition of child pornography offences must also be stricter, and i fully agree with the definition given by the parliamentary committee: 'the production, sale and distribution or any other form of trafficking in child pornography and the possession of this type of material is punishable'. however, "detention shall be punishable only if it is the result of an act committed knowingly or intentionally". we need the mobilization and vigilance of all citizens, not only of the police forces via europol, of the public authorities, but also of the internet users, of the economic producers of the network, in order to be able to identify the users of these electronic messages. the stakes are too high not to call for a general mobilization against this danger, and that is why i can only vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - the 21st century is the century of communications. paradoxically, it has become more common to contact friends or colleagues on the other side of the world than to talk to one's neighbors. in this vast internet market, some have found a way to make easy money amidst human misery. unethical producers and distributors have decided to satisfy the depraved desires of some by making child pornography available on the internet. no one is disturbed by the number of prostitutes in the streets near this building, or by their display in brussels windows, no one protests when tobacco shops sell, even on high shelves, magazines praising the worst deviations, including paedophiles. and yet, as if all this were unrelated, our assembly is shocked today by child pornography. here too, permissiveness has proved its harmfulness: while it satisfies the delusions of a few, it is the cause of misery for many others. it is therefore necessary that the police and judicial services of our respective states be given the means to combat a scourge that affects the weakest among us; the european union can help in this area, which is cross-border in nature. but if the fight is to be carried out on the level of international cooperation, it is also essential that it be carried out on a daily basis, by stopping the trivialization of all these practices. i will be told, as i am often told, that this has always existed and will always exist. what fatalism in that comment, what abandonment, what contempt for the human condition. i am glad that our institutions are now aware of this tragedy, which is being experienced by thousands of children around the world, including in our countries, and are deciding to remedy it. i am afraid, however, that the usual phenomenon of double standards will render these standards meaningless: what credibility could be given to policies which would limit the fight for human dignity to some and not others? in writing. - the creation of a european refugee fund, which the european parliament has just adopted despite the negative vote of the europe of nations group, provides a good example of these hypocritical proposals which will not solve anything on the ground, and which will only contribute to worsening the situation by transferring costly and uncontrolled competences to europe. as i said in my speech yesterday, this fund is not specifically designed to deal with rare, exceptional, dramatic situations of refugee inflows from countries in crisis. its purpose is to make day-to-day allocations for the management of the usual flow of refugees of all kinds heading for the more developed countries. but what will this fund bring in addition to the existing situation? as in the case of the structural funds, citizens will be led to believe that europe is handing them money that has fallen from the sky to help them manage refugees. in fact, this money does not fall from the sky: it is taken from these same citizens who do not know it. europe is thus earning a good reputation at little cost. the process is always the same: we choose a sad situation (in this case, the refugee situation) in order to appeal, not to rational reasoning, but to the compassion of people. it is explained that europe will provide a synergy to solve the problem at the lowest cost, and to prove this it is stated that the new fund will be a lightweight body to which only limited appropriations will be allocated. but over the coming years, it will become clear that the powers transferred to brussels are exercised in a lax manner, because they are too far removed from the citizens, that the fund has removed the responsibility of the states, that more money is therefore needed, that european controllers are also needed to monitor the use of the appropriations, and that a european administration is needed to manage what has become an uncontrollable monster. we have just witnessed firsthand the birth of a new european drift which will be very costly for all and will only result in the states being turned into recipients of aid, and with their own money.
in writing. - at the end of 1998, the commission proposed a community action programme to promote the integration of refugees into the union. following our opinion and the council's reactions, the commission has replaced this draft with a proposal to create a european refugee fund for an initial period of five years (2000-2004) and i must say that i am very pleased with it! by presenting a multiannual project with a wider scope of action, the commission is building on the treaty of amsterdam to carry out long-term actions in favour of refugees and displaced persons and to respond to the requests made by the tampere european council of october 1999 for the creation of a mechanism adapted to emergency situations. this is a marked improvement on the practice which has prevailed up to now. the fund establishes a system of financial redistribution to balance the burdens borne by member states in receiving refugees and to enable those member states whose reception systems are least developed to make up for the backlog. the fund should integrate the three aspects of european refugee policy into a single instrument: the reception, integration and repatriation of refugees and displaced persons. it will thus support actions in the member states such as the improvement of reception conditions and procedures in terms of infrastructure and services (accommodation, material assistance, social assistance, assistance in administrative procedures), the integration of persons enjoying a stable form of international protection, voluntary repatriation and reintegration in the country of origin. the target groups are refugees under the geneva convention and persons who have applied for refugee status, displaced persons who have applied for protection for a limited period of time. in addition to structural measures, the commission proposes to finance emergency measures in the event of a sudden and massive influx of refugees from the fund. the commission proposes an for revising the appropriations, since much higher amounts will be needed to achieve the objectives of the fund. i would like to conclude by stressing that the creation of this european refugee fund is a first step towards a common asylum system and that we must continue to work towards this!

mr president, to want partnership relations between the old continent and africa means first of all to stop the current system which has worked to the great benefit of the great powers and a few corrupt elites in the south. the african continent is ravaged by epidemics like aids, by visible and sometimes forgotten wars. land mines continue to kill innocent people, and weapons of all kinds are proliferating and ending up in the hands of child soldiers. the number of undernourished people in black africa rose from 90 million in 1970 to 180 million in 1995. these figures speak for themselves. between the famine that is again ravaging ethiopia and that of biafra thirty years ago, it seems that time has stood still. the vast majority of young people in africa are illiterate and unemployed. so today it would be an illusion to think that three quarters of the planet, of humanity, will continue to live in this misery without causing serious destabilization on a global scale. we must also put an end to the policy of assisting: it is like giving fish -
