mr president, the draft directive on the authorization procedures for genetically modified organisms is now back before this house for a second reading, whereas the events since the first reading have only reinforced the fears we had expressed then. on 11 february 1999, at first reading, we opposed this proposal, arguing that the risks posed by gmos to the environment, animal health and human health were not under control and that the mere application of the precautionary principle should lead, if not to a definitive ban on the spread of these organisms, at least to a moratorium of several years. we also criticised the project's authorisation procedures, which we considered both insufficiently rigorous and far too centralised. in the last year, however, studies have shown even more clearly the dangers of gm dissemination. just last week, a committee of inquiry of the french national assembly concluded, and i quote, 'that it considers it premature to put new products from genetically modified organisms on the market'. in these circumstances, the text which is being presented to us at second reading seems to us increasingly outdated. all our objections of principle are more relevant than ever, including the demand for a formal moratorium. and, as in the case of the mad cow, we want a country which is convinced of the serious danger to be given the right to take national measures of prohibition and safeguard. how is it that we are now forced to claim such an obvious right?
- mr president, ladies and gentlemen, genetically modified organisms and their spread are a matter of legitimate concern to european consumers. in the name of the sacred and holy profit, the industrial lobby continues to play the role of the sorcerer's apprentice, dangerously juggling food safety and consumer health. europe must legislate firmly to hold alchemists accountable, to ensure the quality of products and to provide citizens with clear information. we are in full agreement with the philosophy of this report. the emphasis should be on traceability through full information, including to third countries, importers or exporters of gmos. consumer safety requires equal treatment in order to avoid any diversion of traffic or export of products which cannot be sold on the european market. we must also require the prior consent of the receiving country before any trade. while the responsibility of the operator of a dissemination must be formally established, it should also be defined precisely, without haste, to avoid too general environmental liability. finally, the environmental risks must be assessed through an annual cost-benefit analysis of such gmo releases, an assessment which should be carried out in a transparent manner and extended to animal and plant health as well as to public and private property.
- mr president, the first to be surprised by our debate tonight must be the european consumers. they will be surprised to learn that so many years after the mad cow crisis began, the european union still does not have a reliable system for tracing beef. however, there was clearly an urgent need to restore consumer confidence by ensuring that the product could be traced from the barn to the table without any errors, so that any potential risk to human health could be eliminated early and effectively. the extraordinary slowness of the community's response has fortunately been offset by the relevant initiatives of the more enterprising member states. it is all the more regrettable that this possibility has been taken away from them by the treaty of amsterdam. i am thinking in particular of the compulsory labelling system developed in france with breeders and distributors and in force since 1996. this system has proved very effective. it has helped to restore consumer confidence. it was to safeguard this newfound confidence that france legitimately wished not to lift prematurely the embargo on british beef, which did not offer the same guarantees of traceability. she just forgot that she wasn't allowed to. it is a curious europe, indeed, that which penalizes those member states which take the necessary initiatives and make the necessary efforts to build consumer confidence and safeguard the health of their citizens! if we can only act legally at community level, at least let us move quickly and not indefinitely postpone the implementation of the commitments made in 1997 in order to make transparent and comprehensible information available to the consumer. the compulsory labelling of origin should therefore be introduced as soon as possible and certainly not postponed to 1 january 2003 as proposed by the commission. no derogation should be granted, as the commission is still proposing, for minced meat and cut meat, which would mean that 30% to 50% of beef and veal would be exempt from the labelling requirement, depending on the country. nor should we accept, as the commission always proposes, that we should stick to a generic name of the ec type which is too general. consumers want to be sure of the ability of operators to control the origin of meat. the member states should therefore be mentioned. as for beef imported from third countries, it must be subject to the same labelling rules as community meat and if it does not comply with the european union's rules on traceability, this must of course be clearly stated. that is the meaning, mr president, of the amendments which i tabled with mrs thomas-moreau, on behalf of the uen group, and which we propose to all our colleagues who are concerned to contribute to the establishment of genuine traceability of beef.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, fourteen years after the appearance of bse we are finally dealing with the labelling of meat to protect consumers and ensure traceability. it is a protection which is late in coming in principle but mostly illusory in practice. firstly, in the draft regulation, 50% of european minced meat is not required to be labelled. for the remaining 50% there is no labelling requirement until 2003, which means we have three years to dispose of the uk surpluses. and after 2003, the indication of origin may be limited to the mere mention of 'ec origin', without any indication of country. in fact, to drown out the prion even more, the label is overloaded with the following: place of birth, fattening, slaughter, boning, with the state of origin, the region of origin, the holding of origin; that's twelve mentions, plus the price, plus the weight, that's fourteen mentions. it's not readable. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the labelling is lighter, the mandatory national labelling of france, belgium and finland is maintained. that's good. that's good. we'll vote on the amendments. but everyone can see, if you will forgive me, commissioner, the commission's ill will. the labelling solution is a false good idea. the label does not protect gmos, or chocolate with vegetable fat or tomorrow with gm fat, or american hormone meats later, or prion meat. the only effective protection would be control, which requires states and borders. but we have removed the frontiers and that is the price of europe. we have freedom of movement at the cost of insecurity, and i hope that tomorrow, ladies and gentlemen, no one will be punished. before you got beaten up by a beef nerve, now you could get punished by a british steak.
mr president, this debate on beef labelling is in line with our previous concerns about food safety. the report and its conclusions, if adopted, will raise a number of consumer concerns in such a sensitive area where mad cow syndrome still prevails. for the edd group, product traceability is a guarantee, both for the protection of consumers' health and for the promotion of quality products that all its producers, large and small, know how to generate, by giving priority to quality over low-level commercial and financial interests that do not take into account human health. in this report we consider it very important and essential that all products in the sector be covered by these labelling obligations, from raw meat from slaughterhouses to derived products, minced meat, cut meat and other products. it is also essential to provide the consumer with complete information, indicating on the label all the details concerning the life and slaughter of the animal: place of birth, rearing and slaughter, feeding and fattening techniques, and any antibiotics and growth promoters administered. finally, it is important that these provisions be put in place as soon as possible, because there are good consumer rights at stake. we must act quickly, especially since this is not a new case. so it's time to act. consumer confidence is not something that can be decreed, it must be created. for this reason, as i said in our debate on 5 october 1999, the cpnt members of the edd group will support any measure aimed at full traceability, which can only benefit everyone: the consumer, because he will know, the good producer, because he will protect himself.
- mr president, commissioner, the beef sector has entered into a contract with the public. the contract is based on the transparency demanded by the consumer, and i would even say demanded by the citizen. this transparency is now applied in the beef and veal sector in two areas which are different but inseparable: bse and labelling. france is strengthening its precautionary measures for specified risk materials and is setting up a large-scale protocol to evaluate bse testing in bovine animals. tomorrow the european union is going to define a test programme for all the member countries. in this context, consumers would not understand that labelling can be delayed. i am therefore very keen to ensure that operators in this sector do not find themselves in a legal vacuum which would lead public opinion to ask the legitimate question of whether greater transparency is really desirable. how can we explain that we have reached agreement on chocolate at european union level, while in a sensitive and important area such as beef we are not able to meet the deadlines we have set ourselves? let's not get the debate wrong. i am convinced that the issue of beef labelling is not a mere technical issue. i would like to remind you that if labelling is so important to consumers, it is because they see it as a guarantee of increased product traceability, of the responsibility of all the professionals in the sector and of the european and national public authorities, and also of the improvement of control systems. finally, it is a right to information that our fellow citizens demand. this right to information is the natural counterpart to the development of trade and the proper exercise of competition. the transparency of labelling makes it possible to improve the free movement of beef by reassuring consumers and guaranteeing them the freedom to make informed choices. in the beef sector, the improvement of consumer information through labelling is a strong signal for europe to its trading partners: it demonstrates its willingness, beyond the safety of the products, to preserve the consumer's free choice.

in writing. - the vote on the second reading of the amendments to the draft directive on the authorisation procedures for genetically modified organisms (gmos), as it has just taken place, appears extremely disappointing. we certainly knew from the first reading that the principle of a ban on gmos, or at least a moratorium to allow for more in-depth studies, was rejected. but we could at least have expected parliament to decide now to put in place serious consumer protection. but it didn't. the european parliament has just abdicated on three key points, under conditions which i consider shameful: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment-related aspects of the environment. in their place, an amendment was voted which simply asks that 'special attention be paid to this problem in order to identify and phase out by 2005 antibiotic resistance markers contained in gmos, which may have negative effects on human health and the environment'; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the risk of involuntary gene transfers to other organisms: amendment no 12, which called for measures to prevent such involuntary transfers, was not adopted. in its place, a much more vague amendment no 38 was voted, which simply asks that we try to assess the various forms of risk that these transfers may entail; on the liability and insurance of persons carrying out voluntary releases of gmos: to our great indignation, amendment no 33 was rejected, which called for those legally responsible for these gmo releases to bear full responsibility for any damage to human health or the environment, and required them to take out sufficient insurance to compensate for any damage. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. unfortunately, we already know from the white paper that the commission has prepared on the subject that it is not in favour of compulsory insurance in this area. we are particularly disgusted by the rejection of amendment no 33, because if we are to allow products containing gmos to be placed on the market, at least those who sell them should accept their responsibilities. the biotechnology industry lobbyists tell us that there is no risk and that the obligation to insure is impossible because the risk is uninsurable. i should know. because i've never seen an insurance company refuse to cover a non-existent risk. one of the obscure aspects of this case is that the french government, which, according to the latest news, includes environmentalists, had officially expressed a reserved opinion on this amendment. once again the biotechnology industry lobby groups have done their job well at all levels, away from the public eye.
in writing. - i would like to warmly congratulate mr bowe on his report on the deliberate release of gmos into the environment. this topic, which is the subject of much debate, is topical, since yesterday two european regulations came into force which require manufacturers to label 'food and food ingredients' containing more than 1% of gmos and 'genetically modified additives and flavourings' without specifying a threshold. as a consumer, i am very pleased with this mandatory labelling which will allow us to make informed choices even though i would have liked stricter rules requiring a very clear indication on the top of the packaging! this first step is positive, however, as it has led several large companies to abandon the introduction of gmos in their products. turning to the subject of interest today, it is a proposal for a revision of directive 90/220/eec which covers both the deliberate release of gmos for experimental purposes and the deliberate release for placing products on the market. in view of the progress of scientific research in this field, it appeared necessary to clarify the scope of this legislation in order to protect consumer health and the environment. the proposals from the committee on the environment establish a strict and transparent framework which is perfectly responsive to consumer concerns. the three main amendments i support are aimed at: - preventing any accidental contamination of fields by cross-pollination of gm and non-gm crops. to this end, it is necessary to either impose the observance of minimum distances between fields where gmos are grown and fields reserved for traditional crops, or the obligation to confine gmos crops to special greenhouses depending on the risk of genetic pollution they entail; the dissemination of all gmos containing a marker gene for antibiotic resistance should therefore be prohibited; - strict liability for producers should be imposed. like the rapporteur, i remain convinced that the person legally responsible for the release of gmos into the environment must bear full civil liability for any damage to human health or the environment. this principle of responsibility, combined with the principle of traceability of gmos and, above all, the precautionary principle, will make it possible to limit the risks as much as possible! the uncertainties which remain in this area require the utmost caution! i will end by repeating and insisting that we must listen to the expectations of the european citizens! our public opinion has repeatedly shown its reluctance to see the frankenbouff develop and its attachment to healthy and natural food. we must therefore be the spokesmen for this desire to preserve quality food in the european union!
in writing. - as an introduction, i would like to recall that the objective of food labelling, according to directive 79/112, is clearly stated: 'the primary concern in any rule relating to food labelling should be to inform and protect the consumer'. consumers need to be confident in what they eat. in this case, it is not just a question of changing our taste and traditions in chocolate, but of dealing properly with the consequences of mad cow disease. it is astonishing, given the seriousness of the issues at stake, that an effective traceability system is still not in place today, so many years after the crisis. we will not repeat the debate of december 1999, but the commission was well advised to monitor the application of this regulation scrupulously and, once again, made a serious political error. let us return to the beef embargo for a moment. the french government, once again, has put reason and prudence before the ideology of the single market. when you know what his options are in european affairs, you can see what it must have cost him. the reason for france's choice is that the community institutions are still not in a position to ensure the real traceability of food products. our consumer information and protection system is totally flawed: for example, it is impossible for a citizen of the union to know whether british beef is in the composition of ravioli imported from another member state. should our public opinion have confidence in a commission which does not ensure compulsory traceability of beef, but lifts an embargo? i did not accept that the commission should teach france lessons, which knows that the impact of the voluntary regulation it has adopted has effectively helped to restore consumer confidence. we have defended this point of view by tabling amendments in the committees on the environment, public health and consumer policy and agriculture and rural development. we are pleased to note that some of our amendments in the committee on agriculture and the environment have been adopted. the committee on the environment has amended the commission's proposal on some essential points. it is high time to establish a system of trust and transparency. we supported a fast and rigorous application of traceability in this vote to ensure flawless traceability and clear and transparent information and are satisfied with the results. we hope that today's vote will not lead to any further scandalous requests for extensions or derogations in a few months' time.
in writing. - the lisbon summit was to be the social europe summit. in fact, it is a new neoliberal wave that has swept through lisbon to put the eu on the front line in the global economic war. far from social and democratic rights, and a little closer to the social model of the united states, the summit once again praised the law of profit, the flexibility of the workforce, all-round competition with new privatisations and liberalisations. in short, everything should be listed on the stock exchange. and this with the complicity of all the leftwing governments present in lisbon. to make us swallow the pill, the eu promises almost universal access to the internet and advanced vocational training. to top it all off, full employment in 2010 - that is, the creation of 20 to 30 million new jobs - is right under our noses. these fine promises mean only one thing: the massive development of precarious employment, small jobs and low wages, with the continued threat of dismissal, and, as a bonus, a project to overhaul the unequal social protection system. the bosses, on the other hand, are once again receiving unfair subsidies. new economy, but it's the good old recipes that we're left with.
in writing. - the solemn declaration of the first africa-europe summit in cairo begins by referring to the 'links which have existed between africa and europe for centuries' and which have 'developed on the basis of common values such as the strengthening of democracy'. given that this centuries-old past is one of slavery, massacres, forced labour, plunder, conquest and colonial oppression, through which the rich countries of europe have drained this continent of its blood, one wonders which is more ignoble: the morgue of the representatives of the imperialist countries or the baseness of the local heads of state who have agreed to co-sign such a declaration, claiming to do so on behalf of their peoples. our solidarity goes to the peoples of africa who have paid a heavy price to our ruling classes and it is not enough to cancel a debt that has already been largely repaid. a genuine cooperation with africa could only begin by giving back to the people of this continent what was stolen from them during a century of colonization and what is still being stolen from them today. a genuine cooperation on an equal footing could only be established between a europe and an africa which would no longer be under the control of these industrial and banking groups which derive their wealth from the exploitation of the working classes of both continents. in these circumstances, we voted against the joint resolution welcoming the cairo summit, but we voted in favour of the only amendment which contains concrete proposals.
in writing. - this cairo summit is the first meeting on the scale of the entire african continent. yet the eu still wants to divide africa into the mediterranean and black africa. in this period of neocolonial transition, the eu is seeking to impose a neoliberal model of relations dominated by liberalization and structural adjustments. the famous partnership of equality has, in reality, no other objectives than to remind africans that they are debtors to international law and that they must submit to the tools of the neoliberal panoply. the various conflicts in africa have been discussed, but they have not found support because of the rivalries of the great western powers who divide or contest the zones of influence. as for the aids issue, while its urgency is acknowledged, and in addition to a moralising approach, the fine speeches do not make us forget the cold reality of the figures that show a decrease in eu development aid to africa, as central and eastern europe has become a priority. the few promises of debt cancellation that africans have managed to wrest from a few eu countries do not prevent the eu from continuing to oppose the overall question of cancellation of the debt of the third world countries, which starves the peoples every day. with the africa-europe civil society forum, which brought together more than 80 ngos in march, we declare our opposition to structural adjustment programmes and continue to support the debt cancellation campaigns.

- madam president, behind the letter of this report i would like to point out a few figures. the first number is 700. limiting the number of meps to 700 would not be a cause for concern if it did not undermine the representativeness of our parliament. by marginalizing small countries, while allowing the establishment of high electoral thresholds in the larger ones, entire sections of european society will no longer be able to be represented in this house because of a sordid electoral mechanism. we must reaffirm the paramount and absolute vocation of our parliament to represent the people, and the peoples of europe in all their diversity. second digit: two thirds. two thirds of the votes are the majority needed for our parliament to censure the commission. this high threshold of two thirds is a sad and unique case. what european government can boast of being thus, with impunity, free from real parliamentary control? we must establish a symmetry of form. if a simple majority is sufficient to give the commission the mandate, then the same majority must be able to withdraw the commission's confidence. what the popular representation has done, it has the power to undo. it's the rule everywhere, it should be the rule here. third and last digit: 2009. the report suggests the date of 2009 for the election of meps on transnational lists. so, ladies and gentlemen, there are two possibilities: either our parliament considers this measure to be wrong and therefore it must be abandoned - even in 2009 - or it recognizes, as the greens do, that such lists are indispensable for creating genuine families of thought in europe, and so it allows this important political debate to take place as soon as the 2004 elections. otherwise we would lack both lucidity and ambition. the report also lacks clarity and ambition, and while it is not bad, it does not live up to the challenges. by changing its size, the european union will change its nature. so our continent must re-write its rules, not simply clean them up. this timid igc 2000 cannot be an end in itself, but the first step towards a constitution.

- mr president, the ageing of the population and the decline in the number of people with a job, although real, are being put forward by the commission and other members to pave the way for pension funds for supplementary pensions. the momentum of growth and job creation is being drained. with the capitalisation mechanisms, it is the adaptation of pensions to the single market and the introduction of the euro. this approach risks a system based on private insurance, which would gradually replace social security. health and pensions would no longer be rights but would become commodities subject to the laws of the market. the strategy for pension funds is essentially to channel savings into the financial markets. such a system is very dangerous and deeply unfair, because it favors the richest, those who can save, and leaves the poorest with a miserable retirement. mr kuckelkorn's original report considered retirement first as a social insurance against certain vital risks, before being a process of capital formation. but the adoption of the amendments which unreservedly support the capitalisation mechanisms have profoundly changed it. that is why i cannot support this report, which makes the commission's approach more difficult. we believe, on the contrary, that a high level of social protection must be maintained, based on solidarity independent of financial profitability. the system of distribution guarantees the rights of employees, ensures their retirement, in the framework of national solidarity, solidarity between workers and pensioners, between generations, between men and women, between the public and private sectors. new resources and a revalorization of the purchasing power of pensions are to be found in contributions which could be levied on financial products at the same level as those levied on wages. employer contributions should be linked to the employment policy of companies and a tax introduced for firms that lay off employees.
mr president, this report seeks to harmonize supplementary pensions in europe. in fact, it aims, nothing more or less, to open up all european pension systems to finance. it advocates the development of a genuine single market for pension funds, arguing that the use of capitalisation is inevitable. it should be noted that when it comes to the financial interests of the most powerful, the principle of subsidiarity is not hesitated to be forgotten in order to propose a single model. the report makes cynical arguments and wants to give credence to the idea that capitalisation alone would better protect modest incomes. in reality, the aim is not to supplement public pension schemes but, on the contrary, to gradually empty them of their substance. the employees know that retirement is a right, though. they fought for it. this right is built on intergenerational solidarity. that is why they do not want to invest their pensions in the stock market under any circumstances. in several countries powerful social movements have already opposed such attempts. their threats have prevented, for example, the french government from introducing pension funds. it is in full agreement with these past, present and future struggles, and it is in support of them that we will vote against a report which relegates this parliament to the rank of a lobby of high finance. retirees need a pension that is adequate, stable, and protected. no pension fund, no stock exchange, can ever guarantee that. on this question, as on many others, we must choose between increasing profits for a few or satisfying the needs of all.
- mr president, we are voting against this report which is a plea for funded pension schemes. this system forces employees who want to secure a pension to live on to put their money at the disposal of investment funds, trusts, insurance companies, or other private financial groups. at the same time, it makes the amount of pensions dependent on the financial markets, i.e. on speculation. in addition, all those whose wages are too low to pay their taxes to pension funds will be entitled to a poverty pension. to use demographic change to justify this is a fraud. productivity has increased tenfold over the past half century, and if its fruits were not turned exclusively into private profit by the owners and shareholders of companies, this productivity should raise wages and ensure adequate pensions for all. if the distribution of pensions is having difficulties, it is not because there are fewer assets for the number of pensioners, but because there are too many unemployed and low wages. so if the pension funds were to run a deficit, it would be up to the states to take over by taking the necessary sums from the profits of industrial and financial groups.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the reform of the banana cmo proposed by the commission, which aims to replace the present system by the application of the 'tariff only' system, would, if implemented in this way, lead to the disappearance of acp producers in the short term and of community producers in the medium term. at the seattle summit and then at davos, the european citizens were able to see the inability of the wto to reconcile financial priorities with the major interests of the citizens, such as the living environment, working conditions and the quality of consumption, and they would not understand today that their members of parliament are not only calling these values into question but, moreover, are reneging on the commitment made by the union to its acp partners. the banana issue is a perfect example of the difficulties the union is having in establishing the european model, which is so often mentioned by the institutions. in this respect, the 1993 cmo has four main objectives: to ensure the free movement of bananas within the common market while maintaining reasonable prices for consumers, to respect the union's commitments to the acp countries, to maintain community preference for union producers such as martinique, guadeloupe, the canary islands, madeira and crete, and finally to respect gatt obligations. the regulation was contested from the outset and eventually led to several wto condemnations, the last of which was in april 1999. the united states, which was always ready to be the first to take the lead, immediately adopted trade retaliatory measures against the countries of the union. in order to comply with the wto, the commission is proposing to move to a 'tariff only' formula, i.e. to abolish quotas and introduce a single customs tariff, the level of which we do not know. we know that this system is already being challenged by a majority of operators and producers, from all geographical origins. we are right to question the validity of the approach which consists in changing the rules of the game, in the process, by forcing producers to question their operating plans and their market prospects and leads us to define the terms of a reform which is in accordance with the rules of international trade, but not solely dictated by it. the stakes are high. since 1993, the situation of community producers has been steadily deteriorating. the same is true for many traditional acp suppliers. it is impossible for these producers to compete fairly with the major producers and operators in the sector at international level. moreover, it should be noted that more than 60% of the bananas consumed in the union come from non-acp third countries. it is not a question of practicing protectionism, but rather of protecting the sustainability of a certain way of producing. the banana is being defended as a whole production chain, often a whole region, and its life force. the margin of manoeuvre is narrow from a technical point of view, but the choice of a reform model is political. you have to know what goals you're looking for. in my view, the main thing is to defend the european model at international level. this is the position adopted unanimously by the members of the committee on agriculture. i would like to thank my colleagues for their effective cooperation on this matter and mr westendorp and mr fernández martin for their excellent work. in the absence of objective reasons for opting for 'tariff only', i propose that the european commission's proposal retains its first 'transitional' option and implements it without automatically switching to 'tariff only', but by providing for an evaluation of the functioning of the reformed com after a period of ten years. the acp-eu development partnership agreement, which replaces the lomé convention, provides for a ten-year transition period for the acp countries to enable them to comply as closely as possible with wto standards. why should it be any different with bananas? i also propose to ensure that the level of quotas does not increase the already existing situation of over-supply on the market, and i finally propose, given that the third quota will now be open to all, to increase the preferential access duty for acp products to a minimum of eur 300. in any event, accompanying measures are essential to ensure the sustainability and viability of community and acp production. i would suggest a few: regionalisation of aid to correct the differences between the various community production areas, the introduction of a system of compensation for cyclones, marketing aid to restore balance to the dollar banana distribution chains, special support measures for organic production and, finally, accelerated aid. i hope that parliament will follow the line proposed by the committee on agriculture, but we also need the understanding of the council and the commission. we - mr president, today the trial of 13 iranian jews accused of espionage opened in tehran. the trial is closed. these people have been imprisoned for several months, in conditions that are almost unknown. it was only the day before yesterday that the lawyers, some of whom are hired, were able to take note of the file. there is no guarantee of the rights of the defence. so i'm afraid this is just a mock trial. yet the seriousness of the charge can lead to a death sentence. when the case began, we could hear some high-ranking regime officials publicly calling for them to be killed immediately. this case, which was fabricated - and i think we are all convinced of this - has greatly mobilized international public opinion. with strong mobilizations all over the world, including today in strasbourg, international pressure has had an effect as iranian leaders have changed their position, stating in particular that most of the accused will no longer appear on the charge of espionage, which is equivalent to death. three have been released on bail; finally, the court announced this morning that the trial was postponed to may 1st, which is already a first step. however, some of them still face the death penalty and others heavy sentences. the various changes in the attitude of the authorities illustrate its embarrassment. until the last moment, he was unable to clearly define the charges. it is also clear that the outcome of this trial will depend in part on the evolution of the iranian political situation. the last parliamentary elections in february saw the reformist movement win over the conservative movement, which includes the most extreme elements. the trial therefore begins at a particular moment: on the one hand, iran is showing signs of openness and progress, on the other, the conservatives are trying to hold on to power using all the means at their disposal. the case of the 13 jews in iran is therefore likely to be used by one faction against another, as their internal conflicts continue. in this kind of battle, justice has little place, human rights even less. so we must act. the european union is based on the values laid down in the 1948 universal declaration of human rights; will increase with future enlargements. the european union remained traumatised by its impotence in the face of the violent process of disintegration taking place in the balkans. it has been unable to crisis effectively at international level. the balkan crisis can be said to have set off a decisive trend in european defence and security policy. the decisions of the european councils in cologne and helsinki on the establishment of the military and civilian resources needed for the union to be able to manage crises with complete autonomy are proof of this. the cologne council led to the establishment of the stability pact for south-eastern europe on 10 june 1999, in which the member states of the european union and the states of the region, of course, but also the united states and russia, participate. this pact is part of the overall stabilisation approach which has been developed since 1996 by the european union. the key to this approach are the association and stabilisation agreements to be signed by bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, the federal republic of yugoslavia, the yugoslav republic of macedonia and albania. at the moment, negotiations are under way with macedonia. croatia, which has recently experienced positive political changes, should be involved in the near future. these agreements constitute an entirely new contractual framework for the countries of the region; they are strongly inspired by the institutional arrangements and conditionality of the europe agreements linking the european union to the ceecs. these agreements are tailor-made and differentiated to take account of the specific situation of each country concerned. they offer a long-term prospect of membership of the european structures, on the basis of the amsterdam treaty and when the criteria defined in copenhagen are met. this is above all an important political signal and a decisive stimulus for the countries of this region in crisis. moreover, these agreements encourage stronger regional cooperation, which i believe is essential to the creation of a pole of stability in the region.

the report also calls for the introduction of a european standardisation system for the management of the euro, which would be based on the principle of 'one currency, two currencies'. these findings do not seem to shake the confidence of our assembly in the model of community construction chosen: it will make the peoples happy, even if they do not want it.

schools helps to maintain the consumption of milk products, and these same milk products are necessary for the healthy nutrition of children, a condition for growth free of deficiencies. the choice of subsidized milk is one of teaching children balanced eating habits at an age when eating behaviour and taste education are shaped for a lifetime. this function has particular resonance in the age of eating disorders and junk food. for example, in europe, the increase in the number of obese children resulting from the culture of soda and multicolored sugary drinks is alarming. needless to say, commission. - mr president, i thank mr lannoye for this initiative and for initiating the debate in this chamber on what i consider to be a very important subject. one of the objectives of the commission communication 'air transport and the environment - towards sustainable development' is precisely to launch the debate on the desirability of establishing a community framework for decision-making procedures concerning operating restrictions to be imposed on airports in the union on environmental grounds. in the ensuing debate in the various institutions, the council of ministers and parliament will have the opportunity to comment on this communication in general and on specific aspects such as night flights. as the commission has pointed out in this communication, it is difficult for it to see how uniform and binding rules on operating restrictions, which would apply to all community airports, such as the general ban on night flights, could provide the most balanced solution to the problem of noise pollution at certain airports. the commission is of the opinion that decisions should continue to be taken at local level. however, it also believes that a common framework for the procedures leading to such decisions is needed, so that when a region decides to ban night flying, for example, it does so in the same way as a similar region a little further away. and this framework could include mandatory consultation of all interested parties, sufficient time to adapt to new restrictions and a common basis for assessing the environmental effectiveness of the proposed restrictions. i would also like to say a word about the hushkits. as regards the issue of the accelerated withdrawal of the noisiest aircraft, the commission remains committed to the work under way in the international civil aviation organisation on the development of a new noise standard and withdrawal rules for the noisiest aircraft. if all goes well, and we hope so, this work will lead to the adoption in september 2001 by the 33rd icao assembly of new binding international noise rules. compared to the hushkits regulation, which merely freezes the current situation with regard to aircraft whose certificate has been renewed, real international rules aimed at phasing out these aircraft would produce better results in terms of environmental protection. in the meantime, in view of the refusal of the united states to refrain from taking action against the hushkits regulation, the provisions of the latter regulation on non-addition will enter into force on 4 may. since the provisions on the prohibition of the use of aircraft registered in third countries will not enter into force until 1 april 2002, the commission's evaluation of the conclusions of the 33rd assembly of the international civil aviation organisation will provide the necessary elements to assess at that time whether the hushkits regulation should be replaced by internationally agreed phasing-out rules. all this is in motion, the commission is working on it and thanks parliament for its understanding and cooperation in this area.

the council of the european union have repeatedly stressed that the treaty does not provide for any specific competence for a forestry policy of the union. the union does not therefore have the necessary instruments to intervene in the sense of the two resolutions. wood is not one of the products listed in annex 1 to the treaty, there is no legal framework and therefore wood cannot be the subject of a specific market policy, even temporarily. even if such interventions are theoretically possible under wto rules, they require a well-founded and reasoned legal, economic and commercial justification to convince our trading partners to accept them. so far, the commission has not received a detailed analysis that would justify such a move. i'll come back to that a little later. firstly, national aid to the wood sector is therefore the most appropriate means, at national, regional or local level, of supporting the farms most affected by the sector and the member states must lay down the detailed rules for such aid. the commission is therefore examining national aid schemes to mitigate the consequences of hurricanes on the forestry economy, which are submitted to it by the governments of the member states, in the light of the effects on competition at european level. the commission services examine these aid schemes, in particular in the light of article 87 (2) (b) of the treaty, which concerns the compatibility of aid provided by member states in the event of natural disasters. the aid notified by the french government contains a general measure to promote the transport of plywood, which may result in some of it being transported to countries outside the union. the commission services, including the legal services, stress that article 87 (2) (b) does not in itself constitute a derogation from the gatt rules and are examining the compatibility of this measure with the treaty on the basis of information recently received. further information could be requested from the french authorities. as regards the co-financing of aid proposed by the member states under article 30 of regulation (ec) no 1257/99 on support for rural development by the european agricultural guidance and guarantee fund, i would stress once again that the commission is prepared to show maximum flexibility. but it is first up to the member states to make changes to their initial programmes. in the meantime, two member states, including france, have submitted adapted programmes which now include an important element of support for the forestry economy following the storms of late 1999. in this context, measures concerning the removal, storage, transport, protection and restoration of destroyed forests are proposed to support the sector. these are currently the subject of negotiations between the commission and the member states, but it can now be said that the commission has a favourable position on them.

in writing. - i don't need to remind you how hard the battle was to maintain the funds needed to distribute milk to schools. in april 1999, the preliminary draft budget presented by the european commission envisaged cutting the budget line in question by half! this reduction presaged the eventual disappearance of these aids. this has not failed to provoke strong reactions inside and outside the european parliament. experts and nutritionists agree that milk is essential for the proper intellectual and physical development of all children. children from disadvantaged families, who lack access to certain dairy products with essential nutritional content, can fill these gaps through meals offered in school canteens. it was our children's health that was at stake in such a proposal. this was unacceptable when public health was enshrined in the new title xiii of the treaty of amsterdam. it was, moreover, in total contradiction with the conclusions of the agriculture council of 14 and 15 june 1999. our ministers had stressed the importance of encouraging the consumption of milk because of its high nutritional value, especially for children and young people. it was only after long and bitter discussions that the european commission proposed to increase the budget line by €31 million, bringing the total amount committed for aid for milk distribution in schools to €84 million. this is the situation in the year 2000. for the future, the european commission has proposed to set up a co-financing system. the distribution subsidies would be financed by the european union to the tune of 50%, with the other half being borne by the states. that is not an acceptable proposal ! it was clear that the commission's ultimate aim was to dismantle the scheme for aid to the distribution of milk in schools! the proposal of our european parliament, which i wholeheartedly support, is to make the community pay 95% of the cost of european subsidies for milk distributed in schools! it is the only guarantee that this system will last. i also support the decision to include drinking yoghurt and milk drinks in the regulation. this is necessary to take account of changes in dietary habits and preferences and to make the programme more attractive to consumers. today i can say that i am pleased to have been involved in this fight and to see that the many letters to the ministers concerned, the questions to the european commission and the press releases have borne fruit!
in writing. - the question of community subsidies for the distribution of milk in schools dates back to 1997 and is of growing interest in each of our member states, especially as it concerns issues of public health and the economy, which are therefore close to european citizens. to see this, one only has to read the many letters we received when it became clear that the european commission wanted to stop this programme! i can therefore only urge you to follow the advice of our rapporteur who not only wants to continue such a programme but also opposes the european commission's proposal for a 50/50 co-financing. such a brutal co-financing would risk causing some member states to abandon the financing of their national share and would thus lead to discrimination within the union. while i do not deny the need to improve the management of this budget line, i do believe that improvement of the system can and should be done smoothly, and i therefore urge you to support the european parliament's committee on agriculture and rural development and its rapporteur in adopting this report.

- mr president, it is clear from this annual report that europe is not giving itself the means to pursue its policy on transeuropean transport networks. but beyond simple budgetary and financial considerations, more generally, it is the commission's general guidelines in this area that are to be criticized. of course, we subscribe to the principle that the people of europe need to have transeuropean networks, both for the mobility of people and goods, for economic and social cohesion and for rail alternatives to the whole motorway. we cannot, however, accept either the method imposed or the solutions proposed. are all 14 projects selected relevant or prioritized in relation to the needs of the population? have they been associated or concerted or, as the report suggests, do the transeuropean networks respond to the logic of the free market alone? it is not by chance that, of the 14 projects, the seven whose timetable and financing are still uncertain are precisely those which do not meet the requirements of profitability alone. but the most negative point seems to us to be the financing. it is assumed that public funds cannot increase, which is questionable. it therefore proposes to use private funds in the form of partnerships, which is an essential element of the project. this approach to rail transport challenges the public service. it is obvious that private operators, if they are involved in the financing, will seek maximum profitability. private companies must be made to contribute because they use infrastructure for their own benefit, but in the form of a tax levy, not by taking part in the capital of railway companies. we must develop the concept of a european public railway service, and we reject privatisation and the opening up of public enterprises' capital, including for new projects. europe is once again responding to the real need of the people to have a high-quality and efficient european rail network for users and staff by racing for profit.
mr president, we are in favour of the development of a transeuropean transport network which gives priority to rail transport over road transport. however, the development of the transeuropean main lines must not be at the expense of suburban transport or the so-called secondary lines. but rail transport, both large and small, should be a public service designed to meet the needs of the public, not to generate private profit. the participation of private capital necessarily means the pursuit of profitability, to the detriment of both users and workers in this sector. too many recent disasters, notably the paddington railway station in britain, illustrate the incompatibility between the search for profitability and safety. however, as the explanatory memorandum to the report points out, public investment is steadily declining and has fallen from 1.5% of the european union's gnp to 0.9% in less than 20 years. this leads to a deterioration of public rail transport and a reduction in the number of employees, which contributes to increasing unemployment. if the european union states do not change their policy, that is, if they do not give priority to investments in public services over subsidies to the big business, any decision on a genuine public transport service operating under the best safety conditions at european level will be a matter of wishful thinking.

mr president, the resolution before parliament on air transport presents serious dangers which i wish to stress. the proposal is essentially to transfer the responsibility for traffic control to the european level, to privatise the operational control services and even to introduce competition between these services. air traffic has doubled since 1986. it will double again by 2015. the resolution complete disregard of the transport needs of the european population. european airlines are competing on the same routes, each of them is setting up global alliances separately, with the sole concern of immediate financial profitability, multiplying the number of small carriers, competing at the same times. the european union, instead of promoting an overall plan for the development of transport, according to an intermodal logic between rail and air, has pushed for privatisation and deregulation. the result is a saturation of traffic and nuisances, and at the same time a deterioration in the working conditions and status of air transport employees, with airlines branching out as much as possible to lower social costs. the resolution yields to the dictates of the big companies, which now true that one of the characteristics of european liberalisation, as compared with american liberalisation, is that state aid has been allowed to support the restructuring of certain airlines. it is mr president, i would like to thank the committee for its appreciation of the dangers of counterfeiting and piracy. the green paper initiative shows that it is willing to tackle the problem and i also of consumers. the market is full of counterfeit spare parts for cars and aircraft, toys and pharmaceuticals, which pose a mortal danger to the consumer. piracy also represents a danger to innovation and the very future of certain companies, and i will cite as an example the approximately one hundred thousand jobs that are lost every year in the european union as a result. counterfeiters profit from legitimate industry's investments in research and development of new products and in advertising. in addition, it also takes away from the tax resources of the public authorities. finally, it has been established that this phenomenon is often closely linked to organized crime. the report calls for a comprehensive and coordinated approach to combating piracy and counterfeiting, and this approach has two aspects: prevention and repression. to prevent this scourge, we must know it. that is why we are proposing a broad public awareness campaign, with programmes that the commission may propose to us, and awareness-raising among the police, judicial and customs authorities. for these authorities, training is envisaged, as well as a programme of consultation, involving the exchange of know-how and the adoption of national best practices. prevention must also be achieved through closer cooperation between the private and public sectors and through legal protection of technical devices, while, of course, respecting consumer rights. this is one of the difficult issues in this report, namely the distinction between consumer law and the legitimate demands of the professional national criminal standards in customs matters is highly desirable. special attention should also be paid to questions relating to international judicial cooperation. to conclude this very brief to the european union and in all relations with third countries. i would add that since the committee reached a consensus on this report when it was voted, it is important to preserve it in the plenary so that the european parliament can give a strong political signal of its commitment to the fight against counterfeiting and piracy. finally, i call on the commission - which i hope will present as soon as possible its proposal for an action programme to respond to the urgency of this phenomenon. it is clear that the urgency is truly absolute, especially with regard to piracy and all audiovisual matters, and the commission must respond strongly and quickly.

these fraudulent goods, it is imperative to cut the tap through which they flow into a single market which thus flouts all the principles which are supposed to regulate its operation. and to do this, in writing. - parliament adopted today the common position on the legal aspects of electronic commerce as it stands. everyone will recognise the value of clear regulation in a field which is constantly evolving and which presents considerable economic and legal challenges. i shall not dwell any longer on aspects which have already been largely developed. i would like to return to another aspect which i consider more essential. we are now rightly regulating disputes which may arise from impersonal and therefore risky electronic transactions in commercial matters. it is now imperative that we think about how to avoid them in advance. and to do this, we must first of all combat the logic which would have us believe that, in a world which is losing its most sacred references, electronic commerce is just another phase of a society without rules, and therefore, as we see, inevitably unfavourable to the weakest. this is not a question of banning an extraordinary tool of culture and openness; it's about being as demanding with him as you are with any legitimate business. and here we get to the heart of the matter: e-commerce, and the internet more generally, is the expression of a society without legal and ultimately human territorial boundaries. this precious good of freedom is caricatured by those who, whether intentionally or not, promote the destruction of protective standards: freedom does not really exist in any society unless each person has the legal capacity to accept or reject, in full knowledge of the facts, what is offered to him, and not just to embark on trials a posteriori, the many difficulties of which have been clearly seen during these debates. the law must be the expression of a general political vision, of a social project. otherwise, it merely follows developments it cannot anticipate or control. international or supranational structures never have this little extra creative soul of mobilizing ideas and collective commitment. the european union is no exception.
in writing. - the report we are debating today concerns relations between switzerland and the european union. it should be recalled that switzerland participated in the negotiations which led to the conclusion of the agreement on the european economic area. however, in a referendum in 1992, the swiss people voted against the agreement. this has resulted in switzerland's participation in the eea agreement being made impossible and its application for membership of the european union, submitted in may 1992, being frozen. it was therefore necessary to find a way to maintain links between switzerland and the eu. this has led to the establishment of bilateral agreements. since 1993, switzerland has submitted a series of requests for participation in the internal market in relation to specific sectors. following these requests, negotiations between switzerland and the european union resulted in a package of sectoral agreements. this 'package' consists of seven agreements covering road and air transport, free movement of persons, public procurement, research and development, mutual recognition of conformity assessment and agriculture. in order to prevent any agreement being removed by referendum after the conclusion of the negotiations, the european union decided to bind these agreements by including in each of them a common clause providing that all agreements could only enter into force simultaneously and could only be applied in their entirety. this ensures a minimum of consistency. the procedure was somewhat slowed down at council level, in particular due to differences of opinion on the agreement on the free movement of persons. under pressure from the european parliament, the council presented last april the single consolidated legislative instrument to approve the seven agreements between the community and its member states, on the one hand, and the swiss confederation, on the other. the proposal for a decision incorporates into a single legal instrument the seven proposals for decisions previously submitted by the commission, with amendments. the council then referred the matter to the european parliament. it was only then that we were able to make a statement and decide whether or not we were going to give our opinion in accordance with this package of agreements. in this case, the rapporteur is calling for us to do so and i will follow his position. this is all the more important as a referendum on the agreement on the free movement of persons will take place in switzerland on 21 may. it is therefore necessary to send a positive political signal by giving this assent. i would like to make a few points, however. switzerland must clarify its position vis-à-vis the european union. it cannot continue to choose a europe according to the map !

in writing. - the draft regulation before us today aims to provide an appropriate legal basis for the european union to finance certain entities set up by the international community following conflicts and which are responsible for implementing certain peace agreements - as is the case in bosnia-herzegovina - or which have the task of providing transitional civil administration in certain regions, as is currently the case in kosovo. the purpose of this text is also to ensure the transparency of funding in the form of grants, but also to allow the extension of the type of action concerned to other entities in the future. on the basis of this text, the european commission would take the financing decisions and, acting on behalf of the union, conclude financial agreements with these various entities. thus, the argument that this regulation is an unavoidable necessity resulting from political decisions taken long ago is nothing more or less than a deliberate desire to strengthen communitarianism. let 's not get it wrong ! this regulation - and this is a request from the council - is intended to transfer to the first pillar, i.e. the broad field of community policies managed by the commission, the financing of joint actions adopted under the cfsp which, until now, were financed from the budget of the common foreign and security policy. here too, we are witnessing a significant strengthening of the powers of the most integrative, par excellence, most federalist body, the european commission, on the grounds, not acknowledged by the council, that certain measures should be maintained and funds should be freed up for other actions. it should be recalled that if the european commission decided to support them, the financing of new entities that could be established by the international community would be ensured by a coverage of the first pillar budget, while the consultation of the european parliament is not envisaged. finally, from a strictly budgetary point of view, the proposal for a regulation puts a little more pressure on heading 4 of the financial perspective - external actions - which is already very much needed for reconstruction in the western balkans and implies, if implemented this year, an amending and supplementary budget. for all these reasons, the french delegation of the uen group cannot support mr laschet's report.
- madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted against mr sterckx's report, which i believe poses serious threats to the future of air transport. firstly, the analysis of the liberalisation of air traffic in this report is not carried out accurately. not to mention the huge environmental impact. this is not to mention the enormous impact on air congestion, which is linked to the fact that the average number of passengers per flight has been considerably reduced by competition. we forget to mention, or only sketch at the surface, the enormous social decline in these sectors and we fail to mention the negative effects on spatial planning, so much so that today, to go to a remote corner of europe, the costs are high, even though, in sectors already well served, the costs are reduced. the balance of this liberalization is therefore negative. worse still, mr sterckx's report proposes a new stage, where not only is there a single european sky envisaged, a proposal which deserves to be considered, but where it is inevitably linked to the privatisation of air traffic control. even the united states of america has not privatized its air traffic control agency. it is under the federal jurisdiction of the federal state of the united states of america. even this liberal country has not made that choice. we must have seen nothing of the deterioration of safety in british transport, of the repeated accidents linked to the privatisation of this mode of transport, to not think that in terms of safety, nothing is better than the public service. the choice made in this report is quite different, it is the opposite, it is completely the opposite. i believe that europe needs the confidence of its people more than ever and that a new stage of liberalisation runs counter to their hopes. they show it regularly. it is not surprising that liberalism will return.
in writing. - i supported mrs fourtou's draft report on the commission's green paper on the fight against counterfeiting and piracy because we are in a preparatory phase and i believe that the serious dangers to which counterfeiting and piracy expose us have been well highlighted by our rapporteur. indeed, beyond the already significant economic issues and the activities of organised crime, consumers are exposed to serious risks to human safety and health. i also agree with the report's emphasis on public awareness and information measures and calls for a stronger enforcement of the increasing counterfeiting and piracy phenomenon. i am more reserved, however, about the degree of harmonization that is desired, particularly in criminal matters. in the same spirit, i would not like the national parliaments to be called upon to simply give a warning, implying that without legislative action at national level, in civil and criminal matters, we would be in a deadlock. such reasoning, which is the seed of the green paper, would be a little short, but i have no doubt that cooperation between the competent authorities and the exchange of experience will make it possible to obtain satisfactory results as soon as possible, without falling into this trap. we must face the obvious: we already have tried and tested practices at national level. they should be better coordinated and not excluded in the name of uniformity, which would be counterproductive. finally, i would like to welcome the call by our rapporteur to the european and national authorities to ensure that protected works, such as office software, are used within their own institutions. i would even go further and say, as our colleague yves butel has said, that in this area more than a code of conduct is required, strict compliance with the regulations.
in writing. - mrs fourtou's report gave us the opportunity to discuss, in advance, the measures to be taken to combat counterfeiting and piracy. this report rightly denounces the harmful consequences of these methods on the economies of our countries and the risks they pose to buyers of lower quality products. parliament adopted some conclusions of the committee on industry, in particular on the challenges of this struggle and the importance of eliminating certain disparities in intellectual property protection regimes to remedy them. we thought it useful to adopt, by way of amendments, other conclusions not adopted by the legal affairs committee, in particular on the need for rapid and effective civil legal protection of intellectual property rights, or on the need for effective, appropriate and realistic patent legislation. similarly, as regards the definitions of scope, it would have been appropriate to add to the intentional and fraudulent aspects of these activities the commercial purpose behind them. the fact that these activities are not based on the pursuit of easy and illicit profit removes one of their essential dimensions, namely that they are in fact a facet of organised crime. on the other hand, i am glad that the plenary adopted our amendment to define innovation and innovation improvement appropriately, since the proximity of these two areas often makes it possible to present as innovations what are only superficial transformations intended to mask real counterfeits. piracy and counterfeiting pose considerable risks, both to those who are victims of it and to those who profit from it. the organized crime, to which they often belong, requires that we define precisely the legal tools we want to create to combat it. the effectiveness of the law, especially in the community area, will lie in this precision and in its capacity to respond effectively to concrete problems.

- doc. a5-0117/2000 by mrs roth-behrendt, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and consumer policy, on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation laying down the rules for the prevention and control of certain transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (com (98) 623 - c4-0025/1999 - 1998/0323 (cod)).

the bse. the starting point of this case is the milk quotas in 1984. in order to have the best milk reference, our british friends have pushed the cows like engines: by overfeeding them. and to save on feed costs, they fed the cows corn meal. and to further save fuel in the manufacture of flour, they lowered the cooking temperature, allowing the pathogen to survive. bse is the tragic child of profit-making and the british agricultural model. we knew about the disease as early as 1986. we didn't do much until 1996. why? because the maastricht treaty had to be sold to public opinion. you shouldn't have scared them. so the press knew, the commission knew, the european parliament knew, but nobody spoke. and when in march 1996 the british, through the british ministers for agriculture and health, admitted that the disease could be transmitted to humans, the necessary measures were not taken. why would you do that ? because this time it was not a question of selling the maastricht treaty, but the amsterdam treaty, and public opinion should not be alarmed. so from silence to lies, the epidemic settled in with the picture we know. first, bse has not disappeared from britain and will not disappear. secondly, the late ban on flour did not eliminate the contamination. thirdly, either the contamination is cross-contaminated with flours fed to chickens, or there is a third route of contamination. in addition to the contamination from the mother, there would be transmission through the fields, through the pastures, through the grass, and as with sheep's clover, we would have cursed lands, lands where the prion would enkystate and return as soon as we put cattle. fourth, britain and the polluting industries have not paid. it is the innocent farmers, the grain growers who have paid, just as the farmers are paying for kosovo. i am therefore saying that the directive and the regulation are sympathetic, but they are a little hypocritical. we all agree that we should have regulations on prevention, that we should adopt the amendments of the committee on agriculture, which should have been taken on the substance. we agree with the scientific approach: how to remove the ilium, the ganglia, the duodenum, the lymph nodes, the lingual, medial, lateral, renal, pre-mora, cervical nodes in the slaughterhouse, but that is not the main point. in the bse disaster, when the moment of truth came, when protection was needed, it was the states that protected. and that's the big lesson of the ets case. firstly, protection is always provided by the states. second, the precautionary principle is to keep the nations. this does not prevent the building of europe, but rather the way children build huts in their gardens: for fun. that is why we are all here, mr president, good playmates.
- mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the logic of maximum profit leads to all kinds of aberrations, including feeding animal meal to herbivores. it's not just the cows that went crazy. as a result, sheep's scrapie has spread to cattle in the form of bse. consumer health requires that all possible measures be taken to prevent and vigorously combat these diseases and their vectors. the measures taken in 1997 are all the more inadequate now that scientists are talking about a third route of contamination. efficient means should therefore be provided to eradicate transmissible spongiform encephalopathies permanently, if possible, namely: to control and treat the waste chain when the waste is used in animal feed; destroy hazardous materials in case of suspicion; prohibit the incorporation of animal protein into the feed of livestock; require traceability by indicating the place of birth and the region of rearing of the animals; establish, at member state level, close monitoring systems, which alone guarantee the effectiveness of control and the transparency of monitoring; impose a rapid and systematic screening procedure and thorough checks, if necessary. finally, slaughter the entire herd if one is infected. food safety is at this price, but it must not be used as a pretext for calling into question the transport of live animals.

random testing for bse and the forthcoming proposal on animal waste. however, i accept amendment no 52. i also accept amendments nos 10 and 49 to article 3, with a slight rewording to create the that we will be continually monitoring the possibility of increasing bse testing for animals. as regards specified risk material: unfortunately i cannot accept amendments nos 16, 17, 18, 40 and 41 to article 8, which make the approval and conditions of use of rapid diagnostic tests subject to the codecision procedure. it is my belief that it is essential to maintain the flexibility of the comitology procedure. i also cannot accept that tests should be able to detect the level of infectivity in all products and at all levels of disease. that's the advice i was given. i partly accept amendment no 19 to rule 8, which calls for an adjustment of the age limits for the elimination of msds under the comitology procedure. however, i cannot accept the restriction of an annual adjustment and, in particular, the proposed deadline for the first adjustment to be 1 january next, which is too early. i also accept amendment no 20 to article 8, which places the principle of granting derogations from the provisions on the disposal of msds in high-risk areas and of taking into account an effective ban on feeding into the codecision procedure. i also welcome amendments nos 38, 39 and 56 to annex iv. they propose mainly that long bones of bovine animals should no longer be considered as srms and suggest a reformulation of the proposed derogation for the removal of the spine in a comitology procedure. as regards the ban on feeding: i accept amendments nos 22 and 42. i accept only part of amendments nos 21 and 57 on condition that the possibility of extending the ban is granted, without taking into account the risk statuses. i also partially accept amendment no 54 to annex v, which lays down the detailed rules for the extended feeding ban. i cannot accept the derogation for dicalcium phosphate as it goes against our scientific advice. i also reject the limitation of the extension of the feeding ban to all species, mainly domestic animals, only if there is a risk of cross-contamination from livestock feed, as we believe that ruminant protein should be banned for all predisposed species. i'm thinking mostly about cats. that's the advice i was given about cats. i accept in part amendment no 50 to annex v which exempts gelatine obtained from the skin from the ban. however, i do not accept the proposal to exempt from the ban cat food based on ruminant protein. i also reject amendment no 23 to article 9, which guarantees the immediate application of food bans, as this amendment is not fully justified by law. as regards the eradication of the disease, i accept amendments nos 25 and 28. i also welcome amendment no 24 to article 11, but i propose a rewording, asking for 'regular' rather than 'immediate' notification. i also accept in part amendment no 26 to article 13 and amendment no 43 to annex vii, introducing the slaughter of whole herds in the case of bse in bovine, ovine and caprine animals and excluding animals intended for research purposes from these provisions. the slaughter of entire herds for bse only, not for scrapie, is acceptable provided that equivalent measures are approved in comitology. i reject the second part of the amendment, which is, in fact, superfluous. i accept amendment no 44 in part, provided that equivalent measures are adopted on a case-by-case basis in committee. i reject amendment no 27 to article 13, which calls for a complete cessation of the activities of a holding when a confirmed case of tse occurs, as i consider that the extremely strict conditions of our proposals are already used anywhere else in the text and is, moreover, inadequate for the control of tse. i would add that the dna regions (protected areas) are too small and too difficult to control. larger, legally
