counsel. - the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the permissible sound power level of towed vehicles (com (91) 0173 - c3-0314/91); i would like to address some of the central issues raised in this debate. first, the danger of an intergovernmental drift. i am quite willing to talk about this because i have been publicly advocating for a long time that we must gradually arrive at a single pillar for the whole of the union. the portuguese presidency has shown that it does not want an intergovernmental drift. firstly, at the intergovernmental conference itself, it sought to involve the european parliament much more closely than had been decided in helsinki. secondly, in the context of the lisbon strategy, the importance of the tasks entrusted to the commission confirms its fundamental role in all that concerns the open method of coordination of the union's socioeconomic policies. we also organised a forum before the feira summit, bringing together parliament, the commission and the council, together with the member states, the european central bank, the european investment bank, the economic and social council, the committee of the regions and the social partners. i therefore fully agree with all those who believe that the union's characteristics must be preserved and strengthened as such, and that an intergovernmental drift is absolutely undesirable. secondly, the intergovernmental conference. the role of the portuguese presidency was not to complete the work of the intergovernmental conference. it was to do what we did, namely, to draw up a report detailing in great detail all the positions and possibilities on the issues arising from the so-called amsterdam relics, and at the same time to ensure that a consensus, which did not exist in helsinki, was reached in order to ensure that the issues on enhanced cooperation, which in our view are closely linked, such as the possibility of extending qualified majority voting in the council and, perhaps, also its link with the european parliament's codecision processes, were included in the agenda of the conference. but this must be done with the understanding that enhanced cooperation is not about overthrowing the union. they must be carried out within the framework of the union and may not contain any arbitration or exclusion mechanism. they can be a fundamental instrument for strengthening integration in the context of an enlarged and more heterogeneous union, while respecting the union's rules. we could then ask whether it will be possible to complete the igc. the question is very clear to me today. i, like all of us, regard the intergovernmental conference as the set of changes needed to make enlargement possible. the choices are now quite clear to all. this report identifies them precisely. a month will be enough to complete the igc if the political will is there. the whole point is whether or not we want to reach a compromise, which is essential, because we know all the possible compromises. do we want to make these compromises together or not? i am convinced that the political will will be there and that it will then be possible to conclude the work during the french presidency. i am particularly comfortable with the charter of fundamental rights, because the portuguese government has always defended the inclusion of the charter of fundamental rights in the treaty. it is also clear that what we have tried to do, without having been given a mandate, is to put this item on the feira agenda, to ask the president of the convention to report to the european council on the progress made, a european council which cannot decide on its inclusion on the igc agenda until the convention has decided within itself whether or not this is a matter which should be given binding legal content. but the feira council decided to leave this matter pending in order to allow the convention to make a clear decision on the matter, whether or not it is possible to include the charter of fundamental rights in the igc agenda. what i want, what the portuguese government wants, is that it be considered a fundamental instrument of the union. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. i can assure you that during this semester, he has not suffered any delay. i have just said that 72 negotiating files were closed in six months. as regards the countries whose negotiations were opened during the portuguese presidency of the council - latvia, lithuania, slovakia, romania, bulgaria and malta - i can tell you this: as far as latvia is concerned, eight chapters have been opened and five have been concluded; for lithuania, eight were opened and five concluded; for slovakia, eight open and six closed; for romania, five and five; for bulgaria, five and four; and for malta, eight and seven. we have therefore worked at a very fast pace, with the excellent cooperation of the commission - and i would like to emphasize the role of commissioner günter verheugen - because we are moving as fast as possible in the enlargement work. the lisbon summit established a strategy. we all now accept that we are going to live in an information society and a knowledge-based economy. the question is whether it will include everyone or not. the fundamental thing in the european vision of this strategy is that it must include everyone. the european response to this is what we call the educational society, a society which is based primarily on lifelong learning, as was emphasized here today. three months after an extraordinary number of decisions, it was not at the feira summit that the process was completed, but despite this, the feira summit has already approved a set of fundamental documents. the small businesses have been mentioned here: the charter for small businesses is approved. the information society was mentioned: the action plan for the information society was approved. we have heard a lot about the fight against poverty: three reports of the greatest importance are already on the table, reports which will make it possible to take decisions in the short term. i am referring to the commission's report on combating exclusion, the report of the high-level group, now the social protection committee, also on social exclusion and the sustainability of pensions. so i have the deep conviction that we will move very quickly. in addition, as commissioner christopher patten has said, the commission is preparing all the indicators for september, so that the various policy coordination measures that have been defined can be given substance and content. as for the tax package, it was not for nothing that it took 12 years to reach an agreement. if it took 12 years, it's because this agreement is not easy. it is not perfect, but it is a fundamental compromise. i am firmly convinced that the political will which has led to this compromise will be present when it is implemented. i therefore believe that the time-table will be respected in answering the questions put. the essential problem with tax unanimity is that if we are to get decisions to be taken without unanimity, we must have unanimity. so far, such unanimity does not seem possible within the union. a few words, first of all, about the incident in dover. this incident has outraged us all, but we must recognize that what is behind it is the inability that europe still shows today to understand that, in view of the ageing of its population, europe must define an immigration policy and agree on this immigration policy with the countries from which those who wish to come to work in europe come. at the same time, it must adopt a set of social measures to ensure their harmonious integration into our societies. that is the crux of the problem and in this area the commission is now responsible for working on essential matters which, in our view, will translate into very important measures for the union in the short term. we are now entering the heart of another issue which will be very important for the life of our societies in the coming decades. it is about our ability to live with difference, our ability to promote tolerance in our societies, to fight against all forms of xenophobia and racism. because let's be clear, xenophobia and racism exist in all of our societies, in all of our countries. they exist as a social phenomenon, and what is tragic is that political forces and especially political forces aspiring to power want to use xenophobia and racism to win votes. what i want to say very clearly, ... (applause)... what i want to say very clearly, is that it is contrary to european values. if we are to accept, in the name of the sovereignty of the states, that these political forces participate in governments in the states, i must say quite frankly that for me a political force which uses xenophobia to win votes and gain power does not belong to the same family of values as myself and, therefore, i have no difficulty in losing face or not with regard to what we have done, in my name, in the name of my government and in the name of the other governments of the 14 member states, when austria saw a party come to power which, in our view, did not respect these fundamental values. that said, i should also like to say that the portuguese presidency of the union has taken great care - and it has not always been easy - to ensure that austria participates fully in the work of the union and, moreover, to guarantee the dignity of austrian representatives, including members of the government from the fpö, in all council bodies. the presidency did so because it was convinced that the right of any government of a sovereign member state such as mine to have an opinion on the government of another sovereign state is one thing - and i have not renounced that right of my state - and that the functioning of a union is another; i think it is our duty to ensure that it is fully operational. of course, as regards the decisions of the 14 member states concerning the relations between their governments and the austrian government, we have defined a procedure which will enable us, in due course, to reassess these decisions, which are, as i said, taken in a strictly bilateral manner and without any effect, because the portuguese presidency wanted it to be so, on the functioning of the union. they will also have no effect on the presence of austria, and the dignity of the austrian representatives, in all the activities of the union which we have been called upon to preside over, because the presidency has decided so, despite some contrary pressures.
commission mr president, i can answer very briefly because my esteemed friend mr beazley - and i use this expression in both a personal and a parliamentary sense - has put a question to me directly in words that would perhaps have been better received in berlin than in paris or london. the honourable member asked me what i thought of the relations between the institutions - between the council, the commission and parliament. i can answer very frankly: in my area of expertise this is a subject which has been the subject of one or two of my speeches. i am very firmly of the opinion that i do not want any extension of the commission's powers in the area for which i am responsible. i want us to manage our powers more effectively, and i want us to be allowed to exercise them fully to support the development of a common foreign and security policy. i do not think we are seeking to take over new powers, but to exercise the powers which the treaty has given us. we should try to exercise these powers in an even more democratic and transparent way. let me give you an example of what i mean. each year we have to refer to the budgetary authority - that is to say, parliament and the council - the level of our commitments in external relations, but we should be involved in a much more open dialogue with the budgetary authority on the destination of these budget lines. there should be a more serious exchange of views on our political priorities. so, again in response to the honourable member, i want us to manage much better what we already have responsibility for. i want us to be allowed to do this, and i want us to be as accountable as possible to this parliament and to the council for what we are doing. our aspirations are as simple and direct as that, and they have the immense advantage of reflecting what is provided for in the treaties. finally, i would like to congratulate the portuguese presidency once again on the end of its term. it was, i repeat, a great pleasure to work with the portuguese government, with its extremely dynamic ministers and civil servants. i have worked under various presidencies during a long political career and i hope not too badly employed, and i do not think i have ever known a better, more competent, more energetic or more courteous president than the prime minister of portugal.
the next item is the report (a5-0175/2000) by mr lehne, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending council directive 91/308/eec of 10 june 1991 on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering (com (99) 352 - c5-0065/1999 - 1999/0152 (cod)).
the commission is aware of the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. the fight against money laundering is a top political priority. the more intensive efforts to eliminate the proceeds of this criminal activity are regularly highlighted in the final declarations of the summits. at both the tampere and feira summits, the european council called on the european parliament and the council of ministers to approve this proposal as soon as possible, which provides for updating and extending the scope of the 1991 directive on money laundering. parliament and the rapporteur have declared their readiness to work towards adopting the proposal at first reading. with this objective in mind, a number of meetings have taken place between the rapporteur, the chairman of the council working party and the commission services. unfortunately, i must admit that the matter has not progressed as well in the council as in parliament, and the debates there have not been able to provide the necessary clarity on a number of points in this proposal. that is why the dossier is being submitted for opinion at first reading in this plenary session, in accordance with the normal procedure. virtually everyone will agree that the directive of 10 june 1991 on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering has had a satisfactory effect. although it is not easy to measure the preventive effect of this directive, it is undeniable that it has become a little more difficult for money launderers to find their way into the financial system in general and the banking system in particular. from the outset, however, it was clear that the 1991 directive would have to be updated at some point. the prohibition on money laundering laid down in the directive only covers income from drug trafficking, which is no longer in line with international practice. in addition, article 12 of the 1991 text already provided for the possibility of extending the obligations imposed by the directive to professions and non-financial activities for which there is a risk of money laundering. but we'll get to that tonight. experience has also shown that a number of technical aspects need to be addressed or clarified. the pressure on the european union to step up its fight against money laundering stems from the action programme on organised crime, approved at the amsterdam summit in 1997, and from the report and resolution adopted by parliament in march 1999. the most difficult and sensitive aspect of the proposal is undoubtedly the extension of the obligations imposed on it, such as the obligation to report any suspicion of money laundering and the extension of the obligation to the non-financial and especially legal professions. as sensitive as this subject is, the commission is firmly convinced that when they act as intermediaries in financial or commercial transactions, these professional categories should be subject to the same obligations as other financial intermediaries. the commission would like to thank the rapporteur and the four committees involved in the preparation of this report for the assistance they have provided in the survey of the professions falling within the scope of the directive. with your permission, i would now like to examine each of the amendments separately. the commission accepts amendments nos 1, 5, 25, 30, 33 and 37 as they stand. the commission generally supports the idea or objective behind most of the proposed amendments, but at this stage it prefers not to opt for a technical solution. it is rather aimed at achieving a compromise which meets both the wishes of parliament and those expressed by the states in the council. this applies to amendments nos 4 and 12. the commission agrees that the notion of organised crime should be adequately defined. however, it considers it preferable to take as a starting point the notion of criminal organisation as defined in the joint action of 21 december 1998. i now turn to amendments nos 6, 15 and 26. the commission is particularly pleased to have the support of parliament for the inclusion of a wide range of occupational categories in the scope of the directive. as regards tax advisers and accountants, the commission has not yet adopted a definitive position on whether these professional categories should be treated on an equal footing with lawyers and therefore fall within the scope of the directive for a limited number of activities or, on the contrary, for a wider range of activities. i come now to amendments nos 17, 18 and 19. the commission proposal has opened an interesting debate on the question of whether it would not be desirable to involve also several groups of dealers in high-value items, such as jewellers, art dealers, etc., in the fight against money laundering. but the problem is that these traders are generally not subject to any legislation and it would be difficult, if not impossible, to verify whether they have complied with their obligations. the commission will continue to look for another way of properly integrating these traders into the scope of the directive. but it wants to avoid this aspect of the issue delaying the adoption of the proposal too long. amendments nos 21 and 22. the commission recognises that differentiated identity requirements may be justified in certain cases. it will continue its activities in relation to this aspect of the proposal. amendments nos 9, 10, 13 and 14. these four amendments deal with definitions. in this respect, the commission accepts the reference to electronic money. a comment has also just been made on this. this is amendment no 9. the commission is prepared to examine the extent to which ucits (collective investment undertakings) and investment firms should fall within the scope of the directive. amendment no 10 refers back to this problem. the commission supports the amendments concerning fraud in the community, namely amendment no 13, and the concept of competent authorities, namely amendment no 14. amendment no 11 is not adopted. the commission agrees to examine with the member states the role that market surveillance authorities could play. amendment no 23 is adopted. as regards the identification of customers, the commission agrees to drop the annex. however, it is still considering the most appropriate text to be included in the draft proposal. amendment no 24 is not a new one. the commission is prepared to consult the member states on possible adjustments to the amounts relating to insurance contracts. amendments nos 31, 32, 41 and 43. the commission is satisfied with the support given to olaf in its role under the proposal. amendment no 34, by mr the commission agrees that the concept of 'independent legal professions' should be defined by each member state. nothing in the proposal prevents member states from going beyond the requirements of the directive. amendment no 38 is not adopted. the commission is in favour of a wider coverage of the gambling sector where it would be possible, in practice, to impose the same control measures. i now come to the amendments which the commission finds unacceptable. let us start with amendments nos 2 and 3. they appear to deprive olaf of any competence under this directive. amendments nos 7, 8, 16 and 45. the commission considers that these amendments may restrict the scope of the directive to the legal professions too much. amendment number 20. the proposal cannot apply to customs and tax officials in the same way as it applies to financial institutions or to the professional categories covered by the directive. this aspect should be left to the member states. amendments nos 27, 28 and 29. these amendments call into question aspects of the 1991 directive which, in the commission's view, do not require amendment. amendment no 35 is adopted. the possibility of having recourse to the bar or an equivalent supervisory body is a choice left to the member states, and the relationship between the member states and the bar or another similar body is a matter for each member state. amendment no 36 is adopted. the commission considers that it is for each member state to decide whether mortgage registries have a role to play in the fight against money laundering. amendment no 39 is adopted. the obligations imposed under this directive may not be applied outside the territory of the european union. the issue of offshore centres is currently being examined by the financial action task force. amendment number 40. the commission cannot accept this deletion, because it would impose on the bar a duty of cooperation which can only be duly fulfilled by the regular authorities responsible for the fight against money laundering. i shall end with amendment no 42. the commission considers that it is not desirable to impose a limitation on the use of cash in this proposal. i shall conclude my reply to your assembly, mr president. i am sorry that i have spoken longer than i should have, but i wanted to comment on all the amendments, since this is an important subject and all the amendments deserve a brief comment.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on wednesday at 11.30 a.m.

the commission's proposal for a regulation on the common organization of the market in bananas is a very important one. this architecture is based on two pillars, namely the creation of an area of freedom, security and justice in accordance with the new title iv inserted in the ec treaty and the integration of the schengen acquis into the union framework, to which is added a variable geometry dimension resulting from the various protocols annexed by several member states to the treaty of amsterdam. the commission's proposal is legally based on the treaty of amsterdam, and its content and wording take account of the institutional constraints i have just mentioned. the commission has carefully examined mr lehne's report, and i should like to congratulate him. in the past, mr lehne has had the opportunity, as rapporteur, to demonstrate his interest, expertise and commitment to the subject he has just presented. the commission is pleased to note that the report adopted by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs broadly supports the commission's proposal. but this is hardly surprising, since, as mr lehne himself has pointed out, the proposal meets a number of requests made by the european parliament itself in various resolutions. as regards the amendments to its proposal, the commission greatly appreciates the constructive contribution of parliament. to clarify our position: amendments nos 3 and 4 can be accepted because the changes in wording they propose avoid any contradiction with other provisions of the regulation. we can also accept amendments nos 1 and 5. amendments nos 7 and 8 are inspired by the desire to clarify the demarcation line between the scope of regulation and other subjects, some of which are governed by the schengen acquis, which is integrated into the community. the commission is sensitive to this desire for clarification, which it has also taken into account in its explanatory memorandum. however, it is of the opinion that the appropriate place for such clarification is not in an article of the regulation and it is prepared to prepare a new text on the basis of the essential points of these amendments. in our view, amendment no 2 cannot be accepted, because it concerns the conditions for issuing visas, which do not fall within the scope of this regulation but will have to be dealt with by another instrument. finally, the commission cannot accept amendment no 6 either. despite all the sympathy one may feel for the idea of granting visa exemption to young people participating in european union youth programmes, the commission must stick to its objective of maximum harmonisation and avoid cases creating derogations or exceptions to the visa requirement. the commission is convinced that efforts to ensure that the need to obtain a visa does not constitute an obstacle for young people wishing to participate in european union programmes will have to be made in the area of rules on visa conditions, which will be dealt with through another instrument and are not covered by this regulation. in conclusion, i would like to thank parliament, the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and mr lehne, the rapporteur, for their constructive approach and, above all, for examining the commission's proposal on visas so quickly. the commission appreciates the diligence of parliament; this speed will make it possible to meet the deadlines set in the action plan adopted in vienna and reproduced in the table of performance following the tampere european council.

- madam president, mr president of the republic, the french presidency of the european union comes at a time when the debate on the meaning and future of european integration is gaining momentum. i do not think it is exaggerating to speak of a crisis of confidence between many citizens and the european institutions, or at least of discomfort and a search for a new european identity. the idea of europe attracts, the reality of europe leaves perplexed or repels. there's a problem with that. in this sense, the slogans that emerge from the large gatherings such as those in seattle, washington, geneva and millau: 'the world is not a commodity', 'politicians admit their impotence in the face of globalisation' and 'it is up to us to decide' are the visible expression of much wider-spread concerns and demands that directly challenge the europe under construction. in order to begin to meet these expectations, the french presidency should, in my group's view, try to send strong signals in three directions, which are closely linked. first, it should express the will to encourage europe to break free from the neoliberal model which structures the present globalisation; secondly, it should demonstrate its determination to promote the return of political will, political choice and political responsibility in the face of the power of markets, corporations and their lobbies; thirdly, it should encourage the effective participation of the social actors of our various countries and of the emerging european citizens' movements in the process of european policy-making. the objectives of the french presidency which you have just presented, mr president of the republic, are they likely to open up such prospects? it would be short-sighted and, to say the least, a little desperate to simply answer 'no', but it would be dishonest of me to say 'yes' outright, even though i am not a norman. the reform of the institutions is certainly essential, but the key issue of citizen participation in the construction of europe is not on the agenda of the intergovernmental conference. the social agenda is a magnificent challenge which we are determined to help to meet. you decisions. it now remains to set quantified objectives and verifiable deadlines, to provide adequate financing and to give effect to the rights of employees to intervene in the management of enterprises. it is also necessary, mr president, to define the type of activities for all that we intend to recover and what we mean by social protection adapted to the requirements of our time. you pact and to the current tasks of the european central bank. it will take political will to win a 15-nation agreement against social and fiscal dumping or to stop the trend towards full liberalization of public services. it will take political will to consider limiting the commission's discretion in competition policy. it is at each of these levels, in my view, and at many others, that action will have to be taken to promote a model of development based on solidarity and a social europe. you have rightly insisted on a europe of men and women. we agree with the idea of promoting trade, we agree closed to traffickers but open to people. we also disapprove of the accelerated militarization of the union, which tends to relegate foreign policy initiatives as such to the background. the success - madam president, mr president, france holds the presidency of the european union for six months. it is not the first time that the european parliament has been asked to make a statement on the situation in the former yugoslavia. i am a member of the europe of democracies and differences group. this name alone constitutes a programme whose primary objective is to ensure that the identities and aspirations of each country are taken into account in the best possible way, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. after the crisis of the santer commission - which shook the institutions - why did you bury the report of the committee of experts exposing the serious institutional dysfunctions? we must learn from the past to prepare for the future and avoid the commission once again being empowered by a technocratic structure that operates without transparency and without democracy. should we not question the political dimension it has given itself? we cannot be satisfied with a europe which adopts more and more dehumanized texts that are too far removed from the needs of the people, who are often the victims of these texts in their daily lives. the fact that the court of justice has the final say in the interpretation of these texts is all the more so since it is the court of justice which, by virtue of its power of interpretation, has the real power to legislate, but without any political control. we therefore reject a government of civil servants as a government of judges. the igc must not be the instrument of a reform which will make the europe of tomorrow a technocratic monster, increasingly ignorant of the legitimate concerns of the peoples and the opinion of the national parliaments which represent them. we cannot accept that this reform leaves certain states the right and the power to impose binding texts on those who do not wish to do so. the promised reform of institutions is choking our nations, especially the smaller ones. new systems of operation and voting are being created which give power and hegemony to what some call pioneer states. this is unacceptable. we must respect differences and let them be expressed, because that is where europe's real wealth lies. while the construction of europe should seek to coordinate the policies of the member states, the objective of integration leads us to an intolerable standardization. this forced uniformity, the source of a single model, goes against what we are trying to defend every day, namely differences. how can we claim to defend the aspiration of everyone to live better when our cultures and traditions are being challenged more and more every day? behind the institutional debates, certain topics are particularly important, such as employment, health, food security and the defence of local products. there is also the whole debate on the balanced development of the territories and respect for their users, as well as the future of public services and state monopolies. we believe that public services in the french way, which are particularly structural in terms of spatial planning and social cohesion, such as postal, railway, energy services, etc., must be defended against the commission's position. is it anti-european to promote national interests? is it anti-european to ask for the amendment of directives such as the birds, habitats, outdoor markets and biotechnology directives? on the eve of enlargement, there is a need to reflect on this acquis communautaire, which some would like to see as 'unchangeable' in principle, in defiance of democracy and subsidiarity. in conclusion, mr president, we hope that you will be willing to give the elected representatives and the various peoples a voice again in order to avoid a new rural and territorial divide. if france is to speak with one voice, the people must be its voice: the "blue" have shown the example. the victory was a great one, mr president, but the championship was only possible thanks to the europe of nations!

mr president, the atrocious death of 58 chinese illegal immigrants, discovered by british customs officers in dover, highlights, first of all, the strength of the migratory pressures exerted on european countries. i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the situation in the community, but that we should be concerned about the situation in the countries of the community. in such a caricatural case, the first possible response, at our level, is to fight against illegal immigration, and in particular against the mafia-like organizations that organize this new human trafficking. we are a little frightened to hear commissioner vitorino say on 20 june, in relation to the dover tragedy, that all this proves, among other things, the need for 'a genuine policy of admission and integration, breaking once and for all with the fantasy of zero immigration'. those who mention the fantasy of zero immigration do so too often, alas, to try to excuse a lax policy in advance. we don't want to fall into that trap. on the contrary, we are calling for the immediate halt to this immigration, not only through a policy of co-development and the fight against the mafias, but also through the reinforcement of external border controls and the re-establishment of internal border controls, which have been unconsciously destroyed by european decisions in recent years. of course, we will probably not be able to re-establish fixed checks at internal borders in the traditional form. instead, we must move towards a more flexible network, organised around common police stations, located close to the borders. but in any case, controls will be needed, otherwise we will be moving towards a gradual de-structuring of our societies which, to be honest, is too well suited to the objectives of globalisation to be unsuitable for the enemies of europe.
council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think that this debate has shown that there is a broad consensus on the guidelines of the tampere summit, and in particular on the triptych, the first - mr president, i should like to thank mr radwan for the quality of his report on the first financial year of the central bank since the euro came into force. the rapporteur's efforts are worthwhile. the report does indeed show a widespread concern which is fortunately in contrast with the unwavering optimism of the many sponsors of the euro and it reaffirms, somewhat timidly, but nevertheless reaffirms, some basic principles which are all superfluous. in particular, mr radwan is recorded as having pointed out that the independence of the central bank cannot be equated with the absence of any obligation to give account, but that it implies on the contrary a maximum of transparency in order to compensate, in particular, as he should have added, for its lack of legitimacy. unfortunately, mr rapporteur, you can see the symptoms, but you cannot accept to recognize the genetic disease of the euro, which is actually causing the scepticism of the markets, which have devalued it by 20%, the indifference of economic actors, who have not yet adopted it, the mistrust of the citizens: 41% of europeans, in the last eurobarometer, already think that the euro is rather bad for them and, admit it, the authorities are beginning to panic, 18 months before the planned disappearance of national currencies. i would add to this the growing hostility of the british and the continued distrust of the danes, which i hope will be confirmed on 28 september. the first responsibility for the sanction that is being imposed on the european currency is obviously that of the conditions under which it was born. the so-called single currency, hastily devised by france and germany following their reunification, and then by nine other countries, was immediately abandoned by the political authorities and put in the hands of an independent bank, poor cosette, entrusted to the tenarders of frankfurt! under these circumstances, it is understandable that the child is a beggar. in politics, cardinal de retz said, we often get the opposite of what we want. the european parliament has been very active in this area. the american reserve was born well over a century after the united states and after a civil war and it acts, not in complete independence, but in relative independence within what i would call a common pool of feelings, that is to say within a single country. without such a seat, the central bank is not independent, it is isolated. his communication is doomed to failure. it can only speak the language of markets, what a french journalist called the esperanto of money, and not that of the people, which is why the euro, which is only a borrowed currency, has become the toy of markets, instead of being the business of europeans. he may raise your euro, mr duisenberg, but it's not your fault. it's the dollar that's going to be down. so please do not, in the meantime, out of wounded vanity, suffocate a european economy which has already paid a heavy price, in growth and jobs, throughout the 1990s for the race to the euro and which does not want to pay a second time the same price for the race to a strong euro. or you can't complain if the governments come back soon, argue about premature independence and false sovereignty, that is, if jean valjean finally comes to take cosette back.

weakness of the euro against the dollar is the consequence of a tremendous outflow of capital from outside the european union. according to experts, nearly chf 950 billion was thus net out of the euro area in 1999 in the form of foreign direct investment, 43 per cent more than in 1998. in short, the euro is widely used to borrow to finance speculative projects, and even in the united states. the develop a resolutely modern european social model. to achieve this, the social and the monetary spheres must work together. the ecb is the sole master of monetary affairs. in the name of fighting inflation and strictly respecting the stability pact, it even dares to call the governments of the member states to order, but never speaks out to criticize the speculation that is rampant on the financial markets. it advocates wage moderation, flexibility, and precariousness of work. it is pushing privatisation to promote competitiveness and return on capital. it also sells the and penalizes the unemployed. it is essential to reopen the debate on the tasks of the central bank for a new credit policy which takes account of employment criteria. we cannot simply add a social guidelines, it is vital to strengthen the control of the ecb by the european parliament and national parliaments.

in writing. - i should like to say at once that i refuse to subscribe to the ultra-liberal vision proposed in mr jarzembowski's report. it goes far beyond what is proposed in the common position presented by the council. it advocated radical liberalisation of the community's railways, refusing to grant transitional periods, which were essential to allow for a gradual adaptation to the new regulations. it proposes a five-year transition period to liberalize international freight services. it adds that, five years after the directive enters into force, member states will have to open up the entire network, both national and international, for freight. and to top it all off, by 2010 he wants the whole network to be open for both freight and passenger services! at no time does mr jarzembowski concern himself with public service obligations, which remain of primary importance in this area. at no point does it mention the risks that radical liberalisation could entail in terms of security. that is why i did not vote for any of the amendments he put to us.
in writing. - rail transport is now at the heart of the deregulation and liberalisation of public services projects being carried out by the european union. the revision of directive 91/440, according to the conclusions of the jarzembowski report, opens the door wide to privatisation by proposing the separation between the management of infrastructure and the provision of transport services, as well as the right of access to infrastructure, in the medium term, to any undertaking with a view to a total opening up of the market and competition in the transport of freight and passengers. the guidelines of the jarzembowski report tend to align railway management as much as possible with that of private companies and to introduce competitive pressure. they take the deficiencies in the functioning of the public service as an excuse and highlight the superior performance of the private sector on the basis of partial comparisons which do not take into account all the elements and tasks fulfilled. the logic of the jarzembowski report will inevitably lead to a deterioration in safety, a deterioration in the quality of services and services, a decline in customer service and a social regression for the staff. this report turns its back on the real need of the european people: a public service coordinated and harmonized at european level, which could today guarantee a high level of efficiency, quality, safety and fairness for employees and users. that is why, unable to accept either the status quo or the way forward, even if it is gradual and accompanied by liberalisation, i voted against the jarzembowski report.
in writing. - mr jarzembowski said that the european union should do everything possible to complete the internal market in the railway sector by 2005, with the aim of giving railway companies the opportunity to take over part of the road market. we can only welcome such a goal, which is desirable from both an economic and an ecological point of view. we are, however, opposed to the proposed total liberalisation of the railways. we do not want to be forced into a single model! rail transport in france is a valuable public service, a real tool for spatial planning in the broad sense of the term, but also and above all from a rural point of view. the french model railways are also an element of social cohesion. it is quite normal to maintain services at unprofitable stations by financing the profits of stations that are much more profitable. that is why, as a french member of the edd group, i am very keen to defend the notion of public service through this dossier. in addition, an absolute and binding opening up of the railway infrastructure could hinder the development of community railways. for example, by the instability and uncertainty it would introduce into a market which requires high levels of technical expertise and investment for railway undertakings and for local authorities. in conclusion, i would remind you that as an edd member of parliament i support maintaining employment and social cohesion, particularly in rural areas, in order to preserve activity. it is even more important to ensure that the public services provided in our villages do not disappear. if the railways are liberalised, we can say goodbye to life in our countryside and that is why we oppose this blind liberalisation and its consequences!
in writing. - we voted for all the amendments which go towards the recognition throughout the european union of diplomas and qualifications obtained in one of the member states. we are for anything which helps to unify the conditions of the workers and to facilitate the awareness of the identity of their interests across borders. we also voted, despite their often ill-considered nature, for all the amendments which go in the direction of greater qualification and in the direction of the exchange of information between the different countries. but we see hypocrisy in the doctors in third countries whose qualifications and diplomas are not recognized. the report says there are no reliable studies on this. but in many european countries, and certainly in france, hundreds of foreign doctors are working in hospitals and are underpaid because their diplomas are not recognized. it would therefore be a matter of hastening the recognition of their qualifications. the shortcomings in the field of health, the inequalities in access to quality care provided by competent professionals, the inequalities between regions and especially between social classes, do not come from a lack of harmonization of regulations. they are due to the insufficient resources available to the public health service. more generally, they come from the fact that a society characterized by inequality inevitably generates medicine at several speeds.
in writing. - i welcome this initiative, which aims to simplify and clarify the directives relating to the general system for the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications. in fact, to be regularly called by students who are in conflict with the recognition system put in place by the 1989 and 1992 directives, i would say without exaggeration that there is urgency! we don't realize how opaque the mechanisms are. this is the most complete legal uncertainty in this field. too many students encounter obstacles when they apply to the administrations of the member states for this indispensable validation of their training. this is partly because it is difficult to identify the services to which they should turn, but also because the staff of these administrations are not sufficiently trained to respond to their requests. in conclusion, they are referred from one department to another, which does not fail to slow down the procedure. all too often they are faced with unjustified refusals, which place them in absolutely intolerable situations, which prevent them from accessing the labour market of another member state. in principle, this is a flagrant violation of the free movement of persons. in human terms, they are people who are denied the right to practise their profession, thus reducing to nothing the efforts they have made to obtain their professional qualifications. there is also the problem of the cost of the recognition procedure, which seems to me to be far too high. i am therefore pleased that measures are finally being taken to put the principle of free movement of persons into practice, even though they still seem to me to be largely inadequate! in concrete terms, the proposal for a directive contains interesting provisions in terms of clarification of existing legislation. it is foreseen that the host member state will take account of the experience acquired by the person concerned after obtaining the diploma and that it will no longer be able to systematically require compensatory measures (proof of aptitude). a new provision will also avoid the requirement of two years' work experience. it also aims to ensure legal certainty as regards the recognition of training obtained by community nationals in third countries. the european parliament, at its first reading, had proposed many other provisions, notably aimed at extending the information obligations of the member states. the council did not accept any of the proposed amendments. this is quite telling and it shows the lack of political will in this area.
in writing. - the framework agreement on relations between the european parliament and the commission provides useful clarifications, particularly on the circulation of information. however, like 145 other members, including the members of the sos democracy intergroup, i did not vote for him for two reasons. first, annex 3, which restricts the transmission of confidential information to the european parliament, is a step backwards from the current situation. it is clear that the european parliament is not always reliable on confidentiality issues. but on the other hand, the commission may use these provisions to better organise transparency around sensitive matters concerning it. secondly, and most importantly, the framework agreement omits the crucial question of the policy of relations between the commission and the journalists it likes. normally, no document should be given to the press before it is sent to the council and parliament. but the truth is, we're far from it. it is very common for us to read in the newspapers proposals for commission texts which have not yet been officially disclosed to anyone. parliamentarians are then in the ridiculous position of having to comment on texts they are not aware of. such cases are far from accidental. this is a deliberate policy of the commission, which is to harass journalists by communicating texts in advance to those it considers friends, so that they can profit from them. those not on the friends list post their articles a week later, and thus appear to be late to the event. it's obviously very bad for them. so, logically, everyone is trying to please the commission to be on the list of friends. it is by these and other means that the commission has everyone. therefore, a framework agreement which sought to respect a minimum of ethics should have clearly prohibited the commission from handing documents to journalists before they were sent to parliamentarians, and should have provided for the sanctioning of officials guilty of breaching this rule. in the absence of such provisions, we consider the commission's good resolutions on transparency to be largely misleading.

in writing. - i am very pleased that our parliament has had to debate the amendment of the 1991 directive on money laundering. it was essential to adapt this text to the new international economic and financial environment. france, a leading figure in the fight against this scourge, has made it clear that it intends to make this issue a priority on the agenda of the european union. the mere mention of a few figures is enough to justify this position. for example, money laundering accounts for between 2% and 5% of global gdp each year. this phenomenon has become a major threat today. financial crime has adapted to the globalisation of international economic and financial exchanges. it is characterised today by two main features: the increasing complexity of the techniques used to launder money and the internationalisation of criminal financial flows. discussions have been resumed at international level with a view to proposing new measures to combat this scourge effectively. this was particularly the case in april last year when a seminar of the united nations commission on crime prevention and criminal justice on the fight against international financial circuits of corruption was held in france. the seminar resulted in the drafting of the bercy recommendations. these approaches are echoed by the work undertaken within the international financial action task force (ifatf) and the financial stability forum. at european level, the european parliament has called since 1996 for the 1991 directive to be updated. the european commission's proposals are in line with those made at international level. the first is to extend the list of infringements. money laundering within the meaning of the directive should no longer only concern the proceeds of drug trafficking, but also participation in activities related to organized crime, as well as fraud, corruption and any other illegal activities affecting the financial interests of the european communities. the obligations imposed by the directive are also extended without reservation to various non-financial activities and professions (accountants and accountants, estate agents, dealers in precious stones and metals, money carriers, casino managers, casino owners and managers). they also apply to notaries and other members of the independent legal professions who carry out activities that are likely to result in money laundering. the principle is to ensure that data subjects identify their clients when entering into business relations with them and to keep documents and supporting documents. credit and financial institutions shall be required to cooperate with the authorities; in other words, banking secrecy is lifted in the event of suspicion of money laundering. i therefore voted in favour of this directive, which is part of an action plan to combat organised crime in general. i would like to conclude by stressing that the debate on the tax haven scandal must lead rapidly to concrete measures to dismantle it.
in writing. - the concerns which inspired this report clearly illustrate the fact that the european union was made for capital and not for men. there is no visa requirement for capital, regardless of origin, but it is required for nationals of many countries, even for stays of less than three months. there is no justification for the segregation between a minority of countries whose nationals are exempt from visas and the majority of countries whose nationals are obliged to do so. why should a national of morocco, senegal or ukraine be denied the same rights as a national of new zealand, israel or the sultanate of brunei? we abstained rather than vote against this report, although we disagree with the spirit of the whole report, because it slightly extends the list of visa-free countries compared with the present situation. we are for human beings to have at least as many rights as you give to capital, that is to say, for the free movement of persons and the abolition of all visas.

mr president, i am very grateful to you for the opportunity to inform parliament of a decision taken this morning by the commission on a proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a community patent. this decision follows the request of the lisbon european council to establish a community patent by 2001. parliament explicitly supported this initiative in its contributions to the extensive consultation process launched by the commission in its 1997 green paper on innovation in europe. we need a community patent to stimulate innovation, which is a determining factor for growth, competitiveness and job creation in europe. our industry, our researchers and our scientists have been insisting for some time on the need for a patent that is affordable, valid throughout the community and guarantees optimum legal security. that's an ambitious goal. the commission proposal achieves this by proposing a patent which exactly meets these criteria. the community patent will coexist with the existing systems it will complement, as it will offer a more attractive alternative to enterprises, large and small, active in the internal market. the proposal is largely based on the existing european patent system which determines the rules and procedures for granting european patents. this implies the accession of the community to the european patent convention. under the regulation on the establishment of a community patent, patents granted by the european patent office may acquire the status of community patents. the patent as proposed by the commission will have the following features: it will be unitary in nature, will be valid throughout the community and will be subject to a single set of rules. this will reduce the uncertainty associated with the existence of 15 different legislations and, naturally, after enlargement, many more. legal certainty will be considerably enhanced by the creation of a centralised judicial system which will ensure the quality and consistency of the case law on community patents. the creation of such a judicial system requires an adaptation of the ec treaty. the current intergovernmental conference gives us the opportunity to do so. we must not miss this opportunity and i would like to count on the strong support of the members of the european parliament to ensure that the igc takes this matter seriously. finally, our proposal will reduce patent fees in europe considerably, as it avoids additional translation costs by limiting the number of languages to the three languages of the european patent office. let me stress the need for an ambitious approach. previous attempts to create a community patent, and more particularly the 1989 luxembourg convention, have failed for lack of ambition, particularly in two key areas: fees and litigation. we must convince the member states of the need to change the treaty in order to create a centralised court for disputes concerning community patents. the commission's proposal also requires that the consequences of enlargement on these costs and litigation be anticipated. unless we are very ambitious, our industry, our researchers and our experts will simply not have the modern patent they need.

the commission is extremely concerned about the recent accidents in fireworks production and storage facilities. the manufacture and storage of pyrotechnic substances are covered by council directive 96/82 of 9 december 1996 on the control of major-accident hazards involving dangerous substances, better known as the seveso ii directive. this directive lays down preventive obligations for the persons responsible for establishments where dangerous substances are present in certain quantities. it also requires them to establish safety management systems and contingency plans and to be able to demonstrate to the competent authorities that they have taken the necessary measures by submitting a safety report. in addition, the seveso ii directive contains a new provision which recognises that the objectives of preventing major accidents must be taken into account in member states' land use or land use policies. they are obliged to pursue the objective set out in the directive, namely the prevention of major accidents and the limitation of their consequences for man and the environment, in particular by controlling the establishment of new establishments, the alterations to existing establishments and new developments (communication routes, living areas, etc.) in the vicinity of existing establishments. in the long term, land use policies must ensure that the minimum necessary distances between hazardous sites and residential areas are respected. member states should also ensure that all competent authorities and planning authorities responsible for decision-making establish adequate consultation procedures. the addition of this provision can be considered a major step forward in the prevention of major accidents. a revision of the seveso ii directive is already under way. after a full investigation of the accidents that have occurred, the commission will integrate into the review process an assessment of the limits assigned to pyrotechnic substances. a proposal to amend the seveso ii directive should be ready by the beginning of next year, i.e. 2001. this amendment can only be made after an evaluation of the experience gained from the enschede accident and the one in romania. this procedure will be carried out in close cooperation with the member states, the european parliament and other interested parties. the transport of explosive materials is covered by directive 94/55 on the transport of dangerous goods by road, which makes the provisions of annexes a and b to the european agreement concerning the international carriage of dangerous goods by road within the same member state or between several member states mandatory. annex a contains provisions on the packaging and labelling of dangerous goods and annex b contains provisions on construction equipment and the proper operation of the vehicle carrying the goods as well as the minimum professional training of drivers. compliance with this legislation ensures a high level of safety in the transport of dangerous goods, including explosives.

- mr president, i take up the protest of air traffic controllers against the european commission's proposal which, behind the pleasant slogan of a 'single european sky', will pave the way for the privatisation of air traffic control. the atkins report clears the way for private groups to take over air traffic control, which, with increased traffic, is likely to bring in money. the report mentions delays which are becoming more frequent. but how could subordinating air traffic control to the demands of private profit end the delays? it is precisely the pursuit of profits by airlines that leads them to make choices that cause these delays. it is in the interests of users and their safety, as well as in the interests of workers in this sector, that air traffic control remains a public service, with the exclusive purpose of ensuring the smooth running of air traffic. competition, the pursuit of profit in such a sensitive area as air traffic control, will inevitably lead to disaster. if it is necessary to put an end to national particularities in air traffic management and if it is legitimate to unify european airspace, this must be done by rejecting any idea of privatization, competition or the search for profitability, and we will vote against this report.

- mr president, this text is important because the legislation in question has significant consequences for the welfare of women and also of children, that is to say, the future of our society. in this respect, we can be surprised that the commission has waited so long to present its evaluation report on the implementation of this directive and proposals to improve the conditions for the exercise of maternity leave. it seems to me that in this proposal for a revision of the directive, which we are asking the commission to submit quickly, it is essential to preserve the reality of three fundamental principles for women and their development: the prohibition of dismissal of pregnant women or women on maternity leave, the right to a minimum compulsory leave and the payment of this leave as part of pension rights. it seems to me that this new directive should also contain substantial improvements, including the possibility for any woman to take maternity leave of 20 weeks, without any obligation for her to take it in full, but with an obligation for the employer to offer it and with a minimum obligation of eight weeks after childbirth, in order to promote the development of the mother-child bond. as regards risk pregnancies and the arrival of handicapped children into care, it is obvious that appropriate proposals will have to be made, providing, taking account of the specificities, for an extension of the duration of maternity leave. as regards the definition of the benefit, it appears that the figure to be taken into account must be at least 80% of the previous salary, including in the establishment of pension rights. finally, it is desirable that this text should reinforce the formal prohibition of dismissal during pregnancy and maternity leave.
in writing. - the european parliament rightly decided at its meeting on 13 april 2000 to postpone the decision giving discharge to the european commission in respect of the implementation of the 1998 budget. this decision was legitimate, since the citizens of our nations have the right to demand an accounting of how the money of the european union, their money, is spent. our group is fully committed to all measures that can be taken to combat fraud and embezzlement. the irregularities found, both those mentioned in mrs stauner's report on the commission's questionable management and those highlighted in mrs rühle's report on the various european development funds, cannot be ignored and undermine the image and credibility of the community as a whole. so, ladies and gentlemen, we must draw all the consequences, in terms of punishing those responsible, but also of implementing much more transparent procedures. as the votes in the committee on budgetary control show, the reports by mrs rühle and mrs stauner seem to us to be in that direction. mrs rühle's report on the various edfs now clearly sets out the commission's responsibilities; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: the concern for a more moral approach to aid policy and the efficiency of its use is now a clearly stated principle, and our group welcomes this. there can be no question, however, of accepting that, under the pretext of better control, in order to achieve a more honest and rational use of european funds - and i am thinking in particular of the african, caribbean and pacific countries - our approach should be used as a pretext for organizing the unfounded trial of certain countries of the union - which is one of the main net contributors, i mean france - by means of a witch hunt, which would allegedly target certain senior officials of the same nationality. greater transparency is also our main concern with regard to the finances of the political groups in our assembly; the citizens of europe would not understand that we were making a different speech. we must therefore take note of the replies given by our institution to the court of auditors' observations and encourage any relevant reform without delay, in accordance with the financial regulation and the principle of transparency. in conclusion, i would say - and this is clear to us - that there should be no confusion between the discharge procedure, which is a global assessment of the management of the european commission, as provided for in the treaty, and the handling of a number of specific cases, which, of obvious gravity, are also of a specific nature and of a small amount, in relation to the total budget. you have to be smart . the fact that we took note of the additional clarifications we asked the commission to provide in the spring in connection with the stauner report does not mean that our group will then be struck with amnesia in the pursuit of unacceptable practices at the expense of our fellow citizens. our group welcomes the commendable efforts made by the rapporteurs stauner and rühle and mr kuhne; however, it is worthwhile to remain vigilant and to be able to observe, from experience, what the european commission will do, in view of the commitments it has made. our group therefore considers it necessary to abstain for the time being.
in writing. - it took the mad cow scandal to raise awareness of the need to improve the traceability and labelling of food products. europe has been very slow to react and has fallen far behind in the beef sector. today, on the basis of unanimous agreement in the council, we have the opportunity to finally show a little determination. the common position before us contains many of the amendments which parliament adopted at first reading. as regards compulsory labelling, indication of origin, dates of application, minced meat and the optional system, i think parliament can be satisfied: the council has heard us. that is why i have strongly supported this common position as it stands and have not voted for any amendments. the debate focused on a few specific points, including the indication of the category of the animal on the label. some colleagues have explained to us in good faith that this does not help to improve the traceability of beef. they're right. but after the succession of food scandals, which our parliament has always vigorously denounced, how can we today fail to take account of the immense role played by the consumer? the express mention of the category is a response to a request. it helps to restore consumer confidence. two types of information should be distinguished: information which improves traceability but is not directly intended to inform the final consumer. it is too specific, and can only be formally read by professionals. it has a sanitary function. it is on the basis of these statements that checks can be carried out. we are talking about the introduction of the identification and traceability system; the second type of information is intended directly for the citizen, like you and me, who buys his meat every day. what does he want to know ? he wants to be sure that the product he is going to eat is healthy: the traceability and identification system will guarantee the safety and quality of beef. but the citizen also wants to know what kind of meat it is. this type of labelling addresses the final consumer directly and provides him with intelligible information. it is a mistake to say that it is useless. on the contrary, labelling is as important as the introduction of health guarantees. europe must restore confidence to its consumers, who have been shunning beef since the mad cow scandal. the consequences are significant for the whole of the agri-food sector, which has been hit hard by this crisis. these two types of information are not competing with each other, they are complementary and each contributes to the restoration of european consumer confidence. our consumers' trust is not decreed, it is earned.

in writing. - a surprising expression came from the lips of the last president of the council when he presented to us on monday evening the balance sheet of the portuguese presidency. "we must not allow an intergovernmental drift to take hold", said prime minister antonio guterres. the debate on a federal europe, which has just been revived, must be conducted in its entirety.' is it not paradoxical to see the representative of the governments of the member states denouncing the risk of an 'intergovernmental drift' of the european union? the paradox is all the more striking because what is now apparent to almost everyone is the impasse to which federal formulas, and in particular the latest one, that of enhanced cooperation, inevitably lead. in an attempt to resolve the insurmountable contradiction between federalism and enlargement, the miracle formula of enhanced cooperation was particularly emphasised throughout the portuguese presidency. it was presented here on tuesday by president chirac as a kind of universal solution, with a "vanguard" of "pioneer countries" charting the way for all. in the context of european federalism, the avant-garde has reappeared in terms which were once very successful in other ideological contexts. the lyrical and ideological promotion of such a formula conceals the real dangers of the generalization of the principle of qualified majority voting and thus the elimination of the rule of unanimity. not only are enhanced cooperation agreements vigorously and rightly denounced by the small and mediumsized member states as an attack on their dignity, but sovereignty is a principle guaranteeing equality and respect for everyone. but even within enhanced cooperation, it is clear that the application of the majority principle, rather than unanimity, risks creating unsustainable tensions, by conferring a de facto monopoly on decisions to a single dominant country. so it is clear that the principle of qualified majority, if it is not applicable to 35, is equally applicable to 2 or 3. the 'miracle solution' is in fact a double source of tension, which could have a profound effect on european cooperation. that is why, instead of enhanced cooperation, which would necessarily be a source of dangerous tensions, we propose differentiated cooperation, concluded between sovereign states, free to decide to conclude whatever agreements they want in whatever fields they wish, provided that they do not harm the fundamental interests of their partners.
