in writing. - first of all, on such a serious and decisive subject, i would like to pay tribute to our rapporteur and to the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism for the diligence and the outstanding work they have done. not only has our parliament accelerated the legislative procedure, as one might expect, but it has also managed to stay ahead of the curve in terms of security by passing principles that it has long recognised. the commission has already proposed three measures to strengthen the system proposed by mr watts: not only should ships which have been stopped more than twice in the last 24 months in a community port be banned from sailing, but parliament believes that this should apply regardless of the age of the ship. - vessels which have been flying the flag of a country on the blacklist for three consecutive years will be prohibited from sailing in community waters. this is to deter the states issuing flags of convenience and the shipowners who irresponsibly resort to this illegal practice. - the installation of a 'black box' on board vessels, with no vessel without a 'black box' being allowed to enter community ports in future. the public is waiting for us and is eager to see our vote. we have not accelerated the procedure to delay it to the end by a conciliation with the council which would take several months! the risks of accidents and pollution are too great, not to mention the working conditions and salary of the sailors! let us be bold and vote on this progress report. this will be to our credit, will preserve our environment and therefore give us a better quality of life.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr watts' report which aims to improve the quality and frequency of inspections in the ports of the member states of the european union. the european commission proposes to introduce a certain uniformity in inspection procedures and specifies the conditions for refusing a ship access to ports in the member states of the union: these are the minimum bases for a common maritime safety policy. these provisions are intended to strengthen the control of the safety of ships in our ports, but they do not make it possible to prohibit the navigation in our territorial waters of dangerous ships which would not call at one of our ports: the limits of these proposals are therefore obvious. it is regrettable that the commission proposal did not include the idea of creating a genuine european surveillance force, on the model of the us coastguards. we will simply have to set up a european system of surveillance and information exchange between the member states. the european parliament will thus have to ensure that the financial and human resources needed for the effective establishment of this rapid reaction and information exchange system are rapidly released by the member states. i would remind you that the european union has some 270 inspectors who are responsible for port control by the states. this is far below the number of inspectors needed to implement the measures we are proposing in ports. the rapporteur has put forward a number of proposals to make these inspections more binding and effective. i therefore fully support the ban on sailing for vessels which have been grounded twice in the last two years, regardless of the age of the vessel. i do not think that this is the best way of doing things, but i think it is the minimum and i hope that we can go further. we must ensure that the measures we are proposing today are applied by all the member states of the european union. the responsibility for implementing these measures thus lies with the member states. without additional inspectors, without additional financial means, the proposed controls in ports will remain a fiction. we therefore expect the member states to make a real commitment to maritime safety.
in writing. - clarifying the chain of responsibility, respecting the social standards of crews, restoring the polluter pays principle and innovating on equipment must be priorities. in this context, the widespread construction of double-hulled vessels, especially those intended for the transport of polluting and/or dangerous goods as soon as possible, is a useful measure. europe cannot be below the regulations of the united states which, thanks to the oil pollution act of 1990, aims to eliminate monocoques between 2000 and 2015. we must at least follow the united states in this direction and take steps to ensure that the fleet of garbage vessels is not diverted to third world countries. in addition, the replacement of the aging fleet is a means of reviving shipbuilding. the improvement of this double-hull system should already be considered. many technicians now point out the difficulties encountered in inspecting and maintaining the space between the two hulls. however, mr hatzidakis makes proposals which restrict those of the commission. as he explained very well, they tend to strengthen maritime safety while respecting the system of competition or, in other words, the search for the lowest cost. in short, what is proposed is to eliminate maritime insecurity without addressing its causes. this draft regulation is a step in the right direction, but all derogations or postponements of implementation must be rejected. we must stick to the commission's proposal.

of the french presidency of the european union. the erika disaster in december 1999 was the reason why the issue of maritime safety was brought up on the community's political agenda, and it was under pressure from the european parliament that the european commission proposed the texts we have voted on today, almost a year after that disastrous shipwreck. it took a second maritime disaster, the sinking of the ievoli sun in the english channel, to accelerate the examination of these texts at first reading. i voted in favour of mr hatzidakis' report and i would naturally like to congratulate the rapporteur on his persistence on such a sensitive subject. the compulsory double hull for oil tankers and the phasing out of older vessels are measures which are going in the right direction and are a concrete response to the legitimate concerns expressed by our citizens. it is regrettable, however, that the transitional period during which single-hull vessels will be able to sail is too long, even though the scale of the measure may explain a gradual pace of prohibition: the adjustments to the retirement schedule of the older vessels, possibly proposed by the council, will have to be the subject of our greatest vigilance. in all cases, the 2015 deadline must be respected. the unilateral decision by the united states to ban single-hull tankers from calling at american ports after 2015 poses a real threat to maritime traffic in eu waters, where these vessels may continue to operate. it is therefore crucial that the timetable for the withdrawal of these vessels from our seas be analogous to the american timetable. finally, it should not be forgotten that the requirement for double hulls for oil tankers can only be one element of a genuine european maritime safety policy. this is an important decision, but it is not enough. the promotion of stricter regulation at international level must remain a fundamental objective of our maritime safety policy.
in writing. - the maritime disasters follow each other and look alike; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the concept of 'customs' and to extend the scope of the term 'customs' to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the concept of 'customs'. in this context, european legislation is needed. this report, which aims to improve the control of ships and to establish harmonised inspection procedures and rules, should therefore be supported as a step forward. however, in our opinion the rapporteur is not going far enough. although it provides for the harmonisation of inspection criteria for all member states, nothing is envisaged for vessels inspected outside the european union and from third countries. what will prevent, for example, a maltese or cypriot ship in bad condition from sailing near our coasts? when will the european union finally take the decision to ban any vessel that does not comply with the rules it has established from entering its territorial waters? will europe, which is usually so quick to legislate on environmental matters, continue to ignore maritime safety for a long time to come, because huge financial interests are at stake and the interests of its members are divergent? when will the union unlock the human and financial resources needed to do the job, so that this text is not just a declaration of intent? we shall therefore vote in favour of this report, which is in the right direction, but we regret that it does not provide for: preventive and enforcement measures to combat intensive emissions of greenhouse gases, which are the main cause of marine pollution; dto take inventory of waste vessels; to prohibit any vessel of any age presenting a clear danger from entering its territorial waters. the revision of directive 94/57/ec is becoming urgent, especially as malta and cyprus, the world's fourth and sixth fleets respectively, are candidates for accession. this community action must be matched by a reactivation of the imo, which, with real police powers to enforce the ism code, would be an effective instrument, like europol. we hope that the council will take up its responsibilities swiftly. the quality of our environment is also a concern.
in writing. - the recent shipwrecks of the oil tanker erika and the chemical tanker ievoli sun have revealed the important role played by classification societies in maritime transport. and we can legitimately ask questions about the reliability and effectiveness of the checks they carry out. first, the recognition of classification societies is left to the member states without prior control or harmonisation at european level. in addition, the training of inspectors for these companies varies from one country to another. furthermore, no guarantee is given as to the independence of the classification societies from the flag and/or the customer. the rapporteur's proposals for harmonisation at european level can only be positive. the second is that the european union should have the means to enforce the standards on classification societies by a recognised and competent authority. additional financial and human resources will be required. classification societies will have to be monitored and, if necessary, sanctioned by suspension of their authorization. in the event of an accident, the financial responsibility of the accredited bodies must be recognised and harmonised. the amount of the compensation will also have to be increased to take account of the material, economic, social and environmental damage. i will support this report, the commission's amendments, but i would ask members to support the amendments of the committee on the environment, in particular those aimed at harmonising the rules for classification societies and the statutes of inspectors.
in writing. - the report by mr ortuondo larrea is the last part of the package of measures to promote maritime safety. this is an important part of the programme as it concerns ship classification societies. i voted in favour of this report which proposes to introduce a certain uniformity between the member states in terms of the quality and expertise of classification societies, whose aggregation will henceforth be the shared responsibility of the member states and the european commission. the proposals also strengthen the responsibility of classification societies by providing for financial penalties, suspension or withdrawal of their registration for any accidents which may be attributable to them. the challenge to classification societies, following the sinking of the erika in december 1999, reminds us of their key role in assessing and preventing risks related to the state of ships. the seaworthiness of a ship is the responsibility of the state whose flag it flies. i hope that the involvement of the european commission in the aggregation of classification societies and the increased accountability of the latter will make it possible to overcome complacency. in this context, it will be necessary to ensure that these measures are applied without delay in the applicant states, whose fleets will have to comply with the safety standards and criteria of the european union. the problem of classification societies goes far beyond the borders of the european union: the european commission must therefore be able to monitor the application of the new measures by the member states, but also by the candidate countries. finally, our common policy on maritime safety must be an international reference and the obligations we require for our ships must be extended to the fleets of third countries. maritime safety must not simply be a matter of urgency after each new disaster that strikes our coasts, but the subject of an integrated and consistent policy at international level.
- madam president, the europe of nations group did not approve the european parliament's resolution on the preparations for the nice european council, because it is entirely inspired by the desire to strengthen supranational institutions applying uniform rules to all members. we reject calls for a european constitution, at least if it means subordinating national constitutions. we reject the idea of a binding charter incorporated in the treaties, because it would be a formidable uniformity machine. we reject the general extension of qualified majority voting accompanied by the parallel extension of codecision and the abolition of the luxembourg compromise. if the nice council fails to reach agreement on this basis, we do not consider it a failure, as the federalists claimed yesterday, when they attacked the french presidency and minister védrine. it would be a great success, because the europe we need on the eve of enlargement is not a rigid, hierarchical, distant, supranational europe, but a flexible europe close to the people, based on respect for national democracies. as regards the current agenda for nice, we believe that the charter should remain a simple declaration, that the commission should be composed of one commissioner per member state, that the weighting of votes in the council should respect the parity of the large states, that majority voting should not be extended to the most important subjects, such as immigration, international negotiations on services, taxation, social security, and finally that specific cooperation should be accepted very liberally, even outside the single institutional framework. more generally, we believe that after nice, another negotiation will have to be opened, but this time in the right direction, to make the institutions more flexible and to re-establish the control of the peoples by making europe not a superstate but a network of national democracies.
- madam president, whether the european institutions are changed at the european council in nice or whether the rivalries between national ruling circles make any institutional reform impossible, the european union will remain exclusively concerned with the interests of the economically dominant class, the large industrial and financial groups, their businesses and their profits. despite some pompous and empty phrases about democracy or the interests of the people, the debate taking place within these institutions has nothing to do with the interests of the working classes and the majority of the population. we will certainly not take sides in the squabble between the spokesmen of three or four great powers vying for dominance of the european union. we are equally unconcerned about whether the charter of fundamental rights will be annexed to the european treaty or dissociated from it, because in any case this charter, which is supposedly a charter of fundamental rights, not only refuses to include the basic rights of workers, but opens the door to measures of social regression. instead of pulling human and social rights upwards, the charter will facilitate operations designed to pull them downwards. we therefore abstained on the details but voted against the whole.
in writing. - on the eve of the nice summit and without prejudging its outcome, i would like to commend the hard work of the french presidency and most of the ministers who spared neither their time nor their effort to come and meet our parliament regularly in committees and in plenary. if, like many others, i sometimes regretted that the prime minister, lionel jospin, had spoken little during this semester "because of cohabitation", i know the strong impulses he has constantly given to his ministers and i want to say it. i would like to thank in particular hubert védrine and pierre moscovici, and martine aubry, who has created the social calendar - one of the highlights of this presidency. the only thing left now is to make a success of the nice summit and, in the field of institutional reform, to convince everyone to make the last concessions necessary to enable a 'good agreement' and a good treaty. it is also necessary, of course, to succeed in referring to the 'charter of fundamental rights' in the treaty itself to give it greater legal force. the importance of the social agenda must be clearly stated in order to ensure its rapid implementation. finally, a framework directive on public services, whose urgency is no longer in doubt, must be put on the rails. i personally have high hopes. and it is this hope that i wanted to express by voting a resolution, even though i do not agree with all the words.
in writing. - the french presidency had announced the birth of political europe. the nice summit will only strengthen the europe of defence and the trade union. the eu, in the framework of nato, will help to impose a new world order that is not very sympathetic to the plight of the palestinians, and is about to endorse, in effect, the liberalisation of rail transport and post offices. the accession of new countries is a pretext for intensifying the process of european construction, which only satisfies industrial groups. the advocates of liberal europe are not only adding to the misery of people already crushed by poverty, but they are imposing a political project on this occasion: to formalize a cluster of rich countries that controls a large european market. in this way, the eu is taking the lead on the new liberal demands of the wto and capitalist globalisation. by amending article 133 of the treaty of amsterdam, europe would extend the qualified majority voting currently in force in the council for trade in goods to other areas such as public services, intellectual property, health or education. finally, the adoption of a social agenda is a deception. the charter of fundamental rights will not be a new label with no future but a liberal banner that is likely to float over europe. we will take part in the alternative social summit with all those who refuse to accept the world as a commodity.
in writing. - i did not hesitate to vote against the joint resolution on the nice european council. the voters i represent here do not share any of these views. this text takes the future (and increasingly distant) enlargement as a pretext for calling for the strengthening of an already exhausted system. as if that were the only way ! as if there were no other possible form of organisation for our continent than the integrationist model, which was originally conceived, it should be recalled, for a hard core of five or six countries. why try to square the circle of enlargement and the representation of states and peoples in an already saturated system when another model, the europe of the nations, would provide simple and effective solutions? why should we also deny that the democratic alibi of this integrated europe is nothing but a false nose? the enlarged europe of integration is not democratic in nature: it violates one of the first human rights, the right to a nation. it is important to remember that democracy is not just about voting. it implies dialogue and dialogue implies a shared sense of community which is often linked to language. our debates in this chamber are more like successive monologues than real exchanges. let us compare them with the liveliness, energy and relevance of the debates in national parliaments: the members of the bourbon, westminster and cortes palaces can compare their ideas because they are expressed in the same cultural context, in the same languages. i also voted against a text which calls for the charter of fundamental rights to be incorporated into the future treaty to be adopted in nice. it is an ambiguous, contradictory text which opens the way to all interpretations. it cannot be claimed, as some do, that this text is harmless. in the hands of the luxembourg court of justice, 'a court with a mission', as one of its judges put it a few years ago, the charter can become the most undemocratic instrument ever created by the construction of europe. the convention which was commissioned to draft it is a foreshadowing of this: the enshrinement of the predominant role of influential groups and activist groups in the construction of the federal europe in gestation. a body which, by its very nature, can only reach a minimal consensus on rights which the peoples of europe already enjoy. finally, a body which has produced a text which will inevitably create a conflict of case law between the court of justice of the european communities and the court of human rights in strasbourg.
- madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we disapproved of the brok report and the lalumière report, not only because of their contents but also because of their subject, namely the common foreign and security policy, which we always thought was a chimera, and which has been adopted by the maastricht treaty eight years ago. for the sake of anecdote and irony, i will remind you of article j2, paragraph 3 of title 5 of maastricht: 'states shall ensure that their national policies are in conformity with the common positions'. this article has not been respected once, nor have the other articles of title 5. on the contrary, it was constantly flouted, the latest example being the recognition of north korea by london, leading the president-in-office of the union to deplore this failure, which he described as exceptional - i quote - before, three days later, berlin followed suit in london, without even having taken the trouble, it seems, to inform the french presidency. we are totally in the dark here, and this is just another disappointment for this poor european construction, or european destruction, if that is the right word to use. i am thinking, for example, of the reform of the institutions, promised for 1995, then 1997 and which still seems to be broken, in the end, a few days before the nice summit, which will only be a further disappointment, adding to our vagaries on enlargement, also promised for ten years, not to mention the successive, and indeed cumulative, failures of the euro. but these are just examples. i could speak of the reduction in appropriations for the meda programme or the edf. the only thing to be taken from these reports, and if only that, we should oppose it, is the mention, which is almost a ritual invocation to nato, since basically the only thing that mr brok manages to put in the 1999 balance sheet is the kosovo issue. it must be said that this time the europeans have found an arbiter, that is to say washington, and that thanks to the efforts of american generals, europe has finally found unity. i repeat: all this is ridiculous and when historians write the history of europe in the 20th century, i think they will mention neither the cfsp nor the ndc, and perhaps it is better that way.
in writing. - the delegation from the other europe group of the union for a europe of nations voted resolutely against the report of the committee on foreign affairs, which mr brok had defended. as in every year, this ritual report from the european parliament, which is in principle devoted to the annual balance sheet of the cfsp, in fact follows the well-known method of progressive changes which consists in continually seeking to widen the federalist gap in a given area, in defiance of the treaties and the decisions of the european councils. in this case, it is the helsinki process and the common foreign policy, in which the rapporteur sets three main objectives. three objectives which we can only reject: reducing european action in the world to that of the union as a single actor, creating a genuine european foreign ministry, to take over the functions of national ministries, and finally abolishing the pillar structure of the european union by generalizing the community method, placing in particular the high representative under the responsibility of the commission. this action plan, which deals with structures, omits only one, albeit decisive, element, namely the definition and content of a european external policy. because far from the virtual visions that dominate this parliament, the diplomatic realities are very different and the cfsp hardly exists. the most striking proof of this has just been given, if need be, by the recognition of the republic of north korea by the united kingdom and germany, without waiting for a common position to be adopted. it is therefore clear that it is by seeking harmonisation, when it is desired, timely and effective, between decisions which remain fundamentally the prerogative of the national actor, that the weight of european diplomatic action can be strengthened, and not by means of totally ineffective structural constraints. that is why our group voted again against the absurd proposals to communitarianise national diplomatic services, which were contained in articles 74 and 75 of the resolution, to transform the union delegations into genuine european embassies, and to create a european diplomatic school. it is almost like a dream when we discover the proposal to put all the real diplomatic staff of the member states, estimated at 40 000 agents, at the service of a virtual foreign policy: a proposal that is both precise and surreal!
in writing. - we voted against the report. under the guise of establishing and developing a so-called european security and defence policy, he bluntly exposes the need for a military policy in the service of what he calls 'the foreign policy objectives of the european union'. that is to say, the interests of the imperialist powers and the big capitalist groups which dominate europe and which dictate the orientations of the union. we are all the more opposed to this imperialist military policy because there is a declared consensus in this house on the subject, and the vast majority of groups, from the extreme right to the greens and the pse, have shown their acceptance and support for this policy. because this policy is, of course, directed against the people. against those who - as recently in the balkans - would suffer from the imperialist military interventions of the union and its allies. but also against the peoples of the european union, who will in any case have to finance the new arms expenditure advocated in the report and who will not even have the guarantee that these military forces will not one day be used against them in the name of 'maintaining order'.
in writing. - by deciding to create the nucleus of a european army, the nice summit will affirm the creation of a europe-power which will 'defend its interests everywhere in the world'. it thus shows its imperialist character, i.e. the protection of its investments abroad, the penetration of its goods, access to raw materials and the exploitation of cheap labour. it will act in concert with the united states within the framework of nato. but this european army will be used primarily to stabilise the eu's immediate periphery. the commercial annexation of east and north africa can only exacerbate social inequalities, generating social explosions, local military conflicts and mass displacements of populations. in the future, by coordinating its diplomatic and military forces, the eu will try to maximise what its member states have done individually over the past century, all in the name of 'peacekeeping' and 'humanitarian operations'. we do not need a euro-militarism. we are radically opposed to this european army, just as we are against nato and our own national army. the creation of a european military industry capable of taking on the united states (eads, dassault, bae) would have the first consequence of a drastic increase in the military budget and a transfer of scientific and technological research to the military sector. workers have nothing to gain and everything to lose from this "new" imperial aim of the eu.
in writing. - the only positive aspects of this report are that it calls for a 'european definition of domestic work' and a 'clear limitation of a maximum number of hours worked'. but under the pretext of looking after domestic workers, the report is concerned mainly with the interests of those who employ them. this would not be shocking if it were only a minority of employers, namely 'older people living alone who need help at home'. but the needs of this category are only mentioned to pass on the demand for 'tax deductibility of domestic services' and 'adaptation of prices and costs to the financial possibilities of individuals'. this clause, if passed, will allow especially wealthy families to subsidize their household expenses with money taken from the community. the second element of cynicism is that the explanatory statement makes domestic workers responsible for the fact that their employers employ them illegally. so, if we do not vote against this report because of the few basic rights it advocates, we do not vote for it either.
in writing. - in march 1999, following various scandals and patent malfunctions, the european commission resigned. this resignation, the culmination of a long period of decay, should not, however, make us forget that the 'delors commission' bore heavier responsibilities than its successor. this resignation, imposed by the elected representatives of the nations of europe, revealed the urgent need for a thorough reform of the working methods within the various directorates-general of the commission, of the decision-making procedures and of the structures, in order to achieve a better use of the resources available in the management of community resources and policies. the union for a europe of nations group, while acknowledging the serious shortcomings of the past, will not make a priori judgments about the commission and its reform, but it is clear that the exercise it is undertaking must first and foremost seek to restore the public's - widely and legitimately initiated - confidence in the european institutions, and this, as the report says, "through significant improvements in performance and efficiency"... but also more transparent practices. the reform of the commission will be judged on its merits, hence the need for regular follow-up reports to be presented by the european commission throughout the programme and the importance of the full report expected by december 2002. as regards the bea, the budget drawn up on the basis of its activities implies an amendment to the financial regulation, article 19 of which provides for a distinction between administrative appropriations - part a - and operational appropriations - part b - and the commission will therefore have to take great care not to infringe parliament's powers of allocation of resources. the french delegation will naturally oppose the introduction of the codecision procedure for any amendment to the financial regulation. by imposing the dismantling of the bat, in order to strengthen the commission's responsibility for the implementation of the programmes, our assembly wanted to tell the commission that 'only tasks which do not involve public intervention could be subcontracted to the private sector, and this in the form of one-off contracts'. as regards comitology, the union for a europe of nations group denounces the federalist view of the report which claims that the member states, through management and regulatory committees, encroach on the commission's management autonomy and reproaches them 'through these committees, for expressing national interests which are sometimes in conflict with those of the community'. the rapporteur even believes that 'the reform of the commission must be an opportunity to limit their intervention to areas which do not involve expenditure'. the management of community policies must be the expression of the pragmatic agreements reached between the countries of the union and, for our part, we believe quite the contrary, especially in view of the general bureaucratic opacity that prevails and the scandals and dysfunctions of a still recent past, that the member states must be more present than ever in the decision-making processes. the rapporteur's desire to eliminate their influence is encouraging in this respect! the commission's proposals, in the context of its reform, also raise a number of human resources issues. i will mention only one, the early retirement measure which is expected to affect some 600 civil servants, or less than 3% of the total workforce. the commission services tell us that this decision should have a neutral budgetary impact... our group would like that, but this is not a sufficient condition and it will be necessary to ensure in particular that the statutory provisions are respected and that these measures do not obscure the other priorities of the reform and do not give rise to political settlements of accounts. it is also well known that certain nationalities are clearly overrepresented in the lower grades of categories c and d, on the unacknowledged budgetary grounds that the staff concerned would not benefit from the 16% relocation bonus! such discriminatory practices are not acceptable. unemployment exists in all our countries and the commission would do well to take advantage of the future procedures for early retirement and the recruitment of several hundred new civil servants to start putting things in order. similarly, nepotism and opacity must disappear within the commission's services, particularly in recruitment for temporary posts. finally, the union for a europe of nations group strongly recalls that the citizens of the european union expect more than ever that reform measures and recruitment should reflect the diversity of opinions and convictions expressed in our countries.
in writing. - in the recent past, various scandals and malfunctions led to the resignation of the european commission in march 1999. this resignation revealed the need for a thorough reform of the structures, procedures and working methods of the commission's departments, in order to ensure maximum use of resources in the management of community policies. the proposals contained in the white paper, which are largely based on the second report of the committee of independent experts, should enable the commission to have the best possible organisational structure and operational methods in order to carry out its tasks under the treaty to the best of its ability, without, however, encouraging it to go beyond its prerogatives, which are also defined in the treaty, as has been the case too often in the past. there is also no doubt that, by virtue of the powers and competences conferred on it by the treaty, the european parliament must fully exercise its role of control over the commission, in particular in terms of transparency and the implementation of the budget of the european union. the citizens of our 15 nations, who elect their representatives, would not understand otherwise, for it is their money that is at stake. the effectiveness of the reform proposed in the white paper will obviously be judged by the results in terms of the use of human and financial resources, in particular by an effective monitoring method, by control mechanisms and by appropriate sanctions. the union for europe of nations group, with regard to the rules of conduct in public life, welcomes the implementation of various codes of conduct concerning the commission - relations between commissioners and between the commission administration and the public - provided, of course, that these texts have a legal basis. the delays in payments alleged by the commission often appear unjustified; it is therefore important to remedy this as soon as possible by speeding up the transfer of sums due, as this situation ultimately harms the functioning of all the european institutions. community policies are expressed in moral and financial commitments to our citizens and to nationals of third countries. it is therefore necessary to ensure that these commitments are respected much more strictly than in the past. as regards human resources, the merit of staff and greater transparency in staff policy in general must become the main points of the new administrative reform. the union for a europe of nations group welcomes in principle the commission's response to the european parliament's call for a comprehensive reform of its human resources policy in the form of a white paper. the union for a europe of nations group, however, strongly emphasises that the reform of the commission must result in the diversity of opinions and convictions expressed in our countries regarding the idea that each person has of europe, its past and its future, being taken into account when recruiting staff. the citizens of our respective countries would not understand otherwise. similarly, opacity and complacency must be removed in recruitment, particularly in temporary posts. the union for a europe of nations group does not at this stage express any hostility in principle to the early retirement of several hundred officials from its services, provided, however, that the statutory provisions are respected, that the early retirement measures do not obscure the priorities of the reform, that these departures are reflected in budgetary neutrality, that they are carried out in the interests of the service and on a voluntary basis and without giving rise to political settlements of accounts. finally, i think it is essential to recall that in this reform, which is essential for the future, we expect both greater rigour and transparency from the commission in its day-to-day management, but also a greater sense of responsibility on its part, within the strict limits of the powers conferred on it.

- the next item is the recommendation for second reading (a5-0348/00) by mr maaten, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and consumer policy, on the common position adopted by the council with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco products (com (94) 0188 - c5-0431/2000 - 1999/0244 (cod))
- mr president, ladies and gentlemen, 80 deaths from the new variant of creutzfeldt-jakob disease in europe and europe, its council of ministers, the commission and parliament have decided to ban animal meal and the non-entry of bovines over 30 months of age into the food chain without prior testing. that's nice, but a little late. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. and when a directive comes to regulate the distribution and information about this drug - i am talking about tobacco - we hear the outcry of some colleagues. but, ladies and gentlemen, if you were really aware of the health problems associated with tobacco, you would demand that this drug be banned, just as you continue to maintain the ban on other substances which are much less lethal in terms of quantity. you are responsible for the health of millions of citizens, but also for the deaths of thousands of young people who are not sufficiently informed. yesterday, in the united states, lawsuits were won against the multinational tobacco companies for poisoning and lying about the non-toxicity of the products. today, in france, the loire-atlantique health insurance fund is getting the right to sue the tobacco industry. but tomorrow, as with the tainted blood or the mad cow disease, the lawsuits will be directed against those who knew and let it happen, that is, you, the decision makers, the legislators. so let's do something together, a small thing in view of the extent of what remains to be done: reduce the levels of nicotine and tar; banning addictive substances, such as ammonia, which is added to nicotine to create an increasing dependence on cigarettes; affix legible warnings covering at least 35% of the surface of the package to inform the public of the risks and dangers of tobacco; eliminate false labels such as light and ultra-light that lead young people, especially young women, to smoke in the belief that it is less harmful, whereas the medical community now agrees that the rise in small cell lung cancers, peripheral, more insidious, more difficult to detect and with even more tragic prognoses is linked to the overconsumption of this type of cigarettes; measure the socio-economic cost of tobacco and convert subsidies to tobacco producers into real conversion subsidies, for example for cereal areas to replace animal flour; accept that products intended for export must follow the same rules as those intended for the european internal market; the commission has also proposed that the price of tobacco be increased, since this is a measure which has a direct impact on consumption, especially among young people, and that tax rates be harmonized. this is not much, ladies and gentlemen, and will not really harm the interests of the tobacco industry, which some people seem more concerned with defending than the health of the population. much remains to be done: to extend this directive to products other than cigarettes such as cigars and roll-your-own tobacco which are no less harmful; the commission has also proposed that the ban on advertising these deadly products be confirmed and that the collective rules for non-smoking areas be extended. we still have a lot of work to do. the adoption of mr maaten's report is a first step which i would urge you to take with the health of future generations in mind.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are dealing here tonight with a subject which is not within our competence. i'm sure it's not the first time. nevertheless, the matter now seems much more serious than usual. so, once again, i'll be addressing substance and not form. the court of justice has just annulled the 1998 directive banning advertising and sponsorship for tobacco products. the court held that a total ban on tobacco advertising could not be justified in the name of the proper functioning of the internal market. but in defiance of the treaties, and believing that it has been entrusted with a mission of salvation, our parliament is moving forward with its head bowed, to pass, at any cost, the text we are discussing today. such an attitude is a perfect symbol of the shortcomings of our european institutions, which are ready to use any means to achieve the ideological goals they have set themselves. but we must remember that there are rules to be followed. history teaches us that it is dangerous to consider the goal to be achieved - no matter how noble and virtuous - as superior to the rules. such stubbornness is a gross lack of realism. instead of learning from the failure of 9 october in luxembourg, we are persisting in an attitude which is legally indefensible. our group, which is deeply committed to the preservation of public health, is concerned about the consequences of such a suicidal political attitude. we would like to kill the directive which we would not otherwise take. public health must not become the subject of a power struggle in order to win new powers at the expense of the states. health is too important a subject to be used as a political tool. so what are the solutions? there is only one solution, in our view: to learn from the court of justice's decision and to recognize that the european commission has gone far too far, unfortunately, in trying to violate the treaties. we must also revise our own copy and draft it in a way which respects the balance required by the treaty.
- doc. a5-0356/2000 by mrs honeyball, on behalf of the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism, on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on summertime arrangements (com (2000) 302 - c5-0322/2000 - 2000/0140 (cod)).
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for a directive on summertime arrangements which we are considering today is a good one. it is based on a large study carried out at the request of the commission. the results of this study are interesting in that they go against a number of commonly held ideas. first, most sectors of activity have now incorporated the principle of summertime. some socioeconomic sectors have also called for the switch to summertime to be made permanent, in particular the it, transport, telecommunications and tourism sectors. time is indeed a basic data element which these sectors must integrate into their products and services. to do this, they need to know in advance the arrangements for summer-time arrangements in all member states. secondly, a number of negative implications have not been clearly demonstrated. thus, any health problems experienced are short-lived and completely reversible. as regards the biorhythms of animals and the working conditions of agricultural workers, the survey results also do not indicate any negative effects. the study does, however, highlight other, less expected implications. summertime is thus in line with the changing lifestyles of our societies, due in particular to longer working hours, the reduction in the closing time of shops, services and public transport. the additional daylight hours brought about by the changeover to daylight saving time are particularly beneficial to the tourism and leisure sector, which is experiencing a resurgence in activity directly linked to the brighter and longer evenings. the summertime arrangements seem to go hand in hand with an improved quality of life, with the positive effects of the summertime period far outweighing the temporary disruptions associated with the change. the european parliament only makes one amendment to the commission's original proposal. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services. if these reports show that the provisions on summertime should be amended, the commission could make appropriate proposals. the first report shall be drawn up by 30 april 2007 at the latest. i do not think that this amendment is contrary to the objective of the commission's proposal. it will make it possible to monitor the implementation of the change of time without calling into question the principle of the change. in the end, we can only welcome this commission proposal, which makes the switch to summertime a permanent instrument of european policy by proposing, finally, to establish the provisions relating to the summertime period for an unlimited period.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as we approach the darkest time of the year, it is refreshing to talk about summer, or even summertime. however, i would like to draw attention to this elaborate and profound clock-setting ritual, the appropriateness of which may be disputed. i have received contacts from farmers who put the welfare of dairy cows, which is also important for milk production, first. the peace of mind of the herders is already being disturbed by mad cow disease. now, we should not add to their stress by deviating from their usual rhythm. cows don't change rhythm in a day or two. it is also difficult for agriculture, because in autumn, when the gardens are planted, the morning dew should have disappeared according to the clock, but, miraculously, nature does not follow the directive. an additional problem is that not only is the natural rhythm of the animals disturbed but also the light-dependent human circadian rhythm. i do not think that the commission's communication has provided any convincing evidence of the need for summertime. i therefore think that the continuation of the arrangement should be reviewed as soon as possible. it is also doubtful whether the summer season will end just before november. in the snow-white north of europe, the memory of summer will have cooled by then. the more reasonable time to decide on summer time should be at the end of september, approximately six months after it began. i am not totally opposed to summertime, because there are also positive aspects to it. i would nevertheless ask the commission to make a critical assessment of the need for summertime in the future. i do believe that we could do without daylight saving time, but i am not ready to give up warm summer weather. but fortunately, it's not up to the politicians.

- the next item is the recommendation for second reading (a5-0349/2000) by mr liese, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and consumer policy, on the common position adopted by the council with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to the application of good clinical practice in the conduct of clinical trials on medicinal products for human use (8878/1/2000 - c5-0424/2000 - 1997/0197 (cod)).
- madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the directive, which is before us today for the second time, is part of a delicate context of international competition in the field of pharmaceutical research, of major health issues, particularly in paediatric matters, and it solves the problem of clinical trials being held at the same time in several member states and at several sites. the common position which the council has transmitted to us certainly improves the commission's proposal and especially the first reading by parliament. there are a number of points on which we can agree. the principle for starting a clinical trial is the tacit approval of both the ethics committee and the competent authorities of the member states. the opinion of the ethics committee is thus decisive since it intervenes first and the absence of a negative opinion allows the trial to begin immediately without wasting time. finally, we agree with the council's proposals on the labelling of medicinal products used in this case. on the other hand, there are other points in the common position which need to be improved, and i understand and welcome the fact that the council is prepared to make a number of compromises. the first point seems to me to be essential and there can be no question of compromise on this point. the consent of the participants in a clinical trial must necessarily be in writing and if this is not possible, for example in the event of temporary inability to write, a witness must be present at the time of consent collection. secondly, this consent must be informed, which means, in particular, that the subject must have been informed of the conditions under which the trial is to be conducted, of the potential risks to the subject and of the possibility for the subject to withdraw from the trial at any time without any constraint. finally, and this seems to me to be a fundamental point, we must ensure that the best possible protection is afforded to those who are not in a position to give consent, that is to say the weakest, children and adults who are legally incapable. it is necessary that they expect a direct benefit from the clinical trial. the opinion of minors, in particular, must at least be heard because of the clinical and psychological characteristics which must be taken into account. it seems only fair to me not to include incapacitated adults in clinical trials that could be conducted on able-bodied adults. finally, adults with disabilities should only be involved in trials that focus on the disease they have and which causes their disability. so even if there are still some points of disagreement with the council, i would like to point out that the result we are seeking to achieve by adopting this directive is the result of a long and fruitful compromise work carried out by mr liese, our rapporteur, whom i thank and congratulate for his participatory and constructive approach, and by the council, which has declared itself cooperative and open to the amendments adopted by the committee on the environment at second reading. i therefore hope, after what mr liese has just said, that we will quickly reach an agreement which will avoid a long and ultimately unproductive conciliation.

in writing. - the group of the european people's party supported the report by mr liese. it was necessary to find a solution to the diversity of legal and administrative situations that apply to clinical trials in the member states. it is therefore desirable to promote the development of medicines in the community, as this can give patients a better chance of receiving effective treatment. it is also necessary to mobilise research and the health ministers of the various member states in favour of paediatric medicines. two thirds of the medicines for children are designed for adults. in the absence of data, the marketing authorisation (ma) does not cover use in children. thus, use in paediatrics may be the result of individual empirical prescriptions. it is therefore necessary to encourage pharmaceutical companies to develop products specifically designed for children and their conditions, so that doses and pharmaceutical forms are adapted to their organism. the report by dr liese enables us to achieve shorter deadlines, harmonised procedures and, above all, a high level of protection, especially for children. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is able to take part in the debate on the future of the european union. moreover, the legitimate desire to protect patients who submit to trials at union level is inseparable from respect for the principle of subsidiarity. consent must therefore be very strictly regulated. we believe that testing on people who are unable to give informed consent should be prohibited. in this respect, dr liese's desire to set stricter limits on the consent of incapable persons is interesting. we also believe that consent should be governed by national law. thus, while it is necessary to establish a framework of rules which cannot be avoided, states must retain the power to adopt more binding legislation, as france has done in this respect. this would be an intelligent application of the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. - should the summertime change introduced at the time of the oil shocks be continued, in order to save energy, and extended until 2001? first of all, the reason for this device has lost much of its interest and value: the energy savings it is supposed to allow are no longer established at all and are limited to the symbolic. on the other hand, in addition to the problems of air pollution, the profoundly disturbing nature for living beings, especially for children, of this double change of time, occurring in march and then in october, is well established and keenly felt by our populations, many of whom ask that this disruptive arrangement of the rhythms of life be reversed. the report commissioned by the commission to justify its proposal merely notes the lack of homogeneous data available and the contradictory nature of existing studies: it therefore provides no relevant basis which could justify the maintenance of the time change regime. the commission proposes to make the changeover to summertime and then to wintertime final, without any time limit. it intends to impose it without any possible derogation on the member states, as well as on the candidate states, without taking account of their geographical specificities. nothing, not even the hour, must escape his unifying will! it must be the same time in brest and brest-litovsk. the concept of time zones cannot be opposed to the benefits of standardization! long live the one federal hour ! however, the choice of the time in force in each member state is still a purely national decision, under the principle of subsidiarity. national governments must not renounce the exercise of this right, but must remain concerned with expressing the will of the people who elected them. the best solution would probably be, contrary to what the commission proposes, to abandon the system of changing time and to maintain gmt + 1 hour throughout the year, at least for france. in this context, i am pleased that two amendments have been adopted by parliament: one rejects the 'unlimited' duration which the commission wanted to give to the time change mechanism; the other allows member states and the european institutions to retain the possibility of reviewing the system.

- mr president, of the 15 countries of the european union, 11 recognize the right of succession, but only eight apply it, with varying degrees of success. austria, the netherlands, ireland and the united kingdom do not have it in their legislation and, outside the european union, neither switzerland nor the united states recognise the right of succession. the introduction of a right of succession system seems at first sight to be justified by a desire for fairness and assistance to artists. in fact, the right of succession does not go in the sense of aid to creation, on the contrary. it's a drag on the art market, which needs to be dynamic and evolve with minimal constraints. for a living artist, who sees his rating consolidate and his production, therefore, re-evaluate, what matters is the dynamics of the buyer and his sales potential. the right of succession generates a complicated jurisdiction, certainly onerous compared to the often modest sums, which in many cases will have difficulty in reaching the interested parties. it creates an additional administration, thus adding to the criticism often levelled at european standards. it undermines the work of galleries, whose efforts should be focused on supporting artists. it raises fears, extra costs and administrative hassles for potential buyers of goodwill and sometimes leads to absurd situations: the right is calculated on the resale price, in the event of a lower value, the mobility of the work is valued more than the creation. so should we extend this system to countries which do not want it - i am thinking in particular of the united kingdom, which is currently the european leader in the art market - at the risk of making them lose all competitiveness?

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are now back to the banana com. last april, after voting in favour of a very large majority of the amendments i proposed to the commission's text, but the commission refusing to accept any of them, we decided to refer this matter back to the committee on agriculture with a view to finding a possible compromise. this was the only way, in the absence of a codecision procedure, to ensure that the priorities were income and market access for community and acp producers. we have tried to reach a conciliation with the commission; it didn't really work out. but parliament must now decide. i would therefore remind you that in november 1999 the commission made yet another proposal to amend the banana cmo, mainly affecting its external component and with the aim of ensuring that the cmo is compatible with the rules of the world trade organisation. the commission proposed at that time that a non-discriminatory quota system be maintained with a slight tariff preference for acp countries and that tariff only be introduced in 2006. in april 2000, parliament adopted my first report and its amendments, which went against the commission's proposal. the report proposed, in particular, the rejection of automatic transition to tariff only, a tariff preference for acp countries of at least eur 300, an evaluation and a possible revision of the internal part of the cmu. the banana issue is far from anecdotal and there are significant issues at stake. since 1993, the situation of community producers has been steadily deteriorating. the same is true for many traditional acp suppliers. i would remind you that the main objective of this common organization of the market is to guarantee access to the community market for its products. it is already impossible for these producers to compete fairly with producers and operators in the sector at international level. it should be noted that 62% of imports today come from third countries, mainly ecuador, colombia, costa rica and honduras. it is not a question here of protecting a product of a certain origin in a protectionist way, but of defending the sustainability of a certain way of producing. the banana is being defended as a whole production chain, on which whole regions often depend for their vitality and social equilibrium. months passed until, last october, the commission published a communication on the application of the 'first come, first served' rule to manage the quota system. i would stress that this is a communication and not a legislative proposal. we therefore had to continue to work on the legislative proposal of november 1999. contacts were established with the commission and the last meeting confirmed that it maintained its position, namely the quota system, managed on a first-come-first-served basis and the switch to tariff only in 2006. my second report is therefore very similar to the first and takes up the amendments voted for by the plenary. but even in the absence of a legislative proposal, the 'first come, first served' rule also had to be decided. the codecision does not say that the system is fair, but it says that it is the only method compatible with the wto rules. however, the united states has already expressed its opposition to this system, as have the acp countries. the rest of our position remains the same: period of application of the system for at least ten years in order to guarantee legal certainty for producers and operators, review after these ten years, no automatic switch to tariff only, tariff preference of 300 euros for the acp. we have asked for guarantees in the event that the commission sets up a system of administering tariff quotas on a first come, first served basis, because it will have serious repercussions on acp producers, who are now unable to take their place in the boat race that is about to begin. it is therefore absolutely necessary to find a way of enabling them to have effective access to the c quota, in addition to the tariff preference of eur 300, and to assess in a systematic way the impact of the system on these producers. i am glad that we were able to achieve a unanimous vote in the committee on agriculture. i thank my colleagues and mr fernández martín, rapporteur for the committee on development and cooperation, for their support. in conclusion, i would like to express my regret that on such an issue the european union seems to be abandoning its values in favour of the rules of world trade. the economy is at the service of man, and in any system where man is predominant, the rules must be adapted to man's will and needs, never the other way around. the commission and the council will bear their own responsibility if they should judge otherwise.
mr president, this never-ending saga of the banana conflict between the union and the countries producing dollar bananas is not anecdotal but exemplary in more than one respect, because 20% of the bananas consumed in the union are produced in the outermost regions of the community and these regions need this production for their development. another 20% of these bananas are produced in acp countries which also need this production for their development and to which we have made commitments which we must respect. both sides were able to increase their production because we offered them a market which we must not take away from them today. we must continue to give these producers the means of living without complaint by buying their produce as a matter of priority. only then can we open our doors to outside producers on the basis of free trade for the remaining 60%. that is what the bmo in the banana sector was aiming at, and that is what our rapporteur mr dary's counter-proposal is aiming at. the fact that banana producers in the dollar zone are using the dogma of free trade, which they consider to be "intangible", to impose a tariff-only system on us should not impress or intimidate us. so let us be as firm in our position in favour of a culture as the americans are in their protectionist position in respect of sugar, tobacco, peanuts and dairy products. we must stand firm, because if we give in today on bananas, why should we not give in tomorrow on the other common market organizations, on the cap, on the european agricultural model which advocates sustainable development? we must hold on, or we will lose all control of our food chain. in the name of the same principles, we will be forced to accept gmos, hormone-treated meat or social dumping. we must stand firm and it is rather up to the wto to evolve and leave its concrete fortress of tariff only which looks too much like profit only. the banana issue is an important milestone on the road to this essential development, which, mr president, the european union should be working on with all its strength.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we are addressing the so-called precautionary principle, albeit late. i say "famous" because it is a very fashionable subject, and you will agree with me that there is not a day that goes by without the press being hyped about the precautionary principle, about everything and nothing, for better or for worse, but more often in the wrong way. the interest in the precautionary principle is not surprising and reflects legitimate concerns, as the public is highly sensitive to the recent food scandals and other cases involving contaminated blood. this interest also reveals the crisis of public confidence in science, which we know is not or is no longer infallible. finally, this interest in the precautionary principle reveals the crisis of confidence of the population in public decision-makers or policy-makers, who are suspected of complacency towards certain pressure groups, especially industrial ones, or more simply suspected of culpable frivolity. all this shows the importance of the political stakes involved in the question of the precautionary principle and in this respect i welcome the commission's initiative and the general quality of its communication on the precautionary principle. to explain the outcome i want our parliament to achieve, i would like to highlight briefly two key issues in this debate. the first issue in the report we are discussing is of a legal nature. although the media have only recently been reporting on this, the precautionary principle is not new to the international legal scene. it is referred to in many international treaties and agreements. the court of justice of the european communities and even the wto dispute settlement bodies consider that the precautionary principle can be applied in environmental or public health matters, and sometimes even against europeans, as the pending raw milk cheese case shows. but these references in international texts are not sufficient to clarify its nature or legal value, especially since these texts contain no definition of the precautionary principle. the consequence is that we are creating unacceptable legal uncertainty for our fellow citizens, but also for the industrialists who no longer know what sauce they are going to eat. the first challenge of the commission's communication and of the report of our parliament is therefore to specify the nature and the legal value of the precautionary principle which we wish to see recognized, to define the conditions under which the precautionary principle can and must be implemented, and finally to determine the criteria which must be met by the measures to be taken in application of the precautionary principle. the second issue in our work on the precautionary principle is of a more political nature. the union must promote a unified conception of the precautionary principle so that it can be present in all the policies implemented by the union within its competence, but also so that this european approach can be invoked against our partners who often have a less ambitious approach to the environment and health than we do. in this respect, it is important that our parliament expresses a very clear position so that the commission can be given a strong mandate to defend the union's positions in international bodies, and particularly in the wto. the text of the resolution, which we have reached after several debates in the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, is largely in line with the council resolution annexed to the conclusions of the nice summit, and we welcome it. the text of the committee on the environment is the result of the continuous search for a compromise or rather a balance between the maximalist and minimalist tendencies which have been expressed in our debates and which both lead to excesses. maximalists seek to block innovation and progress, while minimalists advise that the precautionary principle should be used only in the event of a significant danger to health and the environment, that is to say, above a threshold to be defined, but it is not clear how! in the face of these two approaches, i have tried to strike the right balance for a legally regulated use of this political tool. the european union has the ambition to guarantee its citizens a high level of protection of their health and the environment. i therefore call on you, ladies and gentlemen, to support this reasoned and reasonable conception of the precautionary principle and to reject all amendments which depart from it in one way or another.
- mr president, i am prepared to accept any and all, depending on the circumstances and interests of the moment, the precautionary principle may be the best or the worst of things. i admit that i do not understand the intrusion of animal welfare into this report. the application of this principle must avoid at all costs hindering innovation and economic activity, creating industrial frivolity and immobility, and becoming a means of diverting competition. this principle should only apply if there is a real danger. the commission's action must be exclusively political. the precautionary principle should therefore be defined precisely to avoid the usual interpretative lapses of the court of justice, it should be handled with care and prudence, the factors triggering its application should be clearly identified and it should be integrated into the wto negotiations. in view of the criteria adopted, proportionality, discrimination, consistency, examination of the benefits and costs, examination of the scientific evaluation, the precautionary principle must correspond to the right balance between the seriousness of the risk and the measures taken, unlike what the european union has done for mad cow disease. in the same way, in the name of transparency, let us ensure the rights of expression and defence of producers, artisans or industrialists, by indicating in the evaluation reports their opinions and comments in the same way as those of scientists whose conclusions have been rejected. finally, the authenticity of local products must not be sacrificed to safety at any cost. if calibrated products allow for better food safety, diversity calls for hazards in qualitative terms and therefore a certain risk taking. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the quality of the products is not affected by the quality of the products.

both candidate countries, and thus send a strong message to the latter that it is ready to welcome them in the short term. we warmly welcome this important decision. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the heads of state or government have made short-sighted bargains without a grand vision for the future of europe. they have closed down the community machinery in order to extend its life in view of enlargement. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the council has concluded the fifth day of negotiations in the early hours of the morning, amid general exhaustion and uncertainty as to the precise outline of many decisions. the delay in publishing the written conclusions, which are still not available four days after the council meeting, clearly shows the difficulty of clearly drafting decisions taken in the midst of confusion. once again, last night, hastily and improvised, far-reaching provisions were adopted which had not been discussed before, such as the appointment of the president and the members of the commission by qualified majority, a matter which was not even indicatively included in the summary document forwarded by the presidency to the council. we confirm that this method of decision-making is totally unnatural for democratic countries. but the solution is certainly not what the federalists propose, namely to prepare intergovernmental conferences with assemblies like the one which drew up the charter of fundamental rights, because it will only further strengthen confusion, over-subsidiarity and unrealism. on the contrary, intergovernmental conferences should in future be organised on a more stable basis, with an agenda consisting of proposals adopted by a limited number (for example, one third) of national parliaments. it's the only way to reframe the conversation. in the background, we can see, in the quilt of compromises, two overlapping trends: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right of initiative in the matter of the internal market. as regards the first point, we note in particular the extension, either immediately or in the short term, of qualified majority voting on matters of major importance, such as asylum and immigration policy, international agreements in the field of services and intellectual property, or even the appointment of commissioners. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a step in the right direction. for example, with regard to the trade negotiations mentioned above, national parliaments will lose the last of their sanctioning powers, while a country, if it is in a minority in the council, will not be able to say 'no' if the negotiation is detrimental to its interests. at the same time, the apparent maintenance of the parity of votes of france and germany in the council should not create any illusions: the new rule of the 'democratic net' (the creation of a minority of the negative vote representing 38% of the population) will automatically favour germany, which alone will have almost half of this minority after enlargement to 27 states. it will therefore be easier for it than for others to reach the negative threshold by adding some smaller countries to its zone of influence. at the same time, the gap between the number of german meps and those of other countries, including france, is widening further, which will have consequences in the context of the european parliament's extended decision-making powers. this may seem fair to some, since it tends to reflect the relative weight of countries in terms of population in the institutions. but this way of calculating is based on the implicit assumption that there is a single european people, which is not true. the only way to avoid dangerous conflicts in the future is to preserve the traditional view that europe is based on mutual respect between national communities. for example, the new method of selecting the president of the commission by a qualified majority in the council and a majority in the european parliament leads directly to the installation of the holders of the post who might not be supported by all countries, but would almost necessarily have to be supported by germany. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the new system of electing the president of the commission is in line with the constitution. can this new europe last? the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in practice, however, its predecessors had the foresight, by relaxing closer cooperation, to introduce a new dose of flexibility which, by separating different levels of integration, will facilitate the approach to enlargement. but in the long run, that's not enough. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we therefore call on the french parliament to prevent a serious crisis in europe in the future by refusing to ratify the treaty of nice.
